articles.title: Army vs Air Force: Rally Takes the Lead, Falcons Answer, 21-24
articles.matchup: Final: Air Force Falcons (7-2) 24, Army Black Knights (5-4) 21, Sat., Nov. 7, Michie Stadium, West Point. Next: vs East Carolina, Sat., Nov. 21, 12:00 PM ET, Michie Stadium, West Point
articles.text:
Army Black Knights 21, Air Force Falcons 24. A 24-21 loss at Michie Stadium, and I'll file this debrief the way I was trained: honest, complete and with no excuses. Five and four. Four and two in the American. The Commander-in-Chief's Trophy goes to Colorado this year.

It was a Blackout night at West Point, and the logistics were flawless. The cadets marched in review on the Plain at 4 PM, Thomas Rhett played USAA's Military Appreciation Concert on Howze Field before kickoff, and 33,575 of us in black filled Michie. Right item, right place, right time.

The first half was a supply shortage. Air Force led 10-0 before Godspower Nwawuihe broke a 21-yard touchdown run, but the Falcons scored with seven seconds left in the half and led 17-7 at the break.

Then the second-half resupply arrived on schedule. Cale Hellums finished one drive from 1. Bryson Luter took the next one 19 yards to put us in front 21-17. Two straight scoring drives, done by the book. Nwawuihe finished with 82 yards on 18 carries, Luter 81 on nine, and our offense went three for four on fourth down.

On the first play of the fourth quarter, Air Force hit a 24-yard touchdown to a tight end in the middle of the field, and that was the score that held. Our defense answered with a fourth-down stand at our own end zone after an interception. Caleb Williams and Kai Woolfolk each made eight tackles. But we went three-and-out on the next series, punted with 5:18 left, and never saw the ball again.

Status of the trophy: gone for now. Status of these cadets: still young leaders I'm proud of. We have a week to regroup, then East Carolina comes to Michie Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 21, at noon ET. Beat Navy can wait. Go Army.

The Black Knights rallied from 17-7 down with third-quarter touchdowns by Cale Hellums and Bryson Luter to lead 21-17 before a fourth-quarter Air Force score.
Air Force needed a 6-foot-6 tight end and the last five minutes to get out of West Point.

articles.title: Air Force vs Army: Kibbee's Strike Brings the Trophy Home, 24-21
articles.matchup: Final: Air Force Falcons (7-2) 24, Army Black Knights (5-4) 21, Sat., Nov. 7, Michie Stadium, West Point. Next: vs San Jose State, Sat., Nov. 14, 7:00 PM ET, Falcon Stadium, USAF Academy
articles.text:
Air Force Falcons 24, Army Black Knights 21. Red Pen, hold the presses: we won 24-21 at Michie Stadium, and the Commander-in-Chief's Trophy is coming home to Colorado for the first time since 2022. Seven and two. Mission accomplished, and I am doing a full victory roll in this press box.

Back home that same morning, the In Their Honor Veterans Day Parade went down Tejon Street in downtown Colorado Springs, led by Wanda Daniels, who helped build P-61 night fighters during World War II, with the Pikes Peak Honor Bell making its parade debut. A real aircraft builder leading the formation. Then our Falcons flew east and finished the job.

Pre-flight review of the first half: Carter Cremascoli kicked a 21-yard field goal, Kemper Hodges scored from 3, and Evan Medders ran one in from 4 with seven seconds left in the half. Seventeen to seven at the break. Hodges, whom I am now calling Afterburner, finished with 119 yards on 17 carries.

Army came out of the hangar hot. Two straight scoring drives in the third quarter and a 21-17 Black Knights lead. Turbulence. And then, on the first play of the fourth quarter, Medders looked up on just his sixth throw of the night and found Simon Kibbee, our 6-foot-6 tight end, alone in the middle of the field. Twenty-four yards, touchdown, and a lead we never gave back. Medders went 6 of 8 for 84 and ran for 59 more.

Then the defense flew escort. Korey Johnson intercepted Army, and after the Black Knights stopped us on fourth down near their end zone, our defense forced a three-and-out. When the Black Knights punted with 5:18 left, our offense took the stick and ran out the clock. We were flagged once all night. One. That's a tidy flight plan. Jaylin Reese led us with nine tackles.

ESPN's recap says that is 22 trophy wins for Air Force, six of them in Troy Calhoun's tenure, and our record against Army now stands at 39-21-1. San Jose State visits Falcon Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 14, at 7 PM ET. Fly, Fight, Win.

articles.title: Arizona State vs Colorado: Fette Throws One, Catches One, 20-10
articles.matchup: Final: Colorado Buffaloes (3-6) 10, Arizona State Sun Devils (5-4) 20, Sat., Nov. 7, Mountain America Stadium, Tempe. Next: at UCF, Sat., Nov. 14, Acrisure Bounce House, Orlando
articles.text:
Arizona State Sun Devils 20, Colorado Buffaloes 10. We won 20-10 in Tempe, and yes, I am in the kiddie pool, sunhat and all, and yes, you should grab some water while you read this. Five and four. Three and three in the Big 12. Four and one at home.

Can we talk about Jake Fette? Our freshman quarterback, in his first home game as QB1, threw a touchdown and caught a touchdown. ESPN's recap says he's the first Arizona State quarterback to do both in one game since Jake Plummer in 1996, and the 1996 team was being honored that same night. You can't write it better. On fourth-and-goal from the 1, Cardae Mack took a direct snap, faked the run and lobbed it to Fette in the end zone. Then Fette dropped a 34-yard beauty to Reed Harris to make it 17-0 at the half. Fette went 13 of 19 for 187. Harris caught four for 103. Mack carried 24 times for 80. Hydrate and dominate.

The second half was a sweat-rate test for the offense, and I'll be honest, we were low on electrolytes. But the defense recovered just fine. Albert Smith III had three sacks. Owen Long made 17 tackles and Martell Hughes made 11. Ashton Stamps had an interception, and Colorado's last real chance died on a fourth-and-15 near midfield with 2:43 left. Carson Smith hit from 31 and 21, and Nick McLarty dropped two punts that Daquwan Dunn downed inside the Colorado 5. Field position is a recovery window, people.

After the game, Dance Theatre of Harlem brought Firebird to ASU Gammage, a 1982 classic set to Stravinsky. A bird rising in fire, in Tempe, on a Saturday night. I'm choosing to take that as a sign.

Now we head to UCF on Saturday, Nov. 14. Florida humidity is real, so fill those water bottles tonight. Forks up.

articles.title: Colorado vs Arizona State: A 17-0 Hole, a Late Rally, 10-20
articles.matchup: Final: Colorado Buffaloes (3-6) 10, Arizona State Sun Devils (5-4) 20, Sat., Nov. 7, Mountain America Stadium, Tempe. Next: vs Houston, Fri., Nov. 13, 10:15 PM ET, Folsom Field, Boulder
articles.text:
Colorado Buffaloes 10, Arizona State Sun Devils 20. A 20-10 loss in Tempe, friends, and I'm swinging in the hammock beneath the Flatirons trying to make the numbers feel better. They won't. Three and six. One and five in the Big 12. One and four on the road.

The first half was a system at absolute zero. Arizona State led 17-0 at the break, and we managed 103 yards of offense, 62 of them in the final 45 seconds. I computed that one myself: about three-fifths of our first-half offense came in the last half-minute. Our first first down arrived around the seven-minute mark of the second quarter. A 74-yard touchdown from Isaac Wilson to Ernest Campbell came back on an illegal man downfield flag. Physics is cruel.

The second half was a different experiment. The defense held Arizona State to one field goal. Lampron was everywhere: 18 tackles, two sacks, three and a half tackles for loss. Liona Lefau made 12 tackles and Santana Hopper had three tackles for loss. Elliott Arnold hit a 39-yard field goal as the third quarter ended, and Wilson found Joseph Williams from 7 to make it 20-10 with 8:14 left. Williams finished with seven catches for 121 yards. Wilson went 20 of 31 for 248.

The rally ran out of energy on a fourth-and-15 near midfield with 2:43 left. We ran for 64 yards on 34 tries, and you can't build a reaction with that little heat.

Back home on Saturday, the ATLAS Institute held its ninth annual Whaaat!? Festival at the Roser ATLAS Center on campus, a full day of experimental games and a buffet of cereals. Experimental games, friends. That's what the first half felt like, minus the cereal.

Houston comes to Folsom Field on Friday night, Nov. 13, at 10:15 PM ET. Bring a blanket, bring the kombucha, and bring the second-half version of this team for all four quarters. Sko Buffs.

articles.title: Wisconsin vs Rutgers: Hopkins Debuts, Bowl Ticket Punched, 31-10
articles.matchup: Final: Rutgers Scarlet Knights (2-7) 10, Wisconsin Badgers (6-3) 31, Sat., Nov. 7, Camp Randall Stadium, Madison. Next: at Maryland, Sat., Nov. 14, 12:00 PM ET, SECU Stadium, College Park
articles.text:
Wisconsin Badgers 31, Rutgers Scarlet Knights 10. (Oom-pah, oom-pah.) That's a 31-10 win at Camp Randall, and I jumped around so hard the cheese hat fell off my head. Six and three. Four and two in the Big Ten. Five and oh at home. And that sixth win makes us bowl eligible for the first time since the 2023 season. Curds for everybody!

Folks, a week after a 30-0 loss at Iowa, a freshman named Ryan Hopkins got the nod as our No. 1 quarterback for the first time and played like he'd been running this huddle since my fullback days. Eighteen of 24, 241 yards, three touchdowns. He hit Eugene Hilton Jr. from 21 on our second series. He hit Ryan Schwendeman from 11 late in the third and then threw the two-pointer to Hilton. And with 10:08 left he found our 6-foot-6 tight end, Jacob Harris, who kept one foot inbounds near midfield, broke a tackle and rumbled 66 yards. A big man running free in Madison. Oom-pah.

Gavin Lahm was three for three, from 51, 26 and 22, and the 26-yarder with 24 seconds left in the half broke a 10-10 tie. After that, the defense slammed the barn door. Rutgers did not score in the second half, we won it 18-0, and we sacked AJ Surace five times. Cooper Catalano made 14 tackles with two and a half for loss, and Mason Posa added eight. Shamar Rigby caught four for 71.

Before kickoff, the Salute to Veterans Tailgate filled Camp Randall Memorial Park, put on by UW Athletics, University Veteran Services and the Wisconsin Department of Veterans Affairs, with replica gear from the Wisconsin Veterans Museum. A fine way to open a Salute to Veterans game, and 66,310 of us finished it the right way.

Next we visit Maryland on Saturday, Nov. 14, at noon ET. Pack the curds and the cheese hat. On, Wisconsin!

articles.title: Rutgers vs Wisconsin: Tied at the Half, Shut Out After, 10-31
articles.matchup: Final: Rutgers Scarlet Knights (2-7) 10, Wisconsin Badgers (6-3) 31, Sat., Nov. 7, Camp Randall Stadium, Madison. Next: vs Nebraska, Sat., Nov. 14, 12:30 PM ET, SHI Stadium, Piscataway
articles.text:
Rutgers Scarlet Knights 10, Wisconsin Badgers 31. A 31-10 loss in Madison, and if you're asking where my mood is tonight, take the Turnpike south past Exit 7A and keep going until the road turns to gravel. Two and seven. One and five in the Big Ten.

Let me be fair to these kids first, because they earned it. We went to Camp Randall without KJ Duff, without Dylan Lonergan, and without offensive linemen Tyler Needham and Kwabena Asamoah. AJ Surace stepped in at quarterback and gave it all a young man can give: 14 of 24 for 161 yards and no turnovers. His 30-yard touchdown to Dyzier Carter tied it 10-10 late in the second quarter. Jack Scullion drilled one from 45. Ben Black III caught six for 70. At that point, I was cruising around Exit 11 with the windows down.

Then the boardwalk arm-wrestle flipped. Wisconsin kicked a field goal with 24 seconds left in the half, then won the second half 18-0. Their freshman quarterback, Ryan Hopkins, opening a game for the first time, finished 18 of 24 for 241 and three touchdowns, and their 6-foot-6 tight end Jacob Harris went 66 yards for the last one. The Badgers sacked Surace five times. We ran 36 times for 94 yards, and Antwan Raymond got 56 of those on 15 tough carries. A couple of flags hurt us, too, including one that erased an interception by JJ Conyers.

I won't sugarcoat it. Seven losses means a second straight losing season. That stings, and I'm not going to pretend otherwise.

Back home on Saturday morning, the Rutgers farmers market was open on Jones Avenue in New Brunswick, selling fresh produce at half off for families using nutrition benefits. That's Jersey at its best: show up, feed your neighbors, no excuses. That's what I want from the last stretch of this season.

Nebraska comes to SHI Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 14, at 12:30 PM ET. Exit 9, folks. Bring your voice. RU-RAH-RAH.

articles.title: FIU vs Missouri State: Lyons Runs for 216, Walk-Off Kick 23-20
articles.matchup: Final: Missouri State Bears (3-6) 20, Florida International Panthers (4-5) 23, Sat., Nov. 7, Pitbull Stadium, Miami. Next: at Delaware, Sat., Nov. 14, 3:00 PM ET, Delaware Stadium, Newark
articles.text:
Florida International Panthers 23, Missouri State Bears 20. ¡Qué noche! A 23-20 walk-off on Homecoming at Pitbull Stadium, a Military Appreciation night too, the first time these two ever met in Miami, and five minutes from campus my abuela is slapping a domino on the table so hard the creamer cups jumped. Four and five. Two and three in Conference USA. Four and one at home. Three-game skid, gone.

Let me set up the dominoes. Devonte Lyons, our redshirt freshman, ran for 216 yards on 24 carries with touchdowns from 6 and 17. FIU Athletics says that is the third-most rushing yards in a game in program history. We ran for 276 as a team, and the defense made a fourth-down stop at our own 8 before we marched 92 yards to go up 17-6. Shamir Sterlin had an interception, and Elisha Baldridge led us with seven tackles.

Then the Bears punched back, because nobody sleeps on anybody in this league. A strip sack, a 51-yard scoop and score, a two-point run, and it was 17-17. Ay, my heart.

Robert Czeremcha hit from 42 with 1:55 left. Missouri State tied it with a field goal. And then, mi gente, JJ Kohl got the ball with seconds left and went to work: 15 yards to Kyle McNeal, 20 to Tyson Carter, then Kohl himself took off for 27 to put us at the 13. Clock it. Then Czeremcha from 35. Good as the clock hit zero. FIU Athletics says it is our first game-winning field goal since Sept. 8, 2012, against Akron, and it is our first back-to-back Homecoming wins since the 2017 to 2019 run.

Kohl finished 18 of 26 for 218 yards, and McNeal and Carter combined for nine catches. Somebody make me a colada, because I am not sleeping tonight anyway.

Next we go north to Delaware on Saturday, Nov. 14, at 3 PM ET. Pack a coat, Panthers. ¡Vamos, FIU!

A 23-20 walk-off on Homecoming at Pitbull Stadium, a Military Appreciation night too, the first time these two ever met in Miami, and five minutes from campus my abuela is slapping a domino on the table so hard the creamer cups jumped. Four and five. Two and three in Conference USA. Four and one at home. Three-game skid, gone.

Let me set up the dominoes. Devonte Lyons, our redshirt freshman, ran for 216 yards on 24 carries with touchdowns from 6 and 17. FIU Athletics says that is the third-most rushing yards in a game in program history. We ran for 276 as a team, and the defense made a fourth-down stop at our own 8 before we marched 92 yards to go up 17-6. Shamir Sterlin had an interception, and Elisha Baldridge led us with seven tackles.
Then the Bears punched back, because nobody sleeps on anybody in this league. A strip sack, a 51-yard scoop and score, a two-point run, and it was 17-17. Ay, my heart.

Robert Czeremcha hit from 42 with 1:55 left. Missouri State tied it with a field goal. And then, mi gente, JJ Kohl got the ball with seconds left and went to work: 15 yards to Kyle McNeal, 20 to Tyson Carter, then Kohl himself took off for 27 to put us at the 13. Clock it. Then Czeremcha from 35. Good as the clock hit zero. FIU Athletics says it is our first game-winning field goal since Sept. 8, 2012, against Akron, and it is our first back-to-back Homecoming wins since the 2017 to 2019 run.
Kohl finished 18 of 26 for 218 yards, and McNeal and Carter combined for nine catches. Somebody make me a colada, because I am not sleeping tonight anyway.
Next we go north to Delaware on Saturday, Nov. 14, at 3 PM ET. Pack a coat, Panthers. ¡Vamos, FIU!

Devonte Lyons ran for 216 yards and two touchdowns, the third-most rushing yards in a game in program history, per FIU Athletics.
The Bears tied it twice. Our kicker had the last word, and abuela had the last domino.
Next: at Delaware, Saturday, Nov. 14, 3:00 PM ET, Delaware Stadium, Newark.

articles.title: Missouri State vs FIU: Cooper's Scoop, Obeid's Four, Lost 20-23
articles.matchup: Final: Missouri State Bears (3-6) 20, Florida International Panthers (4-5) 23, Sat., Nov. 7, Pitbull Stadium, Miami. Next: vs New Mexico State, Sat., Nov. 14, 3:00 PM ET, Robert W. Plaster Stadium, Springfield
articles.text:
Missouri State Bears 20, Florida International Panthers 23. That 23-20 loss in Miami came on a field goal with no time left, and I have guided enough float trips to know the river does not care how hard you paddled. Three and six. Two and three in Conference USA. Oh and five on the road.

Here's how we read the current. It was 3-3 at the half after both teams traded interceptions deep in the red zone, with Joel Boamah getting ours. Yousef Obeid put us ahead 6-3 from 42 early in the third. Then Devonte Lyons found the fast water. He ran for 216 yards and two touchdowns, FIU went 92 yards for the second one, and we were down 17-6 early in the fourth.

Respect the rocks, then climb back in the canoe. Obeid hit from 22. Then J.J. O'Neal stripped the quarterback, Jashawn Cooper scooped it up and ran 51 yards to the end zone, and Henry Belin IV ran in the two-pointer. Tied 17-17 with 6:42 left, and I'd like that whole sequence framed and hung in every bait shop on the James River.

FIU kicked a 42-yarder with 1:55 left. Belin answered with a nine-play, 60-yard drive, finding Jmariyae Robinson for 23 and 12 along the way, and Obeid tied it from 30. That was his fourth field goal of the night. The young man was perfect. Jared Lloyd made 17 tackles, which is what a guide calls carrying the whole boat.

Then FIU got the ball back, went 64 yards in six plays and kicked the winner from 35 as the clock hit zero. Belin threw for 225, Robinson caught six for 93 and Isaiah Myers had five for 67, but 276 Panther rushing yards were a lot of white water.

Back home that night, MercyMe, Jeremy Camp, Tim Timmons and Sam Wesley played Great Southern Bank Arena on our campus, so Springfield had a good song to sing while we drove home. New Mexico State visits Plaster Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 14, at 3 PM ET. Keep everybody in the canoe. Go Bears.

articles.title: Kansas vs UCF: 25 Straight Points, One Second Short, 32-33
articles.matchup: Final: UCF Knights (5-4) 33, Kansas Jayhawks (3-6) 32, Sat., Nov. 7, David Booth Kansas Memorial Stadium, Lawrence. Next: at West Virginia, Sat., Nov. 14, Milan Puskar Stadium, Morgantown
articles.text:
Kansas Jayhawks 32, UCF Knights 33. One point, one second, one 33-32 loss at the Booth, and I have a basketball mind, so let me say it the way my brain processes it: we lost on a buzzer-beater. Three and six. One and five in the Big 12. Somebody take the remote from me before I rewatch it again.

The opening was a fast break. Trey Lathan intercepted a throw on UCF's first snap and returned it to the 3, and Isaiah Marshall scored from 1. Then we went cold from the field. UCF led 12-7 at the half, held us to 61 first-half yards, and pushed it to 26-7 early in the third. In my math, that's a 19-point deficit in football, which is roughly a 19-point deficit in basketball. I did the math myself. It's the same number.

And then, Allen Fieldhouse energy in a football stadium. Marshall ran 30 yards for a score. Khijohnn Cummings-Coleman powered in from 1. Martin Connington made a 34-yard field goal. Dylan Edwards scored from 2 with 1:06 left, and Marshall threw the two-point try to Nik McMillan. Twenty-five straight points. That's eight threes and a free throw, by my count, and 31,008 of us were up on our feet.

Marshall was terrific: 125 yards rushing on 13 carries with two touchdowns, and 21 of 32 for 210 through the air. Keaton Kubecka caught five for 71.

Then UCF went 73 yards in less than a minute and scored from 6 with one second on the clock. Replay upheld it. In hoops you'd foul there. Football never gives you that option.

Back home in Lawrence on Saturday, the Lawrence Arts Center ran Napoleon's Dynamite Musical Parody at 2 and 7 p.m. A comedy about a guy who keeps trying, keeps coming up a little short, and keeps dancing anyway. I relate. We go to West Virginia on Saturday, Nov. 14. Rock Chalk.

articles.title: UCF vs Kansas: Piening at the Pylon, Road Streak Ends 33-32
articles.matchup: Final: UCF Knights (5-4) 33, Kansas Jayhawks (3-6) 32, Sat., Nov. 7, David Booth Kansas Memorial Stadium, Lawrence. Next: vs Arizona State, Sat., Nov. 14, Acrisure Bounce House, Orlando
articles.text:
UCF Knights 33, Kansas Jayhawks 32. I am typing this 33-32 win with the knight's helmet on, visor down, because that was the wildest ride Lawrence has run all year and I designed rides for a living. Five and four. Three and three in the Big 12. And the 12-game road losing streak? Closed for permanent maintenance.

Ride Check, first hill: after an early interception set Kansas up at our 3, Isaiah Marshall punched it in and we trailed 7-0. Then we climbed. Will Stone hit from 37 and 23, Duane Thomas Jr. ran one in from 10, and we held the Jayhawks to 61 yards in the first half. Out of the break, Taevion Swint scored from 1 and Alonza Barnett III hit Josh Derry for 44. That made it 26-7. Smooth track, full speed.

Then the drop nobody posted a warning sign for. Kansas scored 25 straight points, and Dylan Edwards took a 32-26 lead into our faces with 1:06 left.

Here is where my gauge broke. Barnett, in his first full game back from a hamstring injury, went 10 plays and 73 yards in less than a minute, with 65 of his yards on that drive, and found Caden Piening at the left pylon from 6 with one second showing. Replay review. Call stands. Somewhere in Lawrence a seismograph twitched. Barnett finished 18 of 31 for 251 yards and two scores, Derry caught eight for 143, and Curtis Tackett made 11 tackles. We were perfect on five red-zone trips and drew zero penalties. Zero. That ride clears inspection.

Back home that night, the UCF Percussion Ensemble and Steel Band played Beyond Drums at a church on East Robinson Street, part of the Milk District Salon Concert Series. Their whole point is that percussion is more than drums. Our point today: a road trip can be more than a loss. Arizona State visits the Bounce House on Saturday, Nov. 14. Keep your hands and feet inside the stadium, and Charge On.

articles.title: New Mexico State vs Liberty: Williams Shines, Aggies Fall 14-30
articles.matchup: Final: Liberty Flames (8-1) 30, New Mexico State Aggies (3-6) 14, Sat., Nov. 7, Aggie Memorial Stadium, Las Cruces. Next: at Missouri State, Sat., Nov. 14, 3:00 PM ET, Robert W. Plaster Stadium, Springfield
articles.text:
Liberty 30, New Mexico State 14. ¡Ay, Aggies! I'll give this one a chile grade of mild with a little char, and I mean that kindly. Downtown that morning, Las Cruces held its 30th annual Veterans Day Parade, with a cannon blast to kick it off and a theme of honoring 250 years of military service to the nation. The Organ Mountains had a busy day watching.

And our opening drive? Hatch hot. Trey Hedden, back in the No. 1 job, took us 75 yards in seven plays and hit AJ Williams III for a 24-yard touchdown. 7-0 Aggies, and Liberty had not trailed in conference play all season.

Then Liberty kicked three field goals, and a 15-yard touchdown with 18 seconds left in the half made it 16-7. After a scoreless third quarter, we cooked up a 12-play, 90-yard drive, and Hedden found Williams again from 5 yards out. 16-14 early in the fourth, and Aggie Memorial was roasting.

Williams was the whole chile field tonight: eight catches for 150 yards and two touchdowns, with a long of 44. Hedden finished 19 of 29 for 256 yards. On defense, Tory Gethers made 10 tackles with a sack and two tackles for loss, Nick Session also had 10, and Chance Barron had eight. Sone Aupiu got a sack too. Brody Richter averaged 49.3 a punt, with a 58-yarder that I'd grade Christmas-style.

The hard part: Liberty answered with a five-play, 78-yard drive, our fourth-down try came up short on the next series, and the Flames scored again. We ran for only 44 yards, and James Jones was held to 51 on 15 carries. Three turnovers, too, including an interception in the final minute.

We're 3-6 and 2-3 in Conference USA, and 2-3 at home. Next is a trip to Missouri State on Saturday, Nov. 14, at 3 PM ET at Robert W. Plaster Stadium in Springfield. Roast it, peel it, keep going. Aggies up.

We led the conference leaders. For a while, the whole valley smelled like roasting chile.

articles.title: Liberty vs New Mexico State: Flames Answer, Win 30-14
articles.matchup: Final: Liberty Flames (8-1) 30, New Mexico State Aggies (3-6) 14, Sat., Nov. 7, Aggie Memorial Stadium, Las Cruces. Next: vs. Middle Tennessee, Sat., Nov. 14, 3:30 PM ET, Williams Stadium (VA), Lynchburg
articles.text:
Liberty 30, New Mexico State 14, and praise the Lord and hand me the program, we are 8-1! Back home, the Harvest Festival set up on the open fields at 2219 Coffee Road with live music from 3 to 9, the Liberty Worship Collective among the artists, and every ticket going to ministry. Lynchburg had a harvest. Out in the desert, so did our Flames.

Now, I'll tell you the truth, gently. We trailed in a conference game for the first time this season when the Aggies marched 75 yards on their opening drive. My middle schoolers would have panicked. These young men didn't. Chase Reeves answered with a 35-yard field goal, then hit from 41 and 49. Jayden Davis recovered a fumble to set up one of those kicks.

And with 18 seconds left in the half, Deshawn Purdie hit Makai Jackson for a 15-yard touchdown that was ruled incomplete on the field and overturned on review. Jackson got a foot down and held on. 16-7 at the break.

The Aggies came back hard, going 90 yards on 12 plays to make it 16-14 early in the fourth. Here's where I was proudest. We answered with a five-play, 78-yard drive, and Kam Davis scored from 8. Then the defense stopped them on downs, and Peyton Jones finished a 10-play, 72-yard drive with a 1-yard plunge.

Purdie went 19 of 28 for 252 yards and a touchdown with no interceptions. Jackson caught six balls for 76 yards, Rashawn Cunningham had four for 51, and Darius Copeland had two for 53. Kam Davis ran 15 times for 63. Derrell Farrar made 10 tackles, and Aidan Vaughan and Michael Floyde each came up with an interception. We held the ball for 37:05, held their ground game to 44 yards and never gave it away. Sam Crossan averaged 47.7 a punt. Reeves went three for three on field goals and kicks after touchdowns, 12 points all by himself.

We're 8-1 and 5-0 in Conference USA. Middle Tennessee comes to Williams Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 14, at 3:30 PM ET. Come on home, family. Go Flames!

articles.title: Georgia Tech vs Louisville: Jackets Grounded at Home, 17-44
articles.matchup: Final: Louisville Cardinals (6-3) 44, Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets (2-7) 17, Sat., Nov. 7, Bobby Dodd Stadium, Atlanta. Next: at Clemson, Sat., Nov. 14, 12:30 PM ET, Memorial Stadium, Clemson
articles.text:
Louisville 44, Georgia Tech 17. Jackets fans, I've re-run this simulation a few times now, and the outputs don't change. It was Military Appreciation Day at Bobby Dodd, and 44,680 of us came out to Midtown to honor those who served. That part of the night went exactly to plan. The football did not.

We actually opened fine. Aidan Birr hit a 32-yard field goal to tie it 3-3 in the first quarter. Then Louisville scored on an 8-yard throw, a 4-yard throw and a 52-yard end-around, and the curve bent away from us fast. 24-3 in the second quarter is a steep slope. Louisville averaged 7.0 yards a carry, which by my math is a first down every carry and a half.

The staff tried a new variable in the first half, alternating Alberto Mendoza and Grady Adamson drive by drive. Mendoza found Isaiah Fuhrmann for a 10-yard touchdown with 10 seconds left before the half, and Adamson hit Chris Corbo for an 11-yard score in the fourth. Mendoza went 13 of 25 for 148, and Adamson 12 of 19 for 93 with an interception.

The good data points: Justice Haynes ran 12 times for 87 yards, 7.3 a carry, with a 33-yard burst. Dalen Penson caught five balls for 66 yards, and Corbo caught six. Tae Harris and Taje McCoy made eight tackles each, and Ronnie Thomas III recovered a fumble. Alex Bacchetta punted four times for a 43.3 average, and graph paper says those were textbook parabolas.

The bug report is short and painful: 4 of 17 on third down, 251 rushing yards allowed, and a third straight loss. Both quarterbacks deserve credit for staying in rhythm while swapping in and out all half. I'll keep debugging, and I'll keep believing.

We're 2-7 and 1-5 in the ACC. Next is a trip to Clemson on Saturday, Nov. 14, at 12:30 PM ET at Memorial Stadium. Recalibrate and launch again, Jackets.

articles.title: Louisville vs Georgia Tech: Kienholz Leads the Romp, 44-17
articles.matchup: Final: Louisville Cardinals (6-3) 44, Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets (2-7) 17, Sat., Nov. 7, Bobby Dodd Stadium, Atlanta. Next: at North Carolina, Sat., Nov. 14, time TBA, Kenan Stadium, Chapel Hill
articles.text:
Louisville 44, Georgia Tech 17. Hold your hats, everybody, and then throw them in the air! That's four wins in a row, bowl eligibility for the sixth straight season, and the 100th win of Jeff Brohm's head coaching career. Back home, the Louisville Orchestra played Vivaldi's Four Seasons and Max Richter's reworking of it at The Brown Theatre on West Broadway at 7:30. Down in Atlanta at the very same hour, our Cardinals were composing a fourth straight win of their own.

Carson Hilbert opened with a 42-yard field goal. Lincoln Kienholz threw an 8-yard touchdown to Tre Richardson, then a 4-yarder to TreyShun Hurry. Then Richardson took an end-around 52 yards to the end zone, and I nearly flung my foam finger into the next section. 24-3 in the second quarter. By halftime it was 27-10.

Kienholz ran the whole show: 17 of 25 for 182 yards and two touchdowns, plus 81 rushing yards on nine carries. Hurry caught eight balls for 104 yards. Richardson finished with 104 all-purpose yards and two scores. As a team we ran for 251 yards at 7.0 a carry. Keyjuan Brown had 54, Isaac Brown scored from 11 for his 10th touchdown of the season, and Braxton Jennings added a 2-yard score late.

Hilbert made all three of his field goals and all five kicks after touchdowns, 14 points from one right foot. Jackson Voth brought back three punts for 81 yards, including a 68-yarder.

On defense, Stanquan Clark made eight tackles with 1.5 for loss, Kalib Perry had seven, and Micah Rice came up with an interception. Georgia Tech went 4 of 17 on third down. My face-paint score for this one? Full coat of Cardinal red, both cheeks and the ears.

We're 6-3 and 5-2 in the ACC, still in the conference race. Next is a trip to North Carolina on Saturday, Nov. 14, at Kenan Stadium in Chapel Hill, kickoff time to be announced. Go Cards!

articles.title: Navy vs Temple: Gutierrez Runs for Five, Steadies the Ship 42-35
articles.matchup: Final: Temple Owls (2-7) 35, Navy Midshipmen (3-6) 42, Sat., Nov. 7, Navy-Marine Corps Memorial Stadium, Annapolis. Next: vs Memphis, Sat., Nov. 21, 12:00 PM ET, Navy-Marine Corps Memorial Stadium, Annapolis
articles.text:
Navy Midshipmen 42, Temple Owls 35. That's a 42-35 win in Annapolis, so ring the ship's bell, because we came through a squall to make port. Three and six. Two and four in the American. On a Saturday when the Yard held its Honor Our Fallen Heroes events and welcomed back the classes of 2011, 2016 and 2021 for reunion weekend, this crew found a way home.

The opening watch was a clinic. Jackson Gutierrez ran in from 1, from 1, from 1 and from 6, and we were up 28-0 with 1:14 left in the half. Full speed, clear seas.

Then the weather turned. JoJo Bermudez took a punt back 78 yards on the final play of the half, caught a 41-yard touchdown in the third, and Temple scored 21 points in the fourth. Our fake punt failed, and Jaxon Smolik made us pay with a 25-yard touchdown to Jayce Freeman that tied it 35-35 with 5:35 to go. I will not pretend that stretch was calm. It was rough water. Nolan McCamy made seven tackles with a sack, and Coleman Cauley added a sack and a half with three hurries, but the Owls kept coming.

Time to plot a course out of it. Our answer was nine plays and 75 yards, every inch of it on the ground, and the big wave was Gutierrez breaking tackles on a 39-yard run. He finished it himself from 4 with 1:14 left. Career-high five rushing touchdowns, 180 yards on 30 carries, and 178 more through the air, including a 49-yard strike to Jordan Collins, who had 112 yards on two catches. Michael Barrow ground out 109 on 21 carries. We ran for 317 yards and held the ball for 40 minutes and 46 seconds. Giuseppe Sessi intercepted Smolik.

Now an open week to patch the hull, then Memphis comes to Navy-Marine Corps Memorial Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 21, at noon ET. Anchors aweigh.

articles.title: Temple vs Navy: Down 28-0, Tied at 35, Beaten 35-42
articles.matchup: Final: Temple Owls (2-7) 35, Navy Midshipmen (3-6) 42, Sat., Nov. 7, Navy-Marine Corps Memorial Stadium, Annapolis. Next: vs UAB, Sat., Nov. 14, 1:00 PM ET, Lincoln Financial Field, Philadelphia
articles.text:
Temple Owls 35, Navy Midshipmen 42. We lost 42-35 in Annapolis, and I need everybody in Philly to hear me out before they open their mouths: we were down 28-0 and we tied this game at 35. Two and seven. One and four in the American. Loss column, sure. Quit column, empty.

Same day, same opponent, back home on North Broad: Temple women's basketball hosted Navy at the Liacouras Center at 2 PM, with free hot dogs for the first 150 students. So Saturday in North Philly was Temple versus Navy from lunch to dinner, and our football Owls gave the Midshipmen the full Rocky treatment in the second half.

The first half was the part of the movie where Rocky gets knocked down. Jackson Gutierrez ran in four short touchdowns and it was 28-0. Then, on the final play of the half, JoJo Bermudez fielded a punt and went 78 yards to the house. That was the bell. Out of the break, Jaxon Smolik hit Bermudez for a 41-yard score.

And the fourth quarter? Pure montage. Smolik found Jayce Freeman from 6. Samuel Brown V plowed in from 1. Navy tried a fake punt, it failed, and Smolik hit Freeman again, this time from 25, to tie it 35-35 with 5:35 left. Twenty-one points in the fourth. Smolik finished with three touchdown throws, Freeman caught two, and Joseph Auzenne came up with an interception while Adrian Laing recovered a fumble.

Then Navy did what Navy does. Nine plays, 75 yards, all on the ground, with Gutierrez breaking tackles on a 39-yard run before he scored from 4 with 1:14 left. He ran for 180 yards and five touchdowns. Navy ran for 317, held the ball for 40 minutes and 46 seconds, and we managed 45 yards rushing and nine first downs. Avery Powell made 13 tackles, Saboor Karriem made 11 and Jordan Montgomery made 10, and that tells you how many snaps our defense played.

UAB comes to Lincoln Financial Field on Saturday, Nov. 14, at 1 PM ET. Home cooking, South Philly. Bring that fourth-quarter fight from the first snap. That's Temple Made.

articles.title: Louisiana vs South Alabama: Garner Sparks Bowl Bid, 28-26
articles.matchup: Final: Louisiana Ragin' Cajuns (6-3) 28, South Alabama Jaguars (4-5) 26, Sat., Nov. 7, Our Lady of Lourdes Stadium, Lafayette. Next: at UL Monroe, Thu., Nov. 12, 9:00 PM ET, Malone Stadium, Monroe
articles.text:
Louisiana 28, South Alabama 26, and mes amis, we are bowl-eligible for the ninth straight season. I two-stepped around the desk until the neighbors knocked. Earlier that afternoon at Vermilionville, the weekly Cajun Jam filled the Performance Center from 1 to 3 with players of every level. By kickoff, I'd swear our offense was playing the same waltz.

JJ Garner didn't wait for the music. He took the opening kickoff 100 yards for a touchdown. Then on the first play of the second quarter, he ran 65 yards for another. Magnifique! He finished with 136 rushing yards on just 10 carries.

South Alabama tied it 14-14 on an interception return, and Lunch Winfield answered with a 14-yard touchdown run. In the third quarter he threw a 27-yard touchdown to Shelton Sampson Jr. for 28-17. Winfield went 10 of 14 for 147 yards and ran for 97 more. As a team we ran for 312 yards at 7.1 a carry and converted 8 of 13 third downs. My accountant brain loves a column like that.

Then came the nervous part. The Jaguars pulled to 28-26 on a 45-yard run and a 50-yard field goal, and our 48-yard try with four minutes to go was no good. Ça c'est stressful. But Jake St. Andre sacked Bishop Davenport at midfield, and on the next snap Micah Johnson intercepted him with less than two minutes left. Winfield took a knee, and the boudin tasted like victory.

St. Andre led us with nine tackles. Collin Jacob had eight, Micah Johnson had six with 1.5 tackles for loss, and Maxie Baudoin IV added a sack. Tony Sterner was four for four on kicks after touchdowns, and 14,194 of us got to sing all night.

We're 6-3, 5-0 at home and 3-2 in the Sun Belt. A short week sends us to UL Monroe on Thursday, Nov. 12, at 9 PM ET at Malone Stadium in Monroe. Allons, Cajuns!

articles.title: South Alabama vs Louisiana: Jags Rally, Fall Short 26-28
articles.matchup: Final: Louisiana Ragin' Cajuns (6-3) 28, South Alabama Jaguars (4-5) 26, Sat., Nov. 7, Our Lady of Lourdes Stadium, Lafayette. Next: vs. Troy, Sat., Nov. 14, 7:00 PM ET, Hancock Whitney Stadium, Mobile
articles.text:
Louisiana 28, South Alabama 26. Y'all, I had my towel spinning over my head by the fourth quarter, and I still don't know if I was cheering or begging. Back home on the Avenue, the Historic Avenue Cultural Center threw its third annual Block Party from 11 to 3, with music, films and a sneak peek at the Ace Theatre restoration that will be the future home of the Excelsior Band. Mobile knows how to throw a party. Our Jaguars nearly crashed one in Lafayette.

It opened rough: JJ Garner took the opening kickoff 100 yards. Our answer was pure Gulf Coast grit, a 14-play, 63-yard drive that Bishop Davenport finished with a 1-yard run. After Garner broke a 65-yarder to open the second quarter, Jaylen Moson jumped a throw and returned it 72 yards for a touchdown. 14-14. I may have hollered at a stranger.

Dylan Freebury hit a 44-yard field goal before the half to get us to 21-17. Down 28-17 in the third, Davenport took off on a 45-yard touchdown run. The two-point try came up short, but Freebury drilled a 50-yarder early in the fourth, and it was 28-26.

Then our defense got the ball back with four minutes to go after a Louisiana field goal try missed. We had our chance. Davenport was sacked at midfield, and his next throw was intercepted with less than two minutes left. That's the one I'll be drawing up on a napkin all week, trying to fix it.

Davenport was terrific: 16 of 22 for 210 yards, plus two rushing touchdowns. Brendan Jenkins caught six balls for 101 yards. Keenan Phillips returned five kickoffs for 120. Seidrion Langston led us with eight tackles, Xavious Anderson Jr. had seven, and E'Mauri Smiley got a sack. We went 2 for 2 on fourth down. The part we have to fix is the run defense, which gave up 312 yards.

We're 4-5 and 2-3 in the Sun Belt. Troy comes to Hancock Whitney Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 14, at 7 PM ET. Pull up a lawn chair, Mobile, and bring the noise. Go Jags.

articles.title: Michigan State vs Michigan: Boyd's Five Kicks Win Bunyan 15-6
articles.matchup: Final: Michigan State (3-6) 15, Michigan (5-4) 6, Sat., Nov. 7, Michigan Stadium, Ann Arbor. Next: vs. Washington, Sat., Nov. 14, Spartan Stadium, East Lansing
articles.text:
Michigan State 15, Michigan 6, and Paul Bunyan is coming home to East Lansing, where he belongs. On Saturday our hockey team closed its series with Boston University at Munn Ice Arena and the Michigan State Open wrestling tournament ran all day at Jenison Field House. Then the football team went down the road to that little suburb called Ann Arbor and caught the whole game.

I'm a catcher, so let me call the pitches. First pitch: Liam Boyd. He kicked from 21 and 37 for a 6-0 halftime lead. Second pitch: the long drive. From our own 1, we went 79 yards in 17 plays and took nearly 11 minutes off the clock, and Boyd kicked from 38. Third pitch, and fourth, and fifth: Boyd again, from 24 and 49. Five attempts, five makes. Strike them all out.

Our defense was the real ace. We forced four turnovers and had five sacks. Devin Vaught intercepted Tommy Carr in the first quarter. NiJhay Burt intercepted him in the fourth, then forced and recovered Andrew Marsh's fumble. Nikai Martinez recovered a fumble and made seven tackles, and Trey Lisle had a sack. On Michigan's two-point try with 1:35 left, Carr got sacked again.

Alessio Milivojevic came back from injury and went 21 of 32 for 188 yards with no turnovers. Chrishon McCray caught six of those for 92 yards. Brandon Tullis carried 25 times for a career-high 86 yards with four running backs out hurt. We held the ball for 38 minutes and 7 seconds.

The AP says this snaps a six-game losing streak, ends a 13-game Big Ten losing streak for Pat Fitzgerald, and is our first win against Michigan since 2021. We are 3-6 and 1-5 in the Big Ten. Washington comes to Spartan Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 14. Bring Paul. He deserves a home crowd.

articles.matchup: Final: Michigan State (3-6) 15, Michigan (5-4) 6, Sat., Nov. 7, Michigan Stadium, Ann Arbor. Next: at Oregon, Sat., Nov. 14, Autzen Stadium, Eugene
articles.text:
Michigan State 15, Michigan 6, and I have taken off the maize sweater and folded it very carefully, the way you fold a flag. It was a Blue Out and our Military Appreciation Game at the Big House, 111,172 people in the stands for the Paul Bunyan Trophy, and the trophy is riding home to East Lansing tonight.

articles.title: Kennesaw State vs Delaware: Bryson's 99, Varnes' 63, 42-40
articles.matchup: Final: Delaware Blue Hens (4-5) 40, Kennesaw State Owls (3-6) 42, Sat., Nov. 7, Walens Family Field at Fifth Third Stadium, Kennesaw. Next: at Sam Houston, Sat., Nov. 14, 2:00 PM ET, Elliott T. Bowers Stadium, Huntsville
articles.text:
Kennesaw State Owls 42, Delaware Blue Hens 40. Final score 42-40 on Homecoming, and I need a minute to let my heart rate recompile. Three and six. Two and three in Conference USA. It was also our Mental Health Awareness game, which is funny, because this one tested everybody's.

Commit number one shipped in 13 seconds. Davis Bryson took the opening kickoff 99 yards for a touchdown, and the 10,300 at Fifth Third Stadium were on their feet before the popcorn cooled. Then Delaware pushed back hard. A 7-yard interception return put us down 15-6 in the first quarter, and this game turned into a back-and-forth merge conflict for the next three quarters.

We kept resolving it. Rickie Collins ran in from 8. Boogie Woods III ripped off a 26-yard touchdown run and later punched in from 1 with 22 seconds left in the half for a 30-22 lead. Woods finished with 90 yards and two scores on 15 carries. Daniel Kinney was flawless, three for three on field goals from 28, 29 and 35, and three for three on extras. Down 34-33 heading into the fourth, Landon Varnes found Reed Jesiolowski for a 63-yard touchdown with 14:18 left, and Kinney's 35-yarder with 8:25 left made it 42-34.

Bug report, because I log it all: Nick Minicucci threw for 408 yards against us, and Bryson Graves had 125 of them. We committed 15 penalties for 129 yards, which is a performance issue I would like patched before next week. Delaware scored with 24 seconds left, and the two-point try that could have tied it fell incomplete. Isaac Paul led us with 10 tackles, Tywon Christopher got a sack, and Bryson added seven catches for 69 to go with his return. We went 11 of 21 on third down, and that kept us alive.

Next deployment: Sam Houston, Saturday, Nov. 14, at 2 PM ET at Elliott T. Bowers Stadium in Huntsville. Ship it. Let's go, Owls.

articles.title: Delaware vs Kennesaw State: Minicucci's 408 Not Enough, 40-42
articles.matchup: Final: Delaware Blue Hens (4-5) 40, Kennesaw State Owls (3-6) 42, Sat., Nov. 7, Walens Family Field at Fifth Third Stadium, Kennesaw. Next: vs Florida International, Sat., Nov. 14, 3:00 PM ET, Delaware Stadium, Newark
articles.text:
Delaware Blue Hens 40, Kennesaw State Owls 42. Final score 42-40 in Kennesaw, and the last page of this chapter tore right out of the binding. Nick Minicucci hit Bryson Graves from 17 with 24 seconds left to cut it to two, the two-point try failed, and that was the book. Four and five. Two and three in Conference USA.

Back in Newark on Saturday, the university held Blue and Golden, its fall open house, with faculty from every one of its 150-plus majors showing high schoolers around campus. If any of those future Hens were checking the score on the drive home, I hope they saw how this team fought, because the effort deserves a footnote in bold.

Minicucci was magnificent: 35 of 54 for 408 yards, two touchdowns and zero interceptions. Graves caught seven for 125. Da'Wain Lofton caught five for 78, Donovan Lewis caught five for 73 and scored from 12 to put us up 31-30 in the third, and Sean Wilson grabbed six. Viron Ellison Jr. punched in two 1-yard touchdowns. Trace Scott III chose the perfect afternoon for his first career interception and his first touchdown, a 7-yard return that made it 15-6. George Mullins intercepted another one. Tucker Smack drilled a 54-yarder as the first half expired and a 36-yarder for a 34-33 lead after three.

Annotations on what went wrong: they opened the game with a 99-yard kickoff return by Davis Bryson before most of us had found our seats. Landon Varnes hit Reed Jesiolowski for 63 yards to retake the lead early in the fourth, and Daniel Kinney made all three of his field goals. We missed three two-point tries, lost a fumble, and gave up 11 of 21 on third down. Twenty-nine first downs and 493 yards, and still two points short.

Florida International comes to Delaware Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 14, at 3 PM ET. Home again in the First State. I will have my blue pen ready, and I expect a happier ending. Go Hens.

articles.title: Troy vs Louisiana Tech: Five Giveaways Sink Homecoming, 17-41
articles.matchup: Final: Louisiana Tech Bulldogs (7-2) 41, Troy Trojans (4-5) 17, Sat., Nov. 7, Veterans Memorial Stadium (AL), Troy. Next: at South Alabama, Sat., Nov. 14, 7:00 PM ET, Hancock Whitney Stadium, Mobile
articles.text:
Louisiana Tech 41, Troy 17. That's peanuts, buddy, and I know it isn't. It was Homecoming at The Vet. The parade went around the Square in downtown Troy at 10 that morning with the Sound of the South, and Charles Oliver, our Hall of Famer and 1976 NAIA 400-meter champion, was the honorary captain. A town dressed in its Saturday best deserved a better ending.

We had our moments. Our first touchdown drive went 15 plays and 83 yards, and Gavin Griffin finished it from 2 for a 7-3 lead. Hayden Wolfe hit a 41-yard field goal late in the half. Then early in the third, Keno Jones sacked Blake Baker, the ball came loose, and Delvin Whitaker fell on it in the end zone. 20-17. The Vet was shaking like a peanut sheller at harvest.

Then came the stretch I'll be up all night watching. Tech went 74 yards on 15 plays to make it 27-17. On our very next snap, a Tucker Kilcrease throw was intercepted and run back to our 11, and they scored one play later. Seventeen seconds of game clock turned a close one into a 34-17 hole.

The ball security is the whole story. We lost four fumbles and threw an interception, five turnovers in all, and the last came on a strip-sack that Alonzo Jackson Jr. returned 66 yards with 1:05 left, ending a 16-play drive of ours. We ran for only 47 yards and went 3 of 15 on third down.

Plenty of Trojans played their hearts out, though. Justin Powe made 13 tackles. Donnie Smith had nine, with a sack and two tackles for loss. Whitaker had a sack and that touchdown, and Jones had a sack too. Kilcrease threw for 215 yards, Howard Kinchen caught two for 63, and Evan Crenshaw punted five times for a 44.6 average.

We're 4-5 and 2-3 in the Sun Belt. Next is the rivalry trip to South Alabama, Saturday, Nov. 14, at 7 PM ET at Hancock Whitney Stadium in Mobile. Shell it, roast it, move on. Go Trojans.

articles.title: Louisiana Tech vs Troy: Bulldogs Ripen on the Road, 41-17
articles.matchup: Final: Louisiana Tech Bulldogs (7-2) 41, Troy Trojans (4-5) 17, Sat., Nov. 7, Veterans Memorial Stadium (AL), Troy. Next: vs. Southern Miss, Sat., Nov. 14, 5:00 PM ET, Joe Aillet Stadium, Ruston
articles.text:
Louisiana Tech 41, Troy 17. Now that's a Saturday! Y'all, the carpet in my den took another fullback dive tonight. Back home in Ruston, our volleyball team hosted Arkansas State for Senior Day at 1 o'clock, and two hours later the football Bulldogs kicked off at Troy's Homecoming and spoiled the party in the most polite north-Louisiana way you can spoil one.

Kaegan Kent got us going with a 45-yard field goal on the opening drive. Troy answered with a 15-play march, but our defense turned the second quarter into a harvest. Blake Baker found Marcus Calwise Jr. for a 28-yard touchdown, Kent added a 28-yard kick, and Sergio Snider plunged in from the 7. Twenty-to-ten at the half, and Granddaddy would have nodded.

Troy got a strip-sack touchdown early in the third to make it 20-17, and I'll admit I bruised a little. Then the Bulldogs went 74 yards in 15 plays, eating up seven minutes, and Trey Kukuk flipped a 2-yard touchdown to Eli Finley. On Troy's very next snap, Janard Lockhardt intercepted it and ran it back 27 yards to the 11. Andrew Burnette scored on the next play. Seventeen seconds, two touchdowns.

Calwise was the best fruit on the tree, nine catches for 137 yards. Baker went 16 of 19 for 177, and Kukuk 8 of 10 with a score. Kent made both field goals and all five kicks after touchdowns.

And the defense, Lord have mercy. Alonzo Jackson Jr. made 11 tackles with two sacks and 2.5 tackles for loss, and with 1:05 left, after Kolbe Fields knocked the ball loose on a sack, Jackson scooped it and ran 66 yards for the last score. Fields had 10 tackles of his own. Troy ran for 47 yards and turned it loose five times. Lexington Matthews punted four times for a 44.5 average.

We're 7-2 and 5-0 in the Sun Belt, and the good ones take a whole season to ripen. Southern Miss comes to Joe Aillet Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 14, at 5 PM ET. Come home hungry, Ruston.

articles.title: Jacksonville State vs Sam Houston: Homecoming Rout 47-14
articles.matchup: Final: Jacksonville State (7-2) 47, Sam Houston (1-8) 14, Sat., Nov. 7, AmFirst Stadium, Jacksonville. Next: at Western Kentucky, Sat., Nov. 14, Houchens Industries-L.T. Smith Stadium, Bowling Green
articles.text:
Jacksonville State 47, Sam Houston 14, on Homecoming, and pull up a chair for Smokehouse Talk, because this brisket came off the pit perfect. The theme this year was Cocky Reigns Supreme, the parade rolled through the Friendliest Campus in the South, and 20,476 folks filled AmFirst Stadium to watch the Gamecocks do exactly that.

Low and slow at first. Nobody scored in the first quarter, and I didn't fret one bit. Good smoke takes time. Then Caden Creel found Jamill Williams for a 31-yard touchdown, Garrison Rippa kicked a 45-yard field goal, and Jalen Likely ran it in from 8 with 25 seconds left in the half. That's 17-0 at the break, and the bark was setting up nice. I sliced off a burnt end in my own backyard just to celebrate.

Creel opened the third quarter with a 67-yard touchdown to Deondre Johnson. Then the fourth quarter was like opening the smoker door. Creel ran in from 4, the defense sacked Landyn Locke in the end zone for a safety, and Williams took the free kick back 85 yards for a touchdown. It was 40-7 with 12:09 left. Jacob Cornejo added a 1-yard run late.

Creel completed 18 of 28 for 246 yards and two touchdowns, ran for 87 more and a score, and didn't throw an interception. Johnson caught three balls for 82 yards, Darius Cannon had four for 74, and we gained 479 yards. Brennan Core led the defense with seven tackles, and Myles Butler had a tackle and a half for loss. We had zero turnovers, and that's how you keep a fire clean.

We are 7-2, 5-0 in Conference USA and 5-0 at home. Next Saturday, Nov. 14, we go to Western Kentucky at Houchens Industries-L.T. Smith Stadium. I'll pack a cooler of pulled pork for the road, because Bowling Green is a long drive on an empty stomach. Cocky reigns, and the pit stays lit.

articles.title: Sam Houston vs Jacksonville State: Bearkats Fall on the Road 47-14
articles.matchup: Final: Jacksonville State (7-2) 47, Sam Houston (1-8) 14, Sat., Nov. 7, AmFirst Stadium, Jacksonville. Next: vs. Kennesaw State, Sat., Nov. 14, Elliott T. Bowers Stadium, Huntsville
articles.text:
Jacksonville State 47, Sam Houston 14, and class, take out your notebooks, because some lessons hurt. On Saturday morning, a blacksmith was working the fire at Joshua's Forge on the grounds of the Sam Houston Memorial Museum, showing folks how raw iron gets hammered into something useful. Our Bearkats spent Saturday night in Alabama on the anvil side of that demonstration.

Here's the part historians will skip past. It was scoreless after one quarter, and I had my chalk ready for a different kind of story. Then the Gamecocks scored 17 in the second quarter, and Caden Creel hit a 67-yard touchdown on their first drive of the third.

Now here's the chapter I'll read aloud. Thirty-seven seconds of game clock later, Landyn Locke found Chris Reed for a 64-yard touchdown. Sam Houston, on the board, 24-7. I underlined that sentence twice in red, the way I do for the dates students need to remember. Locke completed 16 of 21 for 126 yards and that touchdown, and Reed finished with six catches for 80 yards.

The fourth quarter got away from us fast. Jacksonville State scored on a Creel run, sacked Locke in the end zone for a safety, and then returned the free kick 85 yards. Three scores in about two minutes of game clock. DJ Bailey came in and threw a 7-yard touchdown to Grady O'Neill, who caught six balls for 61 yards. Landan Brown ran for 50 yards on 10 carries, and Jace Arnold had a sack.

The record book will show zero turnovers, and it will also show 10 penalties for 101 yards and one conversion on 11 third downs. Every era has its hard winters. We are 1-8 and 0-5 in Conference USA, and Kennesaw State comes to Elliott T. Bowers Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 14. History is long, Bearkats, and it is still being written.

I underlined that sentence twice in red, the way I do for the dates students need to remember. Locke completed 16 of 21 for 126 yards and that touchdown, and Reed finished with six catches for 80 yards.

The fourth quarter got away from us fast. Jacksonville State scored on a Creel run, sacked Locke in the end zone for a safety, and then returned the free kick 85 yards. Three scores in about two minutes of game clock. DJ Bailey came in and threw a 7-yard touchdown to Grady O'Neill, who caught six balls for 61 yards. Landan Brown ran for 50 yards on 10 carries, and Jace Arnold had a sack.

The record book will show zero turnovers, and it will also show 10 penalties for 101 yards and one conversion on 11 third downs. Every era has its hard winters. We are 1-8 and 0-5 in Conference USA, and Kennesaw State comes to Elliott T. Bowers Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 14. History is long, Bearkats, and it is still being written.

Landyn Locke threw a 64-yard touchdown to Chris Reed, who had six catches for 80 yards.
DJ Bailey threw a 7-yard touchdown to Grady O'Neill in the fourth quarter. Sam Houston had no turnovers.
Scoreless after one. Somebody frame that first quarter for the museum.

articles.title: Coastal Carolina vs Old Dominion: Turnovers Sink Homecoming 8-21
articles.matchup: Final: Old Dominion Monarchs (3-7) 21, Coastal Carolina Chanticleers (3-6) 8, Sat., Nov. 7, Brooks Stadium, Conway. Next: vs Arkansas State, Sat., Nov. 14, 1:00 PM ET, Brooks Stadium, Conway
articles.text:
Coastal Carolina Chanticleers 8, Old Dominion Monarchs 21. Final score 21-8 at Brooks Stadium, and Homecoming in Conway went out with the tide. Three and six. Two and three in the Sun Belt. Six turnovers on your own field, in front of 16,092 who came home for the weekend, makes for a hard afternoon to write about. I will do it anyway, because that is the job.

Low tide notes, first quarter: Deuce Bailey lost a fumble, and Mario Thompson took it 42 yards for a touchdown just 37 seconds after Old Dominion's first score. Late in the half another fumble went the wrong way at our 6, and the Monarchs scored on the next snap. Fourteen of their 21 points came off our mistakes. Nico Cavanillas Alti did his part, hitting from 30 and from 44 as the half expired, and it was 21-6 at the break.

Then the tide came back in for our defense. Old Dominion did not score again. Marcellius Pulliam made 22 tackles, which is not a typo, and he and Nolan Korzeniowski tackled Maurki James in the end zone for a safety in the fourth quarter. Jesse Powell II added 11 tackles. Xzavier Booker had eight with a sack and three tackles for loss. We held the Monarchs to 69 rushing yards and 264 in all, and Roland Podesta averaged 46.6 a punt.

The offense never found its current. We drove 86 yards in the third quarter and Ja'Mez Drummer intercepted us at the 1. Ja'Marion Wayne gave us life with a 35-yard interception return to the Old Dominion 14 with 7:51 left, and we came up empty on downs. Four interceptions in all, three in the fourth quarter. Twenty rushing yards. Two of 15 on third down. Bailey threw for 233, and Karmello English caught five for 57.

Arkansas State comes to Brooks Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 14, at 1 PM ET for the home finale. One more Saturday on the teal turf. Let's make the last one sing. Teal forever.

articles.title: Old Dominion vs Coastal Carolina: Six Takeaways, Skid Ends 21-8
articles.matchup: Final: Old Dominion Monarchs (3-7) 21, Coastal Carolina Chanticleers (3-6) 8, Sat., Nov. 7, Brooks Stadium, Conway. Next: at UConn, Sat., Nov. 21, 3:30 PM ET, Pratt & Whitney Stadium, East Hartford
articles.text:
Hear ye, hear ye: Old Dominion Monarchs 21, Coastal Carolina Chanticleers 8. Final score 21-8 at Brooks Stadium in Conway, and the three-game losing streak has been formally banished from the realm. Three and seven. Two and five in the Sun Belt. We crashed their Homecoming and walked out with six takeaways in the royal treasury.

Back home in Norfolk on Saturday night, the Barry Art Museum's Helios festival lit up 43rd Street with Luke Jerram's giant inflatable Sun, lit from the inside, after Friday's night got washed out by weather. A fitting backdrop. Our defense was the brightest light in two states.

The coronation came early. Quinn Henicle ran in from 2 with 5:05 left in the first quarter, and 37 seconds later Mario Thompson scooped up a Deuce Bailey fumble and carried it 42 yards for a 14-0 lead. With 27 seconds left in the half, we recovered another fumble at the Coastal 6, and on the very next snap Jaxon Potter found Leon Haughton Jr. for a touchdown. Twenty-one points, and two of those touchdowns came gift-wrapped.

Then the second half belonged to the secondary. Four interceptions after the break, from four different Monarchs: Ja'Mez Drummer, Zion Frink, Brandon Crutchfield and Tavares Murray Jr. Drummer's came at our 1 to end an 86-yard Coastal march, and he added two sacks for good measure. Knight him. Ian Brandt punted eight times and dropped four inside the 20, and we held the ball for the final 7:34.

Honest court record: we were blanked in the second half, ran for just 69 yards on 35 carries, and took a safety early in the fourth after an interception left us pinned deep. Potter went 17 of 30 for 150. Haughton caught six for 67, and Josh Rodriguez caught six for 53. Coastal held us to 264 yards. Defense won this one, and the crown fits it.

Now an open week to rest, then a trip north to UConn on Saturday, Nov. 21, at 3:30 PM ET. Polish the crown. Long live the Monarchs.

articles.title: Mississippi State vs Vanderbilt: Homecoming Rally Falls Short 25-23
articles.matchup: Final: Vanderbilt (4-5) 25, Mississippi State (4-5) 23, Sat., Nov. 7, Davis Wade Stadium, Starkville. Next: vs. Auburn, Sat., Nov. 14, Davis Wade Stadium, Starkville
articles.text:
Vanderbilt 25, Mississippi State 23, on Homecoming, and the sock is on the cowbell. The whole week was "There's No Place Like State," from the True Maroon Trek through campus to Will Clark and Rafael Palmeiro running teams at the Diamond Dawg Classic on Friday night. Davis Wade Stadium was packed with 48,904 people in maroon on Saturday. We just couldn't give them the ending.

I keep my feed-store receipts, and the first half reads like a bad month. Vanderbilt held the ball for an 18-play drive, kicked three field goals and led 16-0 at halftime. We didn't make a first down on four straight drives in the first half, and AJ Swann was intercepted before the break.

Then the barn caught fire in a good way. Swann hit Sanfrisco Magee for a 65-yard touchdown on our first drive of the third quarter, and on the very next Vanderbilt possession, Tyshun Willis sacked Jared Curtis, knocked the ball loose, and Will Whitson scooped it up and scored from 14 yards. Two touchdowns in 52 seconds, and it was 16-14. Every cowbell in the place was ringing.

But their kicker never missed. Brock Taylor went 6 for 6, including a 55-yarder with 1:46 left that made it 25-17. We had already gotten to their 8 and settled for Kyle Ferrie's 26-yard field goal. Swann drove us down and hit Magee for 30 yards with 32 seconds left. The two-point try failed, and Vanderbilt got the onside kick.

Swann completed 23 of 36 for 254 yards and two touchdowns, and Magee caught two balls for 95 yards and both scores. Jardin Gilbert made 13 tackles, and Fatt Forrest had 11 with two tackles for loss. We are 4-5 and 2-5 in the SEC. Auburn comes to Davis Wade Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 14. I'm taking the sock off for that one.

articles.title: Vanderbilt vs Mississippi State: Taylor Kicks Six in 25-23 Win
articles.matchup: Final: Vanderbilt (4-5) 25, Mississippi State (4-5) 23, Sat., Nov. 7, Davis Wade Stadium, Starkville. Next: vs. Alabama, Sat., Nov. 14, FirstBank Stadium, Nashville
articles.text:
Vanderbilt 25, Mississippi State 23, and somebody hand me my guitar, because this song just went up a key. While the Nashville Farmers' Market threw its 28th Turnip Green Festival on Saturday morning, with Smiley's cast iron cauldron of braised greens and catfish and cornbread plates, the Commodores went down to Mississippi and brought home the first SEC win of the year.

Verse one was all Brock Taylor. He kicked a 38-yarder in the first quarter, and then we put together an 18-play, 87-yard drive that ate 10 minutes and 19 seconds, finished by Sedrick Alexander on a 2-yard run. Jordan Matthews intercepted AJ Swann with 1:25 left in the half, and Taylor kicked two more. Up 16-0 at halftime. I was humming.

Then the bridge got rough. The Bulldogs hit a 65-yard touchdown, and 52 seconds later Jared Curtis got sacked and fumbled, and they ran it back for a score. Sixteen to 14. My heart did a little breakup ballad. But Taylor came back out and kicked from 54, then from 34, then from 55 with 1:46 left. Six field goals, six makes, 19 points. Somebody write that man a song. I'm volunteering.

State scored with 32 seconds left to pull within two, but the two-point try failed, and we recovered the onside kick to end it. Curtis completed 17 of 27 for 168 yards, Makhilyn Young ran for 63 and Alexander for 59, and we held the ball for 39 minutes and 55 seconds. Issa Ouattara had two sacks, and Mason Lewis made 10 tackles.

That snaps a five-game losing streak. The AP says it's our first win against Mississippi State since 2004 and our first win on their home field since 1971. We are 4-5 and 1-5 in the SEC, and Alabama comes to FirstBank Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 14. Final chorus, all together now.

articles.title: North Texas vs Rice: Six Straight, Mean Green Roll 52-23
articles.matchup: Final: North Texas Mean Green (7-2) 52, Rice Owls (1-8) 23, Sat., Nov. 7, DATCU Stadium, Denton. Next: at UTSA, Sat., Nov. 14, 9:00 PM ET, Alamodome, San Antonio
articles.text:
North Texas 52, Rice 23, and that's six straight wins, Mean Green. Six! The record is spinning and nobody's lifting the needle. Denton had a full Saturday, too: the UNT College of Music had its Afro-Cuban, Brazilian and Latin Jazz Concert at Voertman Concert Hall at 6:30 that night. Somewhere in that building, a drummer was playing in a meter almost as tricky as our second half.

Because the first half was a slow intro. Dominic De Freitas opened with a 37-yard field goal, Jahiem White scored from 3, and Rice had us at 10-7 at the break. Then they even took a run at us. Tyvonn Byars scored, and it was 17-14 midway through the third quarter.

And then the band kicked in. North Texas scored a touchdown on all six of its second-half possessions. White scored from a yard for 24-14. On the very next snap, Zakye Barker forced a fumble and Bryce Garza fell on it at the Rice 31. Five plays later, Tayven Jackson hit Dalton Carnes for 19 yards and a touchdown. Then White went 60 yards to the end zone on the first play of the fourth quarter. That's the hook you hum all week.

The liner notes: White ran 21 times for 139 yards and three touchdowns. Jackson threw for 303 yards and also ran in two scores. Justin Stevenson caught five balls for 117 yards, Max Reese had 72 and Baron Tipton 52. Brendon Haygood added a 4-yard score late, and De Freitas went seven for seven on kicks after touchdowns.

Barker led the defense with 10 tackles, Brandon Jones had eight, and Peyton Taylor came up with an interception and a 41-yard return. Rice did run for 261 yards, so the rhythm section has some rehearsing to do. Fair enough. We still never gave the ball away.

We're 7-2, 5-0 at home and 5-0 in the American, a game clear of Memphis and UTSA. Next is the road gig of the season: at UTSA, Saturday, Nov. 14, at 9 PM ET at the Alamodome in San Antonio. Turn it up.

articles.title: Rice vs North Texas: Owls Hang Around, Fall 23-52
articles.matchup: Final: North Texas Mean Green (7-2) 52, Rice Owls (1-8) 23, Sat., Nov. 7, DATCU Stadium, Denton. Next: vs. Tulane, Sat., Nov. 14, 2:00 PM ET, Houston
articles.text:
North Texas 52, Rice 23. Owl family, this is a result I have to report honestly, even though my heart wants a second trial. Before kickoff in Denton, Rice Engineers Without Borders ran a soccer shootout on Intramural Field 6, where every goal unlocked sponsor money for a bridge the students designed for Prado, Peru. Engineers building bridges on a Saturday morning. That's the Rice I'd put in any brochure.

Now the methods section. For a half, our hypothesis held up. We trailed only 10-7 at the break after Gael Ochoa dropped a 36-yard touchdown throw to Will Swartz. Then Tyvonn Byars punched in a 2-yard run in the third quarter, and it was 17-14 with 8:42 left in the period. I was on my feet. Statistically on my feet, anyway.

The data turned fast. Jahiem White scored from a yard, and on the very next snap we fumbled at our own 31. Five plays later it was a 17-point game. North Texas scored a touchdown on all six of its second-half possessions, and White finished with 139 rushing yards and three scores.

Here's my control group of good news, and it's not small. We ran for 261 yards at 5.4 a carry and held the ball for 32:10. D'Andre Hardeman Jr. ripped off a 56-yard run and finished with 73 yards on seven carries. Ochoa threw for 172 yards on only 13 attempts. Tommy Bauchiero hit a 30-yard field goal, and Patrick Crayton Jr. scored on a 7-yard run on the final play, because Owls do not quit early. AJ Brown led us with six tackles and Koa Akui got a sack.

The sample that hurts: two turnovers to their zero, and a Mean Green offense that went for 495 yards. N is too small to panic, I keep telling myself. Then I panic quietly anyway.

We're 1-8 and 0-5 in the American. Tulane visits Houston on Saturday, Nov. 14, at 2 PM ET. Fresh trial, fresh hypothesis. Go Owls.

articles.title: Georgia Southern vs Marshall: Johnson's Five Scores Roll 49-13
articles.matchup: Final: Georgia Southern Eagles (5-4) 49, Marshall Thundering Herd (5-4) 13, Sat., Nov. 7, Allen E. Paulson Stadium, Statesboro. Next: at Georgia State, Sat., Nov. 14, 3:30 PM ET, Center Parc Stadium, Atlanta
articles.text:
Georgia Southern 49, Marshall 13, and Hail Southern, that one was a creek-side feast. It was the Eagles' Military Appreciation Game, and Operation Teammate brought about 30 military-connected kids and their families out for a VIP tailgate, the Eagle Walk and a halftime salute. Those kids got a show. 24,023 of us at Paulson Stadium got one too.

Max Johnson was the whole harvest. He went 19 of 26 for 271 yards and four touchdowns with no interceptions, and ran 16 yards for a fifth score. He hit Jeremiah Ware for 23 yards to open it, and seven seconds later Chace Calicut stepped in front of a Marshall throw and ran it back 24 yards. 14-0 in the blink of an eye.

Marshall answered with a 45-yard run, and then Johnson found Alex Taylor for a 70-yard catch-and-run, a one-play drive, for 21-7 at the half. After a punt on the first possession of the third quarter, the Eagles scored on four straight drives: Andre Greene Jr. from a yard, Ware from 45, Johnson on his own 16-yard run, and Ty Cummings from 16. Ware and Taylor each finished with 94 receiving yards.

On defense, Brandon Tyson made nine tackles and Ethan Johnson six. We intercepted two throws. The Herd did run for 250 yards, and that is honest film we'll be watching with the lights on this week. But Marshall went 4 of 13 on third down, and we never coughed it up once.

Josh Dallas brought back six punts for 91 yards, Alex Smith averaged 46.8 on his punts, and Tripp Bryant went seven for seven on extra points. Granddad would have called that a full day's work before supper.

We're 5-4 and 4-1 in the Sun Belt, and the East race is right there in front of us. Next is a trip up I-16 to Georgia State on Saturday, Nov. 14, at 3:30 PM ET at Center Parc Stadium in Atlanta. Hail Southern.

articles.title: Marshall vs Georgia Southern: Herd Run Hard, Fall 13-49
articles.matchup: Final: Georgia Southern Eagles (5-4) 49, Marshall Thundering Herd (5-4) 13, Sat., Nov. 7, Allen E. Paulson Stadium, Statesboro. Next: vs. App State, Sat., Nov. 14, 6:00 PM ET, Joan C. Edwards Stadium, Huntington
articles.text:
Georgia Southern 49, Marshall 13. Friends, I'll give it to you straight, the way I'd give it to a patient's family: this one was rough from early on. Back home, the November First Saturday Art Market filled the old factory on Vernon Street with Appalachian makers from 11 to 4, and I'd have traded my seat in Statesboro for a zine workshop by the second quarter.

The turn came in seven seconds. Georgia Southern scored on a 23-yard throw with 3:11 left in the first quarter, and on our first snap after the kickoff a Zion Turner throw was intercepted and returned 24 yards for another touchdown. Down 14-0 that fast. Our answer came right back, and it was a beauty: Jo'Shon Barbie took a handoff 45 yards to the end zone. 14-7. That's the Herd I know.

Then Max Johnson found Alex Taylor for 70 yards on a one-play drive in the second quarter, and the Eagles opened the second half by scoring on four straight possessions. Johnson finished with four touchdown throws and ran for another. Jeremiah Ware and Taylor each had 94 receiving yards.

The parts I'll hold onto: we ran for 250 yards at 6.4 a carry. Barbie went for 83 on 12 carries. Khalil Wilkins broke a 66-yard touchdown run late and completed both of his throws. We put up 412 yards, Owen Sweeney caught four balls for 46, and Cooper Heimbach punted seven times for a 45.4 average without a single complaint. Jalen Marshall made seven tackles and Javae Gilmore six.

The parts that sting: 4 of 13 on third down, two interceptions, and a Georgia Southern offense that went 21 of 30 through the air. Turner finished 11 of 26 for 141 yards. That isn't a knock on any young man in green. It's just the truth on the chart, and the truth is how we heal.

We're 5-4 and 2-3 in the Sun Belt. App State comes to Joan C. Edwards Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 14, at 6 PM ET, and Huntington will be ready to hold this team close. We Are... and always will be.

articles.title: San José State vs Northern Illinois: Spartans Ship It 30-19
articles.matchup: Final: San José State (5-5) 30, Northern Illinois (0-9) 19, Sat., Nov. 7, CEFCU Stadium, San Jose. Next: at Air Force, Sat., Nov. 14, Falcon Stadium, USAF Academy
articles.text:
San José State 30, Northern Illinois 19, and I am pushing this one to production with a smile. It was Parent and Family Weekend at CEFCU Stadium, with a Military and First Responders Salute to Service on the schedule, and the Spartans gave the moms and dads a clean build to take home. Nine thousand, seven hundred and eighty-six people showed up, and every one of them got a working product.

The first commit was Viliami Teu on a 5-yard touchdown run. Trajan Sinatra kicked field goals from 25 and 46 yards, and we led 13-0. The Huskies found two bugs in the second quarter and tied it 13-13, so Sinatra patched it with a 22-yarder, his third field goal, and Dylan Lee intercepted Taron Dickens before halftime. Merge approved, 16-13.

Then the release went out. Caleb Womack recovered a muffed punt at the Northern Illinois 18, and Teu scored from a yard out. A few minutes later the Huskies tried a fake punt at their own 29, our defense stuffed it, and Daniel Rolovich hit Dominique McKenzie for a 29-yard touchdown on the very next play. That made it 30-13, and I opened a celebratory bag of chips at my desk.

Rolovich completed 16 of 27 for 231 yards with no interceptions. McKenzie caught two balls for 71 yards, Anthony Ivey had a 49-yard catch, and Carson Clark caught six. Teu ground out 42 yards on 17 carries with his two scores. The defense was the real uptime story: Tuli Tagovailoa-Amosa made 11 tackles, Womack and Lee had 10 each, and the Huskies went 0-4 on fourth down, including a stop at our own 8 to end the third quarter.

That snaps a two-game skid. We are 5-5 and 3-3 in the Mountain West, one win from bowl eligibility. Next Saturday, Nov. 14, we go to Air Force at Falcon Stadium. Ship it to prod, Spartans. No rollback tonight.

articles.title: Northern Illinois vs San José State: Huskies Fall Short 30-19
articles.matchup: Final: San José State (5-5) 30, Northern Illinois (0-9) 19, Sat., Nov. 7, CEFCU Stadium, San Jose. Next: vs. Nevada, Sat., Nov. 14, Huskie Stadium, DeKalb
articles.text:
San José State 30, Northern Illinois 19, and the cornfield photo is back on the kitchen table where I can look at it. Back home on Saturday afternoon, DeKalb walked in the Day of the Dead procession from El Jimador to the public library, and Banda NIU played the after-hours concert in the lobby. Our town knows how to honor what's gone. I'd just like to stop practicing on football seasons.

It looked like a crop for a while. Down 13-0 in the second quarter, Telly Johnson Jr. ran 4 yards for a touchdown, and Taron Dickens found Zaire McKinney for 19 yards to tie it 13-13 with 3:25 left in the half. Then the Spartans kicked a field goal, and Dickens was intercepted before the break. Still, three points down at halftime on the road. I had my boots on.

The third quarter is where the hail came. DeAree Rogers muffed a punt at our 24, San José State scored a few plays later, and then our fake punt at our own 29 came up short and the Spartans hit a 29-yard touchdown on the very next snap. That's 14 points in about three and a half minutes, and it was 30-13.

I will give the boys this: they never quit. We outgained the Spartans 400 yards to 316, and Elijah Porter ran for 79 yards on 12 carries. Dickens completed 26 of 36 and ran in a 1-yard touchdown with 3:55 left. Jack Murray made nine tackles and Kole Sneed had two and a half tackles for loss. But we went 0-4 on fourth down, and the Spartans stopped us at their own 8 to end the third quarter.

We are 0-9 and 0-5 in the Mountain West, and the AP says we have lost 11 straight going back to last season. Nevada comes to Huskie Stadium next Saturday, Nov. 14. Every farmer has a dry year. You still plant in the spring.

articles.title: Purdue vs Maryland: Five Field Goals, No Homecoming Win, 29-34
articles.matchup: Final: Maryland Terrapins (3-6) 34, Purdue Boilermakers (3-6) 29, Sat., Nov. 7, Ross-Ade Stadium, West Lafayette. Next: at Iowa, Sat., Nov. 14, 7:30 PM ET, Kinnick Stadium, Iowa City
articles.text:
Purdue Boilermakers 29, Maryland Terrapins 34. Final score 34-29 at Ross-Ade Stadium on our 104th Homecoming, and the blueprint had a crack in it right down the middle. Three and six. Two and four in the Big Ten. Third straight loss. David Bell, our 2021 All-American receiver, was back as honorary captain, and 51,929 came home to see a win that never got built.

The first half went almost to spec. Jacobo Echeverria Lozano hit from 47, 26, 24 and 36, and we led 12-7 at the half while holding Maryland to 108 first-half yards, per the AP. Later he added a 22-yarder, five for five on the day, and that gave him 21 field goals this season, a school record for a freshman by five, per the AP. The kid is a precision instrument.

Here is the engineering failure report. Four red zone trips ended in field goals, per the AP. One of them came after a bad snap on third-and-goal inside the Maryland 1. Ryan Browne fumbled at our own 2 in the third quarter, and four plays later Maryland was in the end zone. Xavier Townsend ripped off a 30-yard touchdown run to pull us to 21-19, and on the very next snap DeJuan Williams went 75 the other way. Then Chris Durr Jr. broke a tackle at the 11 and ran 87 yards. Three Maryland touchdowns of 44 yards or longer.

Browne threw for 296 yards on 24 of 38. Tra'Mar Harris caught three for 76. Antonio Harris ran for 51 on five carries. Fame Ijeboi punched in from 2 with 3:50 left to make it 34-29, and we got the ball back and reached the Maryland 11 with five seconds to go. The last play was a sack. Jojo Hayden led us with eight tackles, Trey Smith intercepted Malik Washington, and CJ Madden got a sack. We had 26 first downs to their 12 and two penalties all day. The numbers say we built the better machine. The scoreboard says otherwise.

Next up: Iowa, Saturday, Nov. 14, at 7:30 PM ET at Kinnick Stadium. Back to the drafting table. Boiler up.
