articles.title: Maryland vs Purdue: Washington's Brace, Skid Snapped, 34-29
articles.matchup: Final: Maryland Terrapins (3-6) 34, Purdue Boilermakers (3-6) 29, Sat., Nov. 7, Ross-Ade Stadium, West Lafayette. Next: vs Wisconsin, Sat., Nov. 14, 12:00 PM ET, SECU Stadium, College Park
articles.text:
Maryland Terrapins 34, Purdue Boilermakers 29. Final score 34-29 at Ross-Ade Stadium, and somebody hand me the Old Bay, because the six-game losing streak is finished and so is the 13-game Big Ten skid. Three and six. One and five in the league. The players stormed the field and gave interim coach Aazaar Abdul-Rahim a Gatorade bath, then carried him off on their shoulders. I may have cried into a crab mallet.

Back in College Park on Saturday night, the UMD Wind Orchestra played Parody and Parity at the Clarice, and the program included Ernst Krenek's Three Merry Marches. Fitting, because our third quarter was three merry marches of its own. Malik Washington hit Na'eem Abdul-Rahim Gladding on a screen that went 44 yards for a 14-12 lead. Four plays after Purdue fumbled at its own 2, Washington plunged in from a yard out. Then, right after a Purdue score, DeJuan Williams scooted 75 yards to make it 28-19.

The first half was a crab with no meat: five first downs and 108 yards, per the AP, and we trailed 12-7 at the break, with Washington's 15-yard touchdown run our only score. Whatever got said in that locker room, I want it bottled and sold at every seafood shack on Route 1.

Washington was the story. He wore a brace on his left knee all second half and still went 13 of 18 for 253 yards, two touchdown throws, two touchdown runs. The dagger came early in the fourth: Chris Durr Jr. caught a short one at the 11, broke a tackle, ran across the whole field and went 87 yards for a 34-22 lead. Durr finished with four catches for 127. Williams ran for 99 on 14 carries.

The defense bent but held the door. Nahsir Taylor made 11 tackles with a sack and two and a half tackles for loss, and Lavain Scruggs got a sack too. Purdue reached our 11 with five seconds left, and the final play was a sack of Ryan Browne. Honest note: nine penalties for 107 yards is not seasoning anybody wants.

Wisconsin comes to SECU Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 14, at noon ET. Bring the crabs, bring the noise, and let's make it two in a row. Fear the Turtle.

articles.title: Middle Tennessee vs Western Kentucky: Homecoming Thriller 51-42
articles.matchup: Final: Middle Tennessee (5-4) 51, Western Kentucky (3-6) 42, Sat., Nov. 7, Johnny "Red" Floyd Stadium, Murfreesboro. Next: at Liberty, Sat., Nov. 14, Williams Stadium (VA), Lynchburg
articles.text:
Middle Tennessee 51, Western Kentucky 42, on Homecoming in Murfreesboro, and I'm going to need a second pan of biscuits. Our alumni came home to Floyd Stadium, the youth sports teams got their moment on the video board, and the Blue Raiders gave everybody a finish that will be told at every Thanksgiving table in Rutherford County.

We started like a hot oven. Roman Gagliano threw a 25-yard touchdown to Neo Clifton, then found Ziyon Butler for 65 yards a minute later, and it was 14-0. Western Kentucky clawed back to 14-13, so Gagliano hit Clifton again from a yard out with 29 seconds left in the half. On the first snap of the third, Antonio Martin ran 75 yards for a touchdown. Sit down, I'm not done.

Martin added a 2-yard score and finished with 125 rushing yards on 16 carries. Gagliano completed 30 of 41 for 312 yards and four touchdowns, the last a 4-yarder to Koraun Perdue for a 42-27 lead early in the fourth. Butler caught six balls for 129 yards, and Cam'ron Lacy caught nine. Korey Smith led the defense with seven tackles, and Zeion Simpson-Smith got a sack.

Then the Hilltoppers scored 15 straight and tied it 42-42 with 31 seconds left. I put my hand on my heart. Gagliano did not blink. articles.title: Western Kentucky vs Middle Tennessee: Tops Fall at Buzzer, 51-42
articles.matchup: Final: Middle Tennessee (5-4) 51, Western Kentucky (3-6) 42, Sat., Nov. 7, Johnny "Red" Floyd Stadium, Murfreesboro. Next: vs. Jacksonville State, Sat., Nov. 14, Houchens Industries-L.T. Smith Stadium, Bowling Green
articles.text:
Middle Tennessee 51, Western Kentucky 42, and I have had to set the clippers down twice just to catch my breath. While the Kentucky Museum on our campus threw Sonic Fest on Saturday afternoon, with Government Cheese and Tommy Womack celebrating a year of the Sonic Landscape exhibit, our Hilltoppers were 100 miles down the road writing a song nobody in Bowling Green wanted to hear the last verse of.

Pull up a chair, this one needs a long haircut. We fell behind 14-0 in the first quarter after two quick Roman Gagliano touchdown throws. Then the Tops started trimming. Karl Campbell kicked a 35-yarder, Brock Glenn ran one in from 2, and Campbell hit from 42. We trailed 21-13 at the half, and Glenn found Moussa Barry for 21 yards in the third to cut it to 28-20.

Ajay Allen was the best thing in the shop all day: 116 yards on 15 carries and an 8-yard touchdown run. Jonathan Stafford Jr. caught eight balls for 90 yards. Jaylen Wester made 13 tackles and got a sack. We ran for 238 yards as a team and gained 497 in all.

Down 42-27 in the fourth, Rodney Tisdale Jr. came in and nearly wrote a legend. He hit Quincy Burroughs for an 8-yard touchdown, threw the two-point try to Lofton Howard, and then ran 5 yards for the tying score with 31 seconds left. Forty-two all. Every chair in the shop would have spun.

Then 30 seconds was too much time. Middle Tennessee moved into range, Dominic Bourgeois hit a 48-yarder with 1 second left, and our lateral try on the kickoff ended with the ball bouncing loose and a Blue Raider running it in. That ended our seven-game winning streak in this rivalry.

We are 3-6 and 2-3 in Conference USA. Jacksonville State comes to Houchens Industries-L.T. Smith Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 14. Stand up and cheer anyway, Tops. The next customer is already in the chair.

articles.title: UConn vs North Carolina: Three Turnovers Sink the Huskies, 21-38
articles.matchup: Final: North Carolina Tar Heels (5-4) 38, UConn Huskies (4-5) 21, Sat., Nov. 7, Pratt & Whitney Stadium, East Hartford. Next: vs James Madison, Sat., Nov. 14, 12:00 PM ET, Pratt & Whitney Stadium, East Hartford
articles.text:
UConn Huskies 21, North Carolina Tar Heels 38. Final score 38-21 at the Rent, and I am counting possessions again, because three of them got away from us and became 21 Carolina points. Four and five now. Two and three at home.

Down on Main Street in Hartford on Saturday, the Butler-McCook House opened its doors for its last Open Tour Day of the year, Fighting McCooks and Veterans' Day, a salute to the family's veterans ahead of Nov. 11. Fighting is the right word for our guys, too. They never quit. They just kept handing the ball across the floor.

First quarter, Kalieb Osborne threw one that Timir Hickman-Collins took back 62 yards for a touchdown. In the second quarter, Osborne lost a fumble that became a 6-yard Tar Heel score. In the fourth, Jalon Thompson intercepted him and Carolina cashed that one too. You do not beat an ACC team giving up three turnovers. You barely beat anybody.

And we had our chances. Osborne found Ryder Treadway from 18 to tie it 7-7, then hit Cam Abshire from 24 to make it 21-14. Down 28-14 at the half, Osborne ripped off completions of 23 and 28 yards and a 25-yard run to set up Cyncir Bowers' 13-yard touchdown, and it was 28-21 with 10 minutes left in the third. The Rent got loud. Then Rece Verhoff's field goal pushed it back to 10, and we went 1 for 4 on fourth down. Treadway caught four balls for 82. Bowers ran for 68 on 13 carries.

Hayden Pegg was a one-man press defense: 12 tackles and an interception. K'Von Sherman added 11 tackles, and John Lista had 10. Esean Carter got home for a sack. Jack O'Connor missed his only field goal try. Billy Edwards Jr. completed 29 of 38 against us, and Carolina held the ball for more than 36 minutes, which is a lot of possessions to defend.

James Madison comes to the Rent on Saturday, Nov. 14, at noon ET, the second of three straight at home. Next play, next possession. Protect the ball, and Pack the Rent.

articles.title: North Carolina vs UConn: Takeaways Fuel a 38-21 Road Win
articles.matchup: Final: North Carolina Tar Heels (5-4) 38, UConn Huskies (4-5) 21, Sat., Nov. 7, Pratt & Whitney Stadium, East Hartford. Next: vs Louisville, Sat., Nov. 14, Kenan Stadium, Chapel Hill
articles.text:
North Carolina Tar Heels 38, UConn Huskies 21. Final score 38-21 in East Hartford, and the two-game losing streak is gone. Five and four. Three and one on the road. And yes, Bill Belichick coached his first game back in New England since the Patriots, and the Tar Heels sent him home with a win.

Back in Chapel Hill on Saturday, Festifall turned 53 with its arts market at 100 East Rosemary Street downtown, pottery and paintings and woodwork from all around the Triangle. Very nice. But the finest handiwork of the day was done in Connecticut, by our secondary.

Timir Hickman-Collins opened the scoring, reading Kalieb Osborne and taking an interception 62 yards to the house for a 7-0 lead. Later he fell on a Husky fumble, and Billy Edwards Jr. cashed it with a 6-yard touchdown throw to Jordan Shipp. Jalon Thompson grabbed the third takeaway in the fourth quarter, and Edwards turned that one into a 3-yard score to Jelani Thurman with 3:38 left. Three turnovers, 21 points. As a kinesiologist, I can tell you that is what force production looks like in a defensive back.

Edwards was sharp all afternoon, 29 of 38 for 255 yards and three touchdowns. Thurman caught seven balls for 64 and both of his scores came from 3 yards out, the first with 24 seconds left in the half for a 28-14 lead. That gives him eight touchdown catches this season, tying the school record for a tight end, per the AP. Benjamin Hall ripped off a 39-yard touchdown run and finished with 81 yards on nine carries. We went 9 of 16 on third down and 2 for 2 on fourth.

Peyton Seelmann was everywhere: nine tackles, two sacks, three throws broken up. Rece Verhoff hit from 27 and was perfect on extras. Not a perfect day, mind you. Edwards threw one interception, and UConn cut it to 28-21 in the third before we closed the door.

Louisville comes to Kenan Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 14, kickoff time still to be set. Somewhere eight miles down the road, a certain school is not having this much fun. Go Heels.

articles.title: Washington vs Penn State: 19-Point Rally Falls Short 25-28
articles.matchup: Final: Penn State Nittany Lions (5-4) 28, Washington Huskies (5-4) 25, Sat., Nov. 7, Husky Stadium, Seattle. Next: at Michigan State, Sat., Nov. 14, 4:15 PM ET, Spartan Stadium, East Lansing
articles.text:
Penn State 28, Washington 25. Homecoming at Husky Stadium, 67,879 in purple, and the Nittany Lions back in Seattle for the first time since 1921, when this place was one year old and we were still called the Sundodgers. We rowed hard all afternoon. We just spent the first half facing the wrong way.

Tyler Robles opened the scoring with a 29-yard field goal. Then Penn State scored four straight touchdowns, 21 points in the second quarter alone, and we went to the locker room down 28-6. Carson Hansen ran for 119 yards, Chase Sowell caught four balls for 125, and the Lions turned that half into choppy water.

But this crew does not quit pulling. Robles hit from 47 in the third, three for three on the day. Demond Williams Jr. found Chris Lawson for 39 yards, then Baron Naone from 4, and Williams threw the two-point try to Rashid Williams. After an interception slowed us down, our defense forced a punt, Williams ran 23 yards, hit Lawson for 21 more and found Dezmen Roebuck from 6. Naone caught the second two-point try. 19 straight points. 28-25 with 7:40 left, and the whole lake heard it.

Then Penn State took the ball and never gave it back. Fourteen plays, 70 yards, two kneel-downs at our 4. Jacob Lane and Isaiah Ward each sacked Becht during the day, but on that last drive we couldn't get the stop that would've handed Williams the oars one more time.

Honest notes from the boathouse: Williams went 19 of 33 for 172 yards with two touchdowns and an interception and ran for 43. Lawson caught five for 89, and Jayden Limar ran for 66 on nine carries. Alex McLaughlin led us with seven tackles. Hunter Green averaged 48.5 yards on four punts. Penn State never coughed it up, and we went 4 of 12 on third down.

We're 5-4 and 2-4 in the Big Ten. Next is a trip to Michigan State on Saturday, Nov. 14, at 4:15 PM ET at Spartan Stadium in East Lansing. Bow Down. We'll be back on the water Monday.

articles.title: Penn State vs Washington: Lions Hold On, Run Out Clock 28-25
articles.matchup: Final: Penn State Nittany Lions (5-4) 28, Washington Huskies (5-4) 25, Sat., Nov. 7, Husky Stadium, Seattle. Next: vs. Minnesota, Sat., Nov. 14, 7:00 PM ET, Beaver Stadium, University Park
articles.text:
Penn State 28, Washington 25. We Are... relieved. Back at University Park, the Penn State Jazz Festival had Centre Dimensions swinging in Recital Hall at 3 p.m., with high schoolers sitting in beside our ensemble. Out in Seattle, our Nittany Lions played a set with a great first half, a shaky bridge and a closing riff that held the last note for seven minutes and 40 seconds.

This was our first trip to Seattle since 1921, and the first half felt like we owned the place. Carson Hansen ran in from 12. Rocco Becht hit Zay Robinson for a 24-yard score, then Chase Sowell for 45. Cam Wallace bolted 46 yards for another. Twenty-one points in the second quarter, 28-6 at the half, and I was mentally ordering a double scoop at the Creamery.

Then Washington scored 19 straight. A field goal, a touchdown and two-point try, and another touchdown and two-point try with 7:40 left, and suddenly it was 28-25 on Homecoming in front of 67,879. Creamery ranking for the second-half defense: plain vanilla, slightly melted. Ibn McDaniels did intercept Demond Williams Jr. early in the fourth quarter, and that one mattered.

And then the drive. Fourteen plays, 70 yards, every remaining second off the clock. Becht took a knee at the Washington 4, twice, and the Huskies never touched the ball again. That's the setter in me talking: you don't need the kill when you can just keep the ball in your hands until the match ends.

Hansen finished with 119 yards on 14 carries. Becht went 16 of 27 for 240 yards and two touchdowns with no interceptions, and Sowell caught four balls for 125. Tony Rojas and Kooper Ebel each made eight tackles. We never coughed it up and held the ball for 31:14. The flavor of the day is cookies and cream: a little messy, still delicious.

We're 5-4 and 2-4 in the Big Ten. Minnesota comes to Beaver Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 14, at 7 PM ET. Bring the noise, bring a spoon. We Are.

articles.title: UAB vs Charlotte: Blazers Win Children's Harbor Game, 23-12
articles.matchup: Final: UAB (5-4) 23, Charlotte (1-8) 12, Sat., Nov. 7, Protective Stadium, Birmingham. Next: at Temple, Sat., Nov. 14, Lincoln Financial Field, Philadelphia
articles.text:
UAB 23, Charlotte 12, and forged, not given, folks. Saturday was the 10th annual Children's Harbor Game at Protective Stadium, and our Blazers wore gray jerseys with the names of 99 children served by Children's Harbor stitched across their backs. Kids Takeover filled Blazer Village with games and inflatables. Every one of those names went home a winner.

Act one was a hard watch, I'll be honest. Ryder Burton was intercepted three times, Rod Robinson II lost a fumble, and Charlotte kicked two field goals off those mistakes. We were tied 3-3 at the half only because Jonah Delange hit a 42-yarder with two seconds left. Down 6-3 in the third, this stage needed a new lead, and I mean that in every theater sense of the word.

Enter the defense. Marlin Dean sacked Conner Harrell three times. Tylin Jackson was in the backfield all day with half a sack, a tackle and a half for loss and three quarterback hurries. Jo'Tavion Pierce made eight tackles and Muaaz Byard seven. Charlotte ran 31 times for 59 yards, converted 4 of 17 third downs and finished with 234 yards. That is steel.

Then the final act. Delange tied it with a 46-yarder late in the third and put us ahead 9-6 with a 36-yarder to open the fourth. Ja'Vin Simpkins scored from a yard out with about eight minutes left and from 5 yards with 2:07 to go. Robinson ran 14 times for 101 yards. Bam McReynolds added 54, and EJ Reid caught five balls for 57. Delange went 3 for 3 and made both extra points.

That makes us 5-0 at home, which UAB has not done since 2019, plus 5-4 overall and 3-2 in the American. Next Saturday, Nov. 14, we head to Temple at Lincoln Financial Field. Curtain down on a good one. Take a bow, Blazers, and give those jerseys to the kids.

Down 6-3 in the third, this stage needed a new lead, and I mean that in every theater sense of the word.

Enter the defense. Marlin Dean sacked Conner Harrell three times. Tylin Jackson was in the backfield all day with half a sack, a tackle and a half for loss and three quarterback hurries. Jo'Tavion Pierce made eight tackles and Muaaz Byard seven. Charlotte ran 31 times for 59 yards, converted 4 of 17 third downs and finished with 234 yards. That is steel.

Then the final act. Delange tied it with a 46-yarder late in the third and put us ahead 9-6 with a 36-yarder to open the fourth. Ja'Vin Simpkins scored from a yard out with about eight minutes left and from 5 yards with 2:07 to go. Robinson ran 14 times for 101 yards. Bam McReynolds added 54, and EJ Reid caught five balls for 57. Delange went 3 for 3 and made both extra points.

That makes us 5-0 at home, which UAB has not done since 2019, plus 5-4 overall and 3-2 in the American. Next Saturday, Nov. 14, we head to Temple at Lincoln Financial Field. Curtain down on a good one. Take a bow, Blazers, and give those jerseys to the kids.

Ja'Vin Simpkins ran for two fourth-quarter touchdowns, Rod Robinson II ran for 101 yards and Jonah Delange made three field goals.
Marlin Dean had three sacks as UAB held Charlotte to 234 yards. The Blazers are 5-4, 3-2 in the American.
Charlotte took the ball away four times. We took the fourth quarter.

articles.title: Charlotte vs UAB: 49ers' Defense Fights, Falls 23-12
articles.matchup: Final: UAB (5-4) 23, Charlotte (1-8) 12, Sat., Nov. 7, Protective Stadium, Birmingham. Next: vs. East Carolina, Sat., Nov. 14, Jerry Richardson Stadium, Charlotte
articles.text:
UAB 23, Charlotte 12. Saturday morning in uptown Charlotte, the Salute to Veterans Parade stepped off on Tryon Street at 11, marching south from 9th Street to MLK Boulevard with more than 2,000 participants. Respect to every one of them. By mid-afternoon our 49ers were in Birmingham, and I was opening the Drive Ledger on a game that stayed tied 6-6 deep into the third quarter.

The ledger shows a defense that paid dividends. Collin Gill intercepted Ryder Burton in the first quarter, Jonathan Patterson intercepted him in the second, and Shamar McIntosh made a third interception and returned it 31 yards to the UAB 21 to open the second half. Gill also had a sack and knocked a ball loose, and Kadin Schmitz recovered it and finished with 11 tackles. Four takeaways, zero giveaways. That is a balance sheet I would frame.

The problem is what we did with the interest. Those turnovers produced two Aiden Bui field goals, from 26 and 32 yards, and a 6-3 lead in the third. Bui also missed from 41 early. Against a UAB defense that led the country against the throw coming in, we finished with 59 rushing yards on 31 carries and converted 4 of 17 third downs. Field goals are fine. They are not a long-term investment strategy.

Conner Harrell came home to the Birmingham area, where he won a state title at this very stadium in high school, and he battled. He went 15 of 31 for 175 yards and found Jaden Barnes for a 14-yard touchdown with 1:01 left. Barnes caught six balls for 80 yards and ripped off a 56-yard punt return. Gavin Willis made nine tackles.

UAB owned the fourth with a field goal and two short Ja'Vin Simpkins touchdown runs. We are 1-8 and 1-4 in the American. East Carolina comes to Jerry Richardson Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 14, and the market says buy. I'm buying.

articles.title: App State vs Georgia State: Turnovers Sink Heroes Day, 23-39
articles.matchup: Final: Georgia State Panthers (5-4) 39, App State Mountaineers (5-4) 23, Sat., Nov. 7, Kidd Brewer Stadium, Boone. Next: at Marshall, Sat., Nov. 14, 6:00 PM ET, Joan C. Edwards Stadium, Huntington
articles.text:
Georgia State 39, App State 23, on Heroes Day in Boone. Student Veteran Services and the Military Affairs Committee threw a tailgate on the McKinney Alumni Center patio for military members, veterans and their families, and that part of the day went just right. The football part was a hard climb with bad footing, and I won't pretend the view at the top was pretty.

We had our moments. Malachi Singleton found Dillon Galloway for a 3-yard score in the first quarter. In the second, Chris Lofton took a lateral and threw it 56 yards to Jamel Howse for a touchdown, a double throw that would've made my granddaddy put down his whittling knife. That put us up 14-13. A few minutes later the afternoon turned, because Coby Owens jumped a throw and ran it back 23 yards for a Georgia State score.

The Panthers kept stacking. Ayden Pereira threw three touchdowns on 10 completions, Samer Layous kicked four field goals, and Lanear McCrary Jr. ran for 123 yards. Georgia State piled up 265 rushing yards and held the ball for 37:19. We managed 59 yards on the ground and got sacked five times.

Singleton went 23 of 34 for 241 yards with two touchdowns, two interceptions and a lost fumble. Three turnovers will undo any good work. Lofton was the best player on the field in black and gold: six catches for 117 yards, the 4-yard touchdown from Singleton in the fourth, plus that 56-yard throw. James London made a 37-yard field goal. Alex Mitchell led the defense with eight tackles and Colton Phares had seven.

Honest footing: 3 of 10 on third down, 0 for 2 on fourth, and the first loss to Georgia State in 13 tries. We're 5-4 and 2-3 in the Sun Belt, still one win shy of a bowl.

Next is a trip to Marshall on Saturday, Nov. 14, at 6 PM ET at Joan C. Edwards Stadium in Huntington. Steady climbing. Bring a jacket, and bring a better plan for the run game.

articles.title: Georgia State vs App State: Panthers Win in Boone at Last, 39-23
articles.matchup: Final: Georgia State Panthers (5-4) 39, App State Mountaineers (5-4) 23, Sat., Nov. 7, Kidd Brewer Stadium, Boone. Next: vs. Georgia Southern, Sat., Nov. 14, 3:30 PM ET, Center Parc Stadium, Atlanta
articles.text:
Georgia State 39, App State 23, and the Panthers finally found the express lane up the mountain. Thirteen meetings, and this is the first time we've beaten the Mountaineers. Back downtown on Saturday, the men's basketball team tipped off against Andrews College at the Convocation Center on Capitol Avenue at 1 p.m., so it was a full Panther day in Atlanta. The real party, though, was in Boone.

Ayden Pereira didn't need many throws. He went 10 of 17 for 115 yards, and three of those completions were touchdowns: 22 yards to Grant Hollier, 10 to DJ Riles and 17 to Rodshaun Dorsey. That was Dorsey's ninth touchdown catch of the season, tying the school record. Ten completions, three scores. That's MARTA efficiency, every stop on time.

The defense delivered the turning point. App State had jumped ahead 14-13 on a trick-play double throw for 56 yards, and Coby Owens jumped a route and ran an interception back 23 yards for a touchdown. 20-14, and we never trailed again. Owens later grabbed his second interception, the first two of his career on the same afternoon. Xavier Esqillion and Richard Kramer had two sacks each, Kelan Butler added one, and Jabriel Rhodes-Nelson fell on a fumble. Tyson McCrary led us with seven tackles.

Then we ran the ball like the Connector at 3 a.m., wide open and no brake lights. Lanear McCrary Jr. carried 21 times for 123 yards, and Dennis Murray Jr. broke a 56-yarder on his way to 76. We ran for 265 yards, held the ball for 37:19 and never coughed it up once.

Samer Layous made it rain from the mountaintop: four field goals, from 45, 52, 27 and 45, with the 52 a career long. That's 15 points from one leg, and it kept App State chasing two scores the entire second half.

We're 5-4 and 2-3 in the Sun Belt. Next is Georgia Southern at Center Parc Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 14, at 3:30 PM ET, and you know what that means downtown. Let's ride.

articles.title: Baylor vs Iowa State: Lagway's Legs Power a Homecoming 42-31
articles.matchup: Final: Iowa State Cyclones (4-5) 31, Baylor Bears (6-3) 42, Sat., Nov. 7, McLane Stadium, Waco. Next: at BYU, Sat., Nov. 14, LaVell Edwards Stadium, Provo
articles.text:
Baylor Bears 42, Iowa State Cyclones 31. Final score 42-31 at McLane Stadium on Homecoming, and Waco did it the Baylor way from sunrise on. The oldest and largest collegiate homecoming parade in the country rolled down Fifth Street to campus Saturday morning, floats and bands and all, and by early afternoon the Bears had built a comeback worth putting on a float of its own. Six and three. Four and two in the Big 12.

I will be honest about the before photos. Iowa State led 17-7 in the second quarter after Aiden Flora broke a 40-yard run and Jaylen Raynor found Cameron Pettaway for 50. That room needed a full gut job.

Then DJ Lagway grabbed the hammer. He took off for a 54-yard touchdown run, and in the final minute of the half, a loose ball in the end zone ended up with offensive lineman Koltin Sieracki on top of it for the go-ahead score. Ugly demo, pretty finish, 21-17 at the half. Out of the break, Lagway lofted a 62-yarder to Taz Williams Jr., and Ryelan Morris ran 33 yards for another score. Four straight touchdowns. Shiplap on every wall, 35-17.

Lagway finished 16 of 28 for 229 yards and two touchdowns, the first a 19-yarder to Tony Livingston, and ran 13 times for a career-high 119 yards. Morris added an 11-yard score late to make it 42-23. Gavin Freeman caught six balls for 60. Micah Gifford led us with nine tackles, and Travion Barnes and Devin Turner each got a sack.

The detail work was spotless: zero turnovers and one penalty, for 15 yards, all afternoon. Flora still ran for 182 against us, and Iowa State held the ball for 36 minutes, so the run defense goes on the punch list. But 39,229 came home for Homecoming and left happy, and we are 2-0 with interim coach Joe Klanderman in charge.

Next job site: BYU, Saturday, Nov. 14, at LaVell Edwards Stadium in Provo, kickoff time still to be set. Pack the tape measure. Sic 'em.

articles.title: Iowa State vs Baylor: Flora's 182 Yards Lost in Waco, 31-42
articles.matchup: Final: Iowa State Cyclones (4-5) 31, Baylor Bears (6-3) 42, Sat., Nov. 7, McLane Stadium, Waco. Next: vs Cincinnati, Sat., Nov. 14, Jack Trice Stadium, Ames
articles.text:
Iowa State Cyclones 31, Baylor Bears 42. Final score 42-31 at McLane Stadium, and the forecast from Waco reads cloudy with a long ride home. We led 17-7 in the second quarter, then the pressure system flipped and Baylor scored four straight touchdowns. Four and five. Two and four in the Big 12. Oh and four on the road.

Back in Ames, the Antique Tractor Club at Iowa State rolled out its fifth annual Fall Tractor Show on Saturday in Lot 10 behind Town Engineering, free meal and pedal-tractor raffle included. Old iron that keeps running no matter the weather. That is exactly what Aiden Flora looked like in Texas. Twenty-six carries for 182 yards, a 40-yard touchdown run in the first quarter, and a two-point throw to Jaylen Raynor late for good measure.

The first half was all tailwind for a while. Kyle Konrardy drilled a 57-yard field goal. Raynor hit Cameron Pettaway for a 50-yard touchdown and a 17-7 lead. Then the front moved through. DJ Lagway ran 54 yards for a score, and with 23 seconds left before the half, a Baylor fumble rolled into the end zone and their lineman, Koltin Sieracki, fell on it. Down 21-17 at the break, from up 10. That is a weather event.

The third quarter was the hailstorm. Lagway hit Taz Williams Jr. for 62 yards, Ryelan Morris ran 33 for another score, and it was 35-17. Raynor kept fighting, 22 of 37 for 256 yards and two touchdowns, with a 9-yarder to Vince Benetti on the first play of the fourth and a 3-yard run late. We outgained Baylor 472 to 423 and held the ball for 36 minutes. Lagway still ran for 119 yards against us, and Flora lost a fumble we could not afford. Konrardy missed one of his two kicks, and we went 8 of 17 on third down.

Cincinnati comes to Jack Trice Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 14, kickoff time still to be set. Three games left. Clear skies are possible, so bring the cardinal and gold and let's warm the place up.

articles.title: Arkansas State vs UL Monroe: Red Wolves Lose Rice Bowl, 19-17
articles.matchup: Final: UL Monroe (2-7) 19, Arkansas State (4-5) 17, Sat., Nov. 7, Centennial Bank Stadium, Jonesboro. Next: at Coastal Carolina, Sat., Nov. 14, Brooks Stadium, Conway
articles.text:
UL Monroe 19, Arkansas State 17. It was Rice Bowl day in Jonesboro, the second time the Red Wolves and Warhawks played for a trophy named after rice, which is about as Delta as a trophy gets, and we came off a bye week chasing a third straight win at Centennial Bank Stadium. The rice went back down to Louisiana, and I'm sitting in the blind with the decoys, listening to the wind.

We had our chances. Trey Owens hit Jaylen Bonelli for 40 yards on the opening drive, though Clune Van Andel's 39-yard try missed. Then Owens drove us 75 yards and found Hunter Summers for a 17-yard touchdown. Elias Sherman had already blocked the Warhawks' extra point, so we led 7-6. Tony Carter intercepted Aidan Armenta at our 4, and Timothy Carter capped a 97-yard march with a 4-yard run for a 14-6 lead.

That's when the birds started flying the wrong way. Owens was intercepted with 36 seconds left in the half, ULM kicked a field goal as time ran out, and Armenta ran in from 2 to open the third for a 16-14 Warhawk lead. Makai Shahid intercepted Armenta later in the third and brought it back 17 yards, but a fourth-down sack ended our next good drive.

Van Andel's 41-yarder put us back on top, 17-16, with 5:42 left. ULM ground out seven plays and a 40-yard field goal. We got the ball back, crossed midfield, and on third down Owens was intercepted at the ULM 20 with a minute to go.

Honest scouting report: Owens completed 16 of 29 for 193 yards with that touchdown and two interceptions, and he ran for 67 yards, including a 48-yard keeper. Chauncy Cobb caught five balls for 61 yards and returned three kickoffs for 73. AG McGhee made 14 tackles, Tre Stevens 10 and Joe Drew nine with a sack. But ULM ran for 268 yards, held the ball for 35:32 and converted 9 of 14 third downs.

We are 4-5 and 2-3 in the Sun Belt. Next Saturday, Nov. 14, we head to Coastal Carolina at Brooks Stadium. Patience is the first rule of a good hunt. I'll blow the call again when we earn it.

articles.title: UL Monroe vs Arkansas State: Warhawks Keep Rice Bowl, 19-17
articles.matchup: Final: UL Monroe (2-7) 19, Arkansas State (4-5) 17, Sat., Nov. 7, Centennial Bank Stadium, Jonesboro. Next: vs. Louisiana, Thu., Nov. 12, Malone Stadium, Monroe
articles.text:
UL Monroe 19, Arkansas State 17, and I KNEW IT. I knew it at 2 a.m., I knew it at kickoff, and I knew it when Gavin Howard came down with that ball with a minute left. Saturday morning back home, folks gathered at The Grove on our own ULM campus for the Monroe/West Monroe Walk to End Alzheimer's and planted the Promise Garden. By afternoon the Warhawks gave Monroe one more thing to hold onto: our first win in Jonesboro since 2001.

We kept the Rice Bowl, too. Two meetings, two trophies, and the optimism counter on my desk is pinned at 100 and smoking a little.

Aidan Armenta opened it with a 9-yard touchdown run to finish a 79-yard drive, and after we trailed 14-6 he took us 75 yards to start the third and ran it in from 2 for a 16-14 lead. Austin Carlisle did the heavy lifting the rest of the way: 111 rushing yards on 19 carries and 4 for 4 throwing. Don Chaney added 68 yards, including a 36-yard burst on our first drive. As a team we ran for 268 yards and held the ball for 35:32.

The defense wrote the happy ending. Armoni Rue intercepted Trey Owens late in the half, and Abram Murray kicked a 23-yarder as time ran out. In the third, Kevontay Wells sacked Owens on fourth down. Noah Flemmings led us with eight tackles and a sack. Then Arkansas State kicked a 41-yarder to go up 17-16 with 5:42 left, and we answered with seven plays, nearly four minutes off the clock and a 40-yard Murray field goal with 1:49 left.

One more stand. The Red Wolves crossed midfield, and on third down Howard, who had already forced an Owens fumble in the first half, made the first interception of his career at our 20. Carlisle got the first down, we knelt, and somewhere in Ouachita Parish a man on the overnight shift turned his radio all the way up.

That's two wins in a row on the road in this league. We are 2-7, 2-3 in the Sun Belt, and Louisiana comes to Monroe on Thursday night, Nov. 12. Keep the faith, y'all. It's working.

articles.title: Auburn vs Arkansas: McPherson's Late Kick Wins It 26-23
articles.matchup: Final: Auburn Tigers (5-4) 26, Arkansas Razorbacks (3-6) 23, Sat., Nov. 7, Jordan-Hare Stadium, Auburn. Next: at Mississippi State, Sat., Nov. 14, 12:00 PM ET, Davis Wade Stadium
articles.text:
Auburn 26, Arkansas 23, and well, hey there, War Eagle, that's how you finish a game on the Plains. It was the annual Military Appreciation and Wear Navy game, with Army and Air Force cadets sworn in on Pat Dye Field, ROTC members carrying service flags out with the team and a B-52 thundering above Jordan-Hare before kickoff. 88,043 of us in navy, and by 33 seconds left, every one of us was on our feet.

The first half was not our finest reenactment. Arkansas went up 10-0 on a field goal and a 2-yard run, and we didn't score until Alex McPherson knocked one through from 33 with three seconds left in the half. Then Byrum Brown took charge of the second half like the lead in my personal Iron Bowl plays. He found Chas Nimrod for 15 yards in the third, and after the Hogs kicked to go up 13-9, Brown ran in from 5 early in the fourth for a 16-13 lead.

Arkansas tied it, and Brown hit Keshaun Singleton for a 28-yard touchdown with 3:56 left. Then the Hogs tied it again on a 23-yard throw with 1:54 to play, and my lemonade glass began to shake. Brown didn't. He got us into range, and McPherson drilled a 43-yarder with 33 seconds left, his second game-winner of the season. That's a roll-the-oak night if I ever saw one.

Brown was everywhere: 23 of 34 for 180 yards and two touchdowns, plus 122 yards on 23 carries with a long of 39. Singleton caught six for 58, Christian Neptune six for 33 and Nimrod five for 38. On defense, freshman linebacker Shadarius Toodle was the hero of the reenactment, with 11 tackles, three sacks and four and a half tackles for loss. AnQuon Fegans intercepted KJ Jackson, Eric Winters recovered a fumble, and Hudson Kaak averaged 44.7 yards on six punts.

The honest part: Arkansas ran for 172 yards and held the ball for more than 33 minutes, and we were 4 of 15 on third down. Our front took injuries all day. That's our fourth one-possession win of the season, and I'll take every one of them.

We're 5-4 and 3-4 in the SEC. Next is a trip to Mississippi State on Saturday, Nov. 14, at noon ET at Davis Wade Stadium. War Eagle, y'all.

articles.title: Arkansas vs Auburn: Hogs Rally to Tie, Lose on Late Kick 23-26
articles.matchup: Final: Auburn Tigers (5-4) 26, Arkansas Razorbacks (3-6) 23, Sat., Nov. 7, Jordan-Hare Stadium, Auburn. Next: vs. South Carolina, Sat., Nov. 14, 7:45 PM ET, Donald W. Reynolds Razorback Stadium, Fayetteville
articles.text:
Auburn 26, Arkansas 23. Woooo, Pig. Here comes the stat, and it hurts: 33 seconds. That's how much time was left when Auburn's kicker split it from 43. Back home, Fayetteville's Veterans Day Parade was honoring Northwest Arkansas veterans and their families from 11 to 1, right as our Hogs were kicking off on the Plains. Those folks deserved the salute. We deserved a better last minute.

Science class, first lesson: the run game came back to life. We came into Jordan-Hare last in the SEC in rushing yards per game, and we ran for 172. Cam Settles carried 16 times for 100 yards, including a 46-yard burst. Sutton Smith ripped off a 65-yarder. Braylen Russell punched in a 2-yard touchdown, Max Gilbert hit from 38, and we led 10-0 in the second quarter. 10-3 at the half.

Second lesson: field goals keep you alive, touchdowns win. Gilbert made three of his five tries, from 38, 37 and 46, and the 46-yarder tied it 16-16 with 9:32 left. Then Auburn went ahead 23-16 with 3:56 to go, and KJ Jackson answered like a grown man. He drove us down and found Antonio Jordan for a 23-yard touchdown with 1:54 left. 23-23. Hog Call, louder than I've done it all year.

It wasn't enough time on the clock for us, and it was plenty for them. Auburn moved into range and kicked the 43-yarder with 33 seconds left. Jackson finished 14 of 30 for 180 yards with the touchdown and an interception. He also got sacked hard, losing 27 net yards on the ground, mostly to a freshman linebacker who made three sacks.

The defense kept us in it. Khmori House made nine tackles with two for loss, Miguel Mitchell had eight and two for loss, Joker Johnson broke up two throws, and Carlon Jones got a sack. We held the ball for 33:16 and converted 8 of 18 third downs. Chris Marshall caught five balls for 65 yards. Every one of those players fought for 60 minutes.

We're 3-6 and 1-5 in the SEC. South Carolina comes to Fayetteville on Saturday, Nov. 14, at 7:45 PM ET. Lights on, Razorback Stadium loud, and a whole lesson plan built on that run game. Woooo, Pig. Sooie.

articles.title: Kansas State vs Oklahoma State: Cowboys Run Away, 66-28
articles.matchup: Final: Oklahoma State (6-3) 66, Kansas State (4-5) 28, Sat., Nov. 7, Bill Snyder Family Stadium, Manhattan. Next: at TCU, Sat., Nov. 14, Amon G. Carter Stadium, Fort Worth
articles.text:
Oklahoma State 66, Kansas State 28. Saturday was National Bison Day at the Flint Hills Discovery Center down on Third Street, with kids making bison horn headbands from 10 to 2. Across town at Bill Snyder Family Stadium, 52,134 of us watched the Cowboys stampede through our fields like a herd with someplace to be.

There were a couple of bumper harvests worth hollering about. On our second possession, Blake Barnett found Derrick Salley Jr. behind the defense for a 73-yard touchdown, and it was 7-7. In the second quarter, Logan Bartley stepped in front of a Drew Mestemaker throw and took it 18 yards for a touchdown. Wesley Fair also punched the ball loose from Wyatt Young, and Rex Van Wyhe fell on it.

The rest of the field was dry sorghum. Oklahoma State scored touchdowns on its first six red-zone trips, and Caleb Hawkins ran for 175 yards and three scores. The Cowboys led 28-7 after one quarter and 49-14 at the half, and they piled up 565 yards. We threw three interceptions. That is not how you bring in a crop.

Some rows still came up green. Salley caught a second touchdown, an 18-yarder from Dillon Duff in the third, and finished with three catches for 100 yards. Rodney Fields Jr. carried 20 times for 87 yards and scored from a yard out in the fourth. Jaron Tibbs caught six balls. Fair and Van Wyhe each made eight tackles, Asa Newsom had six, and we went 3 for 6 on fourth down because nobody on this team quit.

That is three straight losses. We are 4-5 and 1-5 in the Big 12, and next Saturday, Nov. 14, we go to TCU at Amon G. Carter Stadium. I'm planting a basil seed right here on my desk. You can't rush a harvest, and you can't rush a season either.

articles.title: Oklahoma State vs Kansas State: Mestemaker Does It All, 66-28
articles.matchup: Final: Oklahoma State (6-3) 66, Kansas State (4-5) 28, Sat., Nov. 7, Bill Snyder Family Stadium, Manhattan. Next: vs. Texas Tech, Sat., Nov. 14, Boone Pickens Stadium, Stillwater
articles.text:
Oklahoma State 66, Kansas State 28, and that ride lasted the full eight seconds and then some. Back in Stillwater on Saturday, the Fall Festival Craft Show filled the Payne County Expo Center with handmade jewelry, crochet and fall finds from 9 to 4. Up in Manhattan, our Cowboys were handcrafting something too: 565 yards of offense and a 49-14 halftime lead.

Drew Mestemaker did a little of everything except sell popcorn. He completed 22 of 28 for 313 yards and four touchdown throws, ran one in from a yard out, and in the third quarter caught a 5-yard touchdown from Wyatt Young. The ESPN wrap says no Bowl Subdivision player had pulled off that combination since 2021. Hold onto your hat.

Caleb Hawkins was the bronc nobody could stay on. He had 96 rushing yards before the first quarter was 10 minutes old, scoring from 21 and 37, and he added a 9-yard touchdown run before the half and a 5-yard touchdown catch after it. He finished with 175 yards on 20 carries. Miles Coleman caught six balls for 95 yards, including a 19-yard score with 11 seconds left in the half, and Justin Bowick opened the day with a 32-yard touchdown catch.

I'll tell you plainly, the defense deserves a buckle too. LaDainian Fields intercepted two throws, Quinton Hammonds returned another 36 yards to the K-State 11, and Isaiah Chisom made 11 tackles. Kansas State scored on a long blown assignment and an interception return early, but our guys kept answering.

Not every ride was clean. Mestemaker threw one interception that went back for a score, and we lost a fumble, so the judges will knock off a point or two. Sam Keltner was perfect, though, nine extra points and a 23-yard field goal.

We are 6-3 and 4-2 in the Big 12. Texas Tech comes to Boone Pickens Stadium next Saturday, Nov. 14, and I'll be the fella in orange from hat to boots. Ride 'em, Cowboys.

articles.title: South Carolina vs Texas A&M: Sellers' Ankle, Sellers' Run, 17-9
articles.matchup: Final: Texas A&M Aggies (4-5) 9, South Carolina Gamecocks (6-3) 17, Sat., Nov. 7, Williams-Brice Stadium, Columbia. Next: at Arkansas, Sat., Nov. 14, 7:45 PM ET, Donald W. Reynolds Razorback Stadium, Fayetteville
articles.text:
South Carolina Gamecocks 17, Texas A&M Aggies 9. Cue the music, because the final score is 17-9 and Williams-Brice just watched LaNorris Sellers limp, then sprint, into Gamecock legend on Homecoming weekend. Six and three. Four and three in the SEC. Four straight wins after opening league play oh-and-three, and bowl eligible.

What a stage it was. Steve Spurrier and the back-to-back national champion baseball teams from 2010 and 2011 were recognized at halftime as part of the new Athletics Hall of Fame class, in front of the 22nd straight sellout, 78,687 strong in Columbia. And while the Head Ball Coach was taking a bow, our quarterback was in the locker room getting his ankle X-rayed. Spotlight, please. He came back out.

This was a grind. Sellers hit Mazeo Bennett Jr. from 1 yard for our only first-half touchdown, after Bennett had already ripped off a 64-yard catch. Texas A&M answered with three field goals and led 9-7 into the fourth. Our offense sputtered, and the Aggies ran it right at us for 206 yards and held the ball for 34 minutes.

Then the defense stole the show. Fred Johnson made 11 tackles with a sack and two tackles for loss. Anthony Addison added eight. We stuffed the Aggies twice on fourth down. Malik Orsan drilled a 43-yarder with 8:14 left to put us up 10-9, and Mason Love kept pinning them back with a 51.4-yard average.

And the finale? One play after Anthony Addison and Justin Okoronkwo sacked Marcel Reed on fourth down, Sellers, bad ankle and all, broke loose for 41 yards and the touchdown with 1:19 left. Texas A&M still got to our 3 on its final drive, and the last throw sailed high. Lights up. Curtain call. Sellers finished 20 of 31 for 251 yards, and Nyck Harbor caught four for 70.

Next stop: Arkansas, Saturday, Nov. 14, at 7:45 PM ET in Fayetteville. Pack the speakers. Forever to thee.

articles.title: Texas A&M vs South Carolina: Three Kicks Not Enough, 9-17
articles.matchup: Final: Texas A&M Aggies (4-5) 9, South Carolina Gamecocks (6-3) 17, Sat., Nov. 7, Williams-Brice Stadium, Columbia. Next: vs Tennessee, Sat., Nov. 14, Kyle Field, College Station
articles.text:
Texas A&M Aggies 9, South Carolina Gamecocks 17. Final score 17-9 at Williams-Brice Stadium, and I am writing this from a closet where I have been practicing silent yells since the clock hit zero. Four and five. One and five in the SEC. Oh and four on the road. We outgained them, outlasted them on the clock, never gave the ball away, and still lost.

Back in College Station on Saturday, the campus exhibit Here for Good, marking 150 years of Texas A&M University, was open, honoring a century and a half of Aggies standing together. I will explain the tradition, then explain the explanation, as is my way: a 150-year school teaches you that one bad November afternoon does not define you. It does, however, sting like a sunburn at Kyle Field in September.

Here is the maddening part. Rueben Owens II ran like a man on a mission, 137 yards on 19 carries, a season high, with a 44-yard burst. Marcel Reed threw for 251 yards. Isaiah Horton caught five for 78, and Aaron Gregory caught five for 48. We piled up 457 yards and 26 first downs and held the ball for 34 minutes and 36 seconds. David Olano hit from 40, from 46 as the first half expired, and from 44 to put us up 9-7 in the third quarter.

Then the drives began dying in the red zone. Olano missed his first kick of the season after 16 straight makes, one that would have pushed the lead to five. We went 0 for 2 on fourth down, and the second of those stops handed LaNorris Sellers the ball one play before he ran 41 yards for the clincher with 1:19 left, on a bad ankle no less. Malik Orsan had already put them up 10-9 from 43. Our last drive reached their 3 and ended with a throw sailing high.

Credit where due: Tyler White averaged 51.3 yards a punt and dropped all four inside the 20. Marco Jones got a sack. Marcus Ratcliffe made six tackles. The defense held a red-hot Gamecock offense to 17 points on the road, and that should have been enough.

Tennessee comes to Kyle Field on Saturday, Nov. 14, kickoff time still to be set. Finish drives, find the end zone, and let the 12th Man do the rest. Gig 'em.

articles.title: Tulane vs Tulsa: Homecoming Turns Sour for Green Wave, 10-60
articles.matchup: Final: Tulsa Golden Hurricane (5-4) 60, Tulane Green Wave (4-5) 10, Sat., Nov. 7, Yulman Stadium, New Orleans. Next: at Rice, Sat., Nov. 14, 2:00 PM ET, Houston
articles.text:
Tulsa 60, Tulane 10, on Homecoming. Wave '26 had Tailgate Village rolling on the Berger Family Lawn from 8 in the morning, and the Tulane University Marching Band led the whole parade from central campus to Yulman Stadium. That parade was the best march anybody in green made all day, and I say that with a heavy heart and an empty beignet bag.

We came in 3-1 at home, and the first quarter looked like a fair fight at 7-0. Then the second quarter turned into a parade marching the wrong direction. Tulsa scored 25 points, Baylor Hayes threw two more touchdowns, and we went to the locker room down 32-0. Hayes finished with 338 yards and four scores, and Oran Singleton Jr. caught 13 balls for 177 yards and three touchdowns. Tulsa ran for 224 more. I have no seasoning for that.

On our side, it never got moving. Trace Johnson went 11 of 19 for 69 yards with an interception. We went 2 of 12 on third down and gained 204 yards. Johnnie Daniels was the bright spot on the ground with 49 yards on 10 carries, and Destyn Hill caught four balls for 55. TJ Smith returned five kickoffs for 130 yards and made seven tackles, and Dickson Agu led us with eight stops. Those two kept swinging to the last snap.

Cooper Helmke put us on the board with a 38-yard field goal early in the fourth quarter. And with one second left, Dagan Bruno found Bredell Richardson for a 4-yard touchdown. That one deserved a beignet, and I gave it one, because you dance home no matter what in this town.

Honest notebook: the defense never got a takeaway, Tulsa never coughed it up, and that is how a 60 happens. Homecoming deserved better, and the Green Wave knows it.

We're 4-5 and 2-3 in the American. Next is a trip to Rice on Saturday, Nov. 14, at 2 PM ET in Houston. Roll Wave, and pack the trombones. We're due a better tune.

articles.title: Tulsa vs Tulane: Hayes and Singleton Strike Oil in 60-10 Romp
articles.matchup: Final: Tulsa Golden Hurricane (5-4) 60, Tulane Green Wave (4-5) 10, Sat., Nov. 7, Yulman Stadium, New Orleans. Next: vs. Florida Atlantic, Sat., Nov. 14, 3:30 PM ET, H. A. Chapman Stadium, Tulsa
articles.text:
Tulsa 60, Tulane 10. Friends, that is a gusher. Back home on Saturday morning, runners lined up for the Route 66 Runway Run on runway 18R at Tulsa International Airport, part of the Mother Road's 100th birthday party. Down in the Big Easy, Baylor Hayes and Oran Singleton Jr. treated Yulman Stadium like their own runway, and nobody on the Tulane side could catch them either.

It opened as a steady pump, 7-0 after one on a 3-yard toss from Hayes to Singleton. Then the second quarter hit pay sand. Owen Carey knocked in a 26-yard field goal, Hayes found Jimmy Calloway from 7, Javon Ross ran in from 11, and Hayes hit Singleton from 3 again with Damari Alston carrying the two-point try. Twenty-five points in one quarter. 32-0 at the half, on Tulane's Homecoming.

The survey kept producing. Singleton caught a 27-yard score early in the third, Alston ran one in from 6, Seth Davis broke a 31-yarder, and Sevion Morrison added a 3-yard run late. Hayes finished 26 of 33 for 338 yards and a career-high four touchdown throws, no interceptions. Singleton set career highs across the board: 13 catches, 177 yards and three scores. We ran for 224 yards as a team without one back carrying the load, and we piled up 562 yards and 31 first downs.

The defense drilled just as deep. Tulane managed 204 yards and went 2 of 12 on third down. Jaylen George and Thomas Davis each had a sack and a half, Zane Woodham got a full one, and JD Drew and NuNu Campbell each intercepted a throw. The Green Wave did not score until early in the fourth quarter, and their touchdown came with one second left. We committed two penalties all day for 10 yards and zero turnovers. Tidy wellhead, no leaks.

Here is why this one feels so good. We came in having dropped four of our last five, and our three league losses had come by a combined 12 points. This team needed a day when every valve opened at once, and it got one.

We're 5-4 and 2-3 in the American. Florida Atlantic comes to H. A. Chapman Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 14, at 3:30 PM ET. The rig is running hot. Let's keep drilling.

articles.title: NC State vs Duke: Wolfpack Shut Out of End Zone, Fall 41-3
articles.matchup: Final: Duke (7-2) 41, NC State (4-5) 3, Sat., Nov. 7, Carter-Finley Stadium, Raleigh. Next: vs. Syracuse, Sat., Nov. 14, Carter-Finley Stadium, Raleigh
articles.text:
Duke 41, NC State 3. It was our Annual Military Appreciation game, and before kickoff the Lowes Food Fan Zone between the Lenovo Center and Carter-Finley Stadium collected paper towels, tissues and supplies for veterans and their families through Support U.S. Armed Forces. That was the warmest part of my grill all day.

The thermometer told the story early. Duke's Nate Sheppard took his first carry 69 yards for a touchdown. We answered with a 39-yard Kanoah Vinesett field goal, and that was the last time we touched the scoreboard. Sheppard scored again from 8, Gavin Strange hit a 25-yarder, and Walker Eget found Jaivon Solomon for an 18-yard touchdown with 26 seconds left in the half.

Then came the moment that sent the whole cooker up in smoke. We tried a 50-yard field goal on the last play of the half. It came up short, Andrew Pellicciotta caught it in the back of the end zone and ran it 100 yards the other way. That turned 24-3 into 31-3, and 56,919 people went quiet in a hurry.

I promised not to cook the numbers, so here they are, raw. We ran 25 times for 32 yards. We gained 217 yards in all, the same number Sheppard ran for by himself. We converted 3 of 14 third downs. CJ Bailey completed 15 of 24 for 123 yards and took hits all afternoon. Amiri Acker caught two balls for 54 yards, Hunter Provience caught five for 51, and King Mack had six tackles and three kickoff returns. Popo Aguirre led us with eight stops.

This was our first game without a touchdown since a 24-3 loss at Duke in 2023, and interim coach Todd Goebbel is now 1-1. We are 4-5 and 2-4 in the ACC, still 4-2 at home. Syracuse comes to Carter-Finley next Saturday, Nov. 14. I'll be at the same lot, same grill, and I'll start the coals earlier.

articles.title: Duke vs NC State: Sheppard's 217 Yards Lead 41-3 Rout
articles.matchup: Final: Duke (7-2) 41, NC State (4-5) 3, Sat., Nov. 7, Carter-Finley Stadium, Raleigh. Next: at Miami, Sat., Nov. 14, Hard Rock Stadium, Miami Gardens
articles.text:
Duke 41, NC State 3. Durham Parks and Recreation closed its fall film series on Saturday night by screening Best in Show at Durham Central Park, which I consider a peer-reviewed summary of our afternoon in Raleigh. Class was in session at Carter-Finley Stadium, and the Wolfpack did not do the reading.

Thesis statement: Nate Sheppard is the most important person in the Triangle. On his first carry of the day, he went straight up the middle for a 69-yard touchdown. He added scores from 8 and 4 yards and finished with 217 rushing yards on 18 carries. That one man matched NC State's entire offensive output of 217 yards. I have checked the math twice. It holds.

Supporting evidence, section two. Walker Eget completed 22 of 31 for 208 yards, and with 26 seconds left in the half he hit Jaivon Solomon on a short throw that Solomon turned into an 18-yard touchdown. Then came the citation I will frame. NC State tried a 50-yard field goal on the final play of the half, it fell short, and Andrew Pellicciotta, back after missing two games, caught it deep in the end zone, weaved across the field and ran it back 100 yards. That made it 31-3 at the half.

The defense earned honors too. NC State ran 25 times for 32 yards, converted 3 of 14 third downs and never reached the end zone. Preston Watson recorded a sack, Nick Morris Jr. led us with six tackles, and we never gave the ball away. Gavin Strange added field goals from 25 and 46 yards and made every extra point.

That is six wins in the last seven meetings with our neighbors from Raleigh. We are 7-2, 4-2 in the ACC and 3-1 away from home. Final exam: next Saturday, Nov. 14, at Miami in Hard Rock Stadium. Grade for this one? Incomplete is not an option. A-plus, with honors.

articles.title: Syracuse vs Clemson: Homecoming Comeback Falls Short 13-18
articles.matchup: Final: Clemson Tigers (6-3) 18, Syracuse Orange (4-5) 13, Sat., Nov. 7, JMA Wireless Dome, Syracuse. Next: at NC State, Sat., Nov. 14, 12:00 PM ET, Carter-Finley Stadium, Raleigh
articles.text:
Clemson 18, Syracuse 13. Homecoming weekend in the Salt City, 'Cuse on the Quad humming all morning in front of Hendricks Chapel, 37,291 in the Dome, and we lost by five again. That's a lake-effect squall, folks, the kind that drops six inches on the Thruway and leaves you shoveling in the dark.

The first half was field goal ping-pong. Tripp Woody hit from 26 and 46 and doinked one from 32. Clemson's kicker made three, and it was 9-6 at the half. Our defense held the Tigers out of the end zone all day, and I'll give that defense a two-foot snowfall for effort. Clemson went 4 of 16 on third down and scored zero offensive touchdowns.

Then came the play that slid the plow into the ditch. Down 12-6 in the third, Steve Angeli's backward toss got knocked loose, and Jahiem Lawson ran it back 22 yards for a score. 18-6. Early in the fourth we marched to the Clemson 4, and on third-and-goal Ashton Hampton intercepted Angeli in the end zone. That one stung like February wind off Onondaga Lake.

Angeli finally found Daunte Bacheyie for a 33-yard touchdown with 3:12 left to make it 18-13, but Clemson took the ball and ran out the clock. Angeli went 18 of 40 for 263 yards, and there was a stretch of 11 straight misses. Bacheyie caught six for 82, Justus Ross-Simmons had four for 84, and Calvin Russell III added five for 80.

The good stuff deserves its own forecast. Ahmad Miller ran for 101 yards on 20 carries. Davien Kerr intercepted Tait Reynolds, Fran Brown Jr. recovered a Clemson fumble, and Keyshawn Johnson had a sack and two tackles for loss. Nissi Ogbebor got home for a sack too. The defense played well enough to win. The offense left too many points out in the cold.

Our five losses have come by a combined 33 points, which tells you how close this team keeps living to a breakthrough. We're 4-5 and 2-5 in the ACC and need two wins to reach a bowl. Next is a trip to NC State on Saturday, Nov. 14, at noon at Carter-Finley Stadium in Raleigh. Grab a salt potato. We go again.

articles.title: Clemson vs Syracuse: Lawson Scoop, Hauser Kicks Win It 18-13
articles.matchup: Final: Clemson Tigers (6-3) 18, Syracuse Orange (4-5) 13, Sat., Nov. 7, JMA Wireless Dome, Syracuse. Next: vs. Georgia Tech, Sat., Nov. 14, 12:30 PM ET, Memorial Stadium, Clemson
articles.text:
Clemson 18, Syracuse 13, and y'all, that's a win that took some choreography. An hour before kickoff, the Clemson University Symphony Orchestra was playing Peter and the Wolf on the green at Patrick Square, every character with its own instrument. Up in the Dome, our defense played the wolf, and Steve Angeli spent the afternoon hearing footsteps.

Nolan Hauser was our whole offense for a while, and I mean that with love. He hit from 32, 36 and 37 in the first half, missed from 57, and we went to the break up 9-6. In the third he drilled a 54-yarder for 12-6, four field goals on the day. He also punted twice for a 54.5 average. Somebody give that young man a second locker.

Then came the step-slide-scoop I'll be teaching the flag corps for years. Angeli tried a backward toss, our defensive tackle jarred it loose, and Jahiem Lawson scooped it up and ran 22 yards to the end zone. 18-6 with 6:39 left in the third. The two-point try failed, and I didn't care one bit.

Syracuse kept coming, and the defense kept answering. On third-and-goal from our 4 with a little more than 10 minutes left, Ashton Hampton intercepted Angeli in the end zone. Hampton finished with eight tackles and two breakups, Sammy Brown made eight stops, and we sacked Angeli three times while he went 18 of 40. At one stretch he missed 11 straight throws. When Syracuse finally scored on a 33-yarder with 3:12 left, our offense took the ball and never gave it back.

Honest film session: no offensive touchdowns and 4 of 16 on third down is not a dance anybody wants to repeat. Tait Reynolds went 17 of 28 for 161 yards with an interception and ran for 61. Jarvis Green broke a 53-yard run and finished with 85. Bryant Wesco Jr. caught six balls for 100 yards and even threw one for 36, though he also lost a fumble.

We're 6-3 and 4-2 in the ACC, and we've won two in a row for the first time in more than a month. Georgia Tech comes to Memorial Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 14, at 12:30 PM ET. Orange you glad we're headed home?

articles.title: Wake Forest vs Merrimack: 77 Points for Jim Grobe's Homecoming
articles.matchup: Final: Merrimack Warriors (4-6) 0, Wake Forest Demon Deacons (8-1) 77, Sat., Nov. 7, Allegacy Federal Credit Union Stadium, Winston-Salem. Next: at SMU, Sat., Nov. 14, 12:00 PM ET, Gerald J. Ford Stadium, Dallas
articles.text:
Wake Forest Demon Deacons 77, Merrimack Warriors 0. Final score 77-0 on Homecoming and Reunion Weekend in Winston-Salem, and the most points in the history of this program. Jim Grobe came back as our Open the Gate honoree and led the team onto the field with the Demon Deacon. The man retired with 77 coaching wins here, tied for the school record. His old team gave him 77 points. Resolved: the universe has a sense of humor.

Steele Pizzella took the keys with Gio Lopez not suited up and played like he owned the building. Twenty-three of 28 for 432 yards and three touchdowns, plus a 13-yard touchdown run, all in the first half. That is 495 yards of offense in 30 minutes, and we went to the locker room up 49-0. He hit Carlos Hernandez twice, from 38 and from 9, the second one capping a 96-yard drive. Kam Shanks caught a 30-yarder. Jack Foley caught six balls for 162. Ty Clark III, Jamar Searcy and Drayden Dickmann all ran one in.

The second half was a highlight reel with a soundtrack. Gannon Jones found Dickmann for an 87-yard touchdown. Shanks took a punt back 79 yards. Joshua Patterson intercepted a throw and ran 98 yards the other way. Ryan Henley finished it from a yard out. Eleven touchdowns in all. We threw for 546 yards, a new school record, and piled up 730 yards, 4 shy of the record set against Syracuse in 2017.

The stand I loved most? Merrimack got to our 9 in the third quarter and ran four plays, the last one a fourth down at the 1, and walked away with zero. That kept our first shutout in 11 years alive. The last one was a 3 to 0 grinder against Boston College, which tells you how rare this was. Merrimack went 3 of 18 on third down. Rushaun Tongue added an interception of his own.

Now the polite roast, because Debate Club demands it: 11 penalties for 115 yards is not a winning argument against anybody in the ACC. Sixth straight win, 8-1, and a game behind Miami in the league race.

Next stop is Gerald J. Ford Stadium in Dallas, Saturday, Nov. 14, at noon ET against SMU. Roll the Quad tonight. Pack the bus tomorrow. Go Deacs.

articles.title: Boston College vs Florida State: Eagles Fall Late, 31-24
articles.matchup: Final: Florida State (4-5) 31, Boston College (4-5) 24, Sat., Nov. 7, Alumni Stadium (Chestnut Hill, MA). Next: at Notre Dame, Sat., Nov. 14, Notre Dame Stadium, Notre Dame
articles.text:
Florida State 31, Boston College 24, on Veterans and Military Appreciation Day at Alumni Stadium, and before I argue anything, the 37,155 of us in Chestnut Hill rose to thank the men and women who served. That part of Saturday went exactly right. The football? Objection, your honor, and I have exhibits.

Exhibit A is the start. Bo MacCormack III ran 6 yards for a touchdown on our first drive, Luca Lombardo drilled a 48-yard field goal, and Mason McKenzie hit Nedrick Boldin Jr. for a 29-yard score. We led 17-7 in the second quarter, and the courtroom was ours.

Exhibit B is the last six minutes of the half. Amari Thomas went 20 yards for a Florida State score, and then the Seminoles lined up for a short field goal and the holder pitched it to the kicker, Gabe Panikowski, for a touchdown. A trick play, a fair one, and I hate it. Then Nehemiah Chandler intercepted McKenzie with seconds left. We went to the locker room down 21-17.

Exhibit C is pure joy. McKenzie got shaken up in the third quarter, came back the next series, and our whole offense spun in a circle before snapping it. He flipped an underhanded 2-yard touchdown to Javarius Green for a 24-21 lead. Marcus Upton had already intercepted Ashton Daniels and returned it 24 yards. For a few minutes, the jury was with us.

The verdict came late. Florida State tied it with a 22-yard field goal and then went 90 yards in 14 plays, and Thomas scored from 11 with 2:29 left. MacCormack finished with 105 yards on 16 carries. McKenzie went 15 of 27 for 166 yards and two touchdown throws. Bodie Kahoun made nine tackles and Charlie Comella eight.

We are 4-5 and 2-4 in the ACC, 3-2 at home. The appeal goes to Notre Dame Stadium next Saturday, Nov. 14. I'm filing it with the Court of Iced Coffee tonight, and I fully expect to lose again.

articles.title: Florida State vs Boston College: Fake FG Sparks 31-24 Win
articles.matchup: Final: Florida State (4-5) 31, Boston College (4-5) 24, Sat., Nov. 7, Alumni Stadium (Chestnut Hill, MA). Next: at Pittsburgh, Fri., Nov. 13, Acrisure Stadium, Pittsburgh
articles.text:
Florida State 31, Boston College 24, and the motion carries. While the Anhinga Music & Art Festival filled Lewis and Bloxham Parks in downtown Tallahassee with zydeco, food trucks and free admission on Saturday afternoon, our Seminoles were up in Chestnut Hill voting through the most important bill of the season: a road win, the first since Nov. 25, 2023.

Let the record show this was interim coach Rick Stockstill's first game, and the man who once played quarterback for Bobby Bowden called a game with some Bowden in it. Down 17-14 late in the half, we lined up for a short field goal. Holder Carter Jula flipped the ball back to kicker Gabe Panikowski, who caught it in stride and scored from a yard out. Motion to reconsider the scoreboard: granted, 21-17.

The opening session was rough. Boston College scored on its first drive and led 10-0, then 17-7. Ashton Daniels answered with a 4-yard touchdown run, and Amari Thomas ripped off a 20-yard score to get us within three. Nehemiah Chandler intercepted Mason McKenzie in the final seconds of the half and returned it 30 yards, and Ja'Bril Rawls intercepted another throw in the third.

Floor debate got tense after Boston College ran a spinning trick play for a 2-yard touchdown and a 24-21 lead. Panikowski tied it with a 22-yard field goal early in the fourth. Then came the vote that mattered: 90 yards in 14 plays, and Thomas bounced outside for an 11-yard touchdown with 2:29 left. Our defense held from there.

The committee report: Thomas ran 19 times for 98 yards and two scores. Daniels completed 15 of 26 for 178 yards with an interception and ran for 38. Micahi Danzy caught seven balls for 86 yards. Ashlynd Barker made 10 tackles and Chris Jones eight. We converted 8 of 14 third downs and ran for 202 yards.

We are 4-5 and 2-4 in the ACC, and bowl eligibility is still on the table. Next up is Pittsburgh at Acrisure Stadium on Friday night, Nov. 13. Gavel down. This session is adjourned with a win.

articles.title: Missouri vs Texas: Stripe Out Stung in the Fourth, 20-34
articles.matchup: Final: Texas Longhorns (7-2) 34, Missouri Tigers (6-3) 20, Sat., Nov. 7, Memorial Stadium, Columbia. Next: at Georgia, Sat., Nov. 14, Sanford Stadium, Athens
articles.text:
Missouri Tigers 20, Texas Longhorns 34. Final score 34-20 at Memorial Stadium, and 63,690 of us in the Stripe Out watched a 20-20 game slip away in the fourth quarter. Six and three now. Three and three in the SEC. Every section came dressed to its assigned stripe on Saturday morning in Columbia, and for three quarters Faurot Field looked and sounded like the place to be.

Breaking news, live from the press box: this defense showed up. Nicholas Rodriguez made 12 tackles. Santana Banner had 10. Cameron Keys and Trajen Greco each fell on a Texas fumble, and one of those turned into a Blake Craig field goal. Brunno Reus averaged 49.6 yards a punt and kept flipping the field.

The offense had its moments. Austin Simmons threw for 252 yards and two touchdowns. He found Brett Norfleet from 2 to open the scoring, and in the third, with the game knotted 13-13, Naeshaun Montgomery spun loose and tiptoed down the boundary for a 72-yard touchdown and a 20-13 lead. Craig hit from 22 and 48. Cayden Lee caught nine balls for 79.

Then the story turned. A Texas third-down incompletion at our 39 was ruled a fumble recovered by the Longhorns, the call stood after review, and three plays later Arch Manning hit Jermaine Bishop Jr. from 25 to tie it. Manning beat us down the boundary to Raleek Brown for the go-ahead score with 5:03 left. Our last real chance ended when a third-down throw for Lee got knocked into the air and Graceson Littleton came down with it. Brown ran in from 8 to finish the job.

Correction desk: we left points in the building. Craig missed two of his four field goal tries, we went 3 of 16 on third down, and Jamal Roberts, the SEC's leading rusher, was held to 66 yards on 19 carries. Those are headlines I never want to file again.

Next assignment: at Georgia, Saturday, Nov. 14, Sanford Stadium in Athens, kickoff time still to be set. Hard road, big stage, and a chance to rewrite this one. M-I-Z.

articles.title: Texas vs Missouri: Manning, Raleek Brown Close Out Columbia 34-20
articles.matchup: Final: Texas Longhorns (7-2) 34, Missouri Tigers (6-3) 20, Sat., Nov. 7, Memorial Stadium, Columbia. Next: at LSU, Sat., Nov. 14, Tiger Stadium, Baton Rouge
articles.text:
Texas Longhorns 34, Missouri Tigers 20. Final score 34-20 at Memorial Stadium, our first trip to Columbia since 2011, and we walked out 7-2, 4-2 in the SEC. Tied 20-20 heading into the fourth quarter, then we scored the last 14. One eyebrow, raised. Exactly according to plan.

Back on the Forty Acres on Saturday morning, the Cockrell School's World of Engineering open house had K-12 kids building their own flying rockets on campus. Arch Manning was in Missouri launching better ones. He went 28 of 38 for 297 yards and three touchdowns. A 24-yarder to Derrek Cooper answered Missouri's opening score. A 25-yarder to Jermaine Bishop Jr. tied it 20-20 late in the third. Then came the one I would frame for the boardroom, a lofted throw down the boundary to Raleek Brown, who ran right past a linebacker for a 23-yard touchdown and a 27-20 lead with 5:03 left.

The defense paid the dividend. Missouri got the ball back near midfield with about two minutes to go, a third-down throw got knocked into the air, and Graceson Littleton came down with it. Brown powered in from 8 with 1:25 left, and the deal was closed. He finished with 85 yards on the ground and two touchdowns. Rasheem Biles had six tackles, two breakups and three hurries, and Colton Vasek got home for a sack. Missouri went 3 of 16 on third down, and Jamal Roberts, the SEC's leading rusher, managed 66 yards.

Audit notes, because I keep books: we lost two fumbles, one of them handing Missouri a field goal, and Naeshaun Montgomery got loose for a 72-yard touchdown that put us down 20-13 in the third. A strange replay review on a third-down throw went our way right before Bishop's tying score. I will take it and count the rest as the cost of doing business on the road. Emmett Mosley V caught five for 85, and Gianni Spetic hit from 27 and 34. That is three straight wins since the back-to-back losses to Oklahoma and Florida.

LSU is next, Saturday, Nov. 14, at Tiger Stadium in Baton Rouge, kickoff time still to be set. Another set of Tigers, another road account to settle. Hook 'em.

articles.text:
Oklahoma 23, Florida 7, and the Swamp's 48-game winning streak against first-time visitors is gone. Across campus, GatorLAN was filling the Reitz Union with 50-plus competitive games for a free weekend of controller-mashing. I wish our offense had the same button combinations. And 90,442 of us watched the Sooners take a nap in our living room.

Reptile index time: Oklahoma's defense played like a snapping turtle, slow and patient, then all jaws. We got 203 yards and 11 first downs. Tramell Jones Jr. went 10 of 22 for 133 yards with two interceptions, and he was sacked three times. The one that hurt most came in the third quarter: down 13-7, fourth-and-3 from the Oklahoma 17, Jones threw across the field for Eric Courtland Jr., and Courtland Guillory closed in time to intercept it in the end zone.

The bright spot came off a punt. Bailey Stockton brought one back 31 yards, and Jadan Baugh cashed it in with a 15-yard run, stretching for the pylon on a play first ruled out of bounds. Replay fixed it. That was the only time the scoreboard lit up for us. Duke Clark caught four balls for 70 yards, including a 33-yarder in the flat, and Dallas Wilson grabbed four for 48.

Our defense deserves its flowers. Myles Graham made 15 tackles, a monster night, and Aaron Chiles added nine with two hurries. But Oklahoma ate 12:45 of clock on a 20-play, 89-yard drive that bridged the third and fourth quarters, and when the Sooners' kicker went three for three, the Swamp emptied early. A gopher tortoise moves faster than that drive, and it still beat us.

We went 2 of 9 on third down and 0 for 2 on fourth. The Sooners held the ball for 37:50. Those are the numbers, and I'm not dressing them up.

We're 5-4 and 3-4 in the SEC. Next is a trip to Kentucky on Saturday, Nov. 14, at Kroger Field in Lexington. Fresh week, fresh skin. Go Gators.

articles.title: Oklahoma vs Florida: Sooners Win First Swamp Trip 23-7
articles.matchup: Final: Oklahoma Sooners (5-4) 23, Florida Gators (5-4) 7, Sat., Nov. 7, Ben Hill Griffin Stadium, Gainesville. Next: vs. Ole Miss, Sat., Nov. 14, Memorial Stadium, Norman
articles.text:
Oklahoma 23, Florida 7. Boomer! (You know what to holler back.) While the Sam Noble Museum in Norman threw open its doors for a free day honoring our state, all science stations and red-dirt geology, our Sooners went to Gainesville and dug up some history of their own. Florida had won 48 straight home games against teams making their first trip to the Swamp. Make that had.

Our first visit to Ben Hill Griffin Stadium, 90,442 in the seats, and the defense rode it like a champion barrel horse. Florida managed 203 yards and 11 first downs. Courtland Guillory chased down a cross-field throw on fourth-and-3 from our 17 and intercepted it in the end zone with Florida down 13-7 in the third. Peyton Bowen grabbed another. Owen Heinecke made 10 tackles, and Kip Lewis and Danny Okoye each got a sack. The Gators went 2 of 9 on third down.

The offense had new hands on the play sheet this week, with Jason Witten calling it on an interim basis, and his fingerprints were on the whole first half. Tate Sandell opened with a 41-yard field goal after a 41-yard strike to our tight end. Then John Mateer faked a handoff, faked a reverse to Isaiah Sategna III and flipped it to a wide-open Hayden Hansen for a 3-yard score. Florida answered with a 15-yard Jadan Baugh run, but Sandell hit from 48 before the half. 13-7.

Then came the drive I want framed in the tack room. Twenty plays. 89 yards. 12 minutes and 45 seconds off the clock. Five third-down conversions. Mateer capped it with a 6-yard toss to Sategna with 4:56 left, and the Swamp began to empty. Sandell added a 31-yarder for three for three on the night. We held the ball for 37:50.

Mateer went 21 of 33 for 207 yards and two touchdowns, no interceptions, and ran 14 times for 56 more. Lloyd Avant carried 13 times for 47. Nobody will mistake it for a track meet. We had one play longer than 20 yards. It was tidy, tough and mistake-free: zero turnovers against two for Florida.

We're 5-4 and 3-3 in the SEC, and the Schooner gets to roll at home next. Ole Miss comes to Memorial Stadium in Norman on Saturday, Nov. 14. Saddle up, y'all. Sooner!

articles.title: Colorado State vs Boise State: Rams Buried by Broncos, 64-38
articles.matchup: Final: Boise State (8-1) 64, Colorado State (3-6) 38, Sat., Nov. 7, Canvas Stadium, Fort Collins. Next: at Washington State, Sat., Nov. 14, Martin Stadium, Pullman
articles.text:
Boise State 64, Colorado State 38. It was Snow Days week on campus, with a Rail Jam and Vendor Village outside Canvas Stadium before kickoff, and the forecast called for winter fun. What we got instead was a Bronco avalanche that started on the second snap and never stopped rolling downhill.

I'm a trail guy, so I'll tell it like a race. Boise went out at a sprint. Dylan Riley caught a short throw and ran 73 yards for a touchdown before most of us found our seats. Oliver Lundberg answered with a 9-yard touchdown run, and for one switchback it was 8-7. Then Boise scored on each of its next three drives, and it was 22-7 after one quarter.

Here is what I'll keep from the climb. Hauss Hejny never quit pushing the pace. He completed 14 of 25 for 253 yards and two touchdowns, hit Tommy Maher for a 13-yard score, found Terrence Smith Jr. for 18 more and ran 9 yards for one himself. He added 69 rushing yards. Maher caught six balls for 99 yards, and Cedric Ross hauled in a 65-yarder. K'saan Farrar threw a 7-yard touchdown to Lavon Brown in the last minute. We put up 513 yards, went 3 for 4 on fourth down and never gave the ball away.

The other side of the mountain is steep. Boise gained 669 yards, converted 5 of 7 third downs and punted once. Max Cutforth missed on three throws all night. Tre'Shawn Moore made 11 tackles, Oumar Diomande got a sack, and D'Mon Brinson had eight stops, but we never found the stop we needed to change the pace.

We are 3-6 and 1-4 in the Pac-12, and the series with Boise now stands at 1-14, the lone win still that 2023 night in this stadium when Dallin Holker caught the last-second heave. Next Saturday, Nov. 14, we head to Martin Stadium in Pullman to face Washington State. Mountain air, thick defense is still the plan. Tonight we got the mountain air part right.

The Broncos brought their own snowplow. We'll be ready with chains next time.

articles.title: Boise State vs Colorado State: Riley, Cutforth Roll 64-38
articles.matchup: Final: Boise State (8-1) 64, Colorado State (3-6) 38, Sat., Nov. 7, Canvas Stadium, Fort Collins. Next: vs. Oregon State, Sat., Nov. 14, Albertsons Stadium, Boise
articles.text:
Boise State 64, Colorado State 38, and if you heard a whoop from the Front Range on Saturday night, that was me. Earlier in the day back home, the Capital City Public Market filled The Grove Plaza downtown with makers and food stands from 10 to 2. By sundown in Fort Collins, our offense was setting up its own market, and everything was on sale.

Max Cutforth, filling in for the injured Maddux Madsen, did not play like anybody's fill-in. On our second snap he flipped it to Dylan Riley out of the backfield, and Riley went 73 yards to the end zone. Zeke Martinez even threw the two-point try to Matt Wagner, so we were up 8-0 before the popcorn cooled. Cutforth went 16 of 19 for 317 yards with four touchdown throws and snuck one in from a yard out himself. Rasean Jones caught six for 116 yards and a 35-yard score, and Terrious Favors and Matt Wagner caught touchdowns too.

Then there is Riley. One hundred ninety-two rushing yards on 19 carries, touchdown runs of 42 and 31 yards, 88 receiving yards and 300 all-purpose yards. He struck the Heisman pose after his third score, and friend, I'd have let him hold it till Tuesday. Harry Stewart III came in and ran for touchdowns from 43 and 6 yards just to make sure.

We scored touchdowns on our first four drives, punted once all night and piled up 669 yards, the eighth-most in program history. We converted 5 of 7 third downs and never gave the ball away. The defense gave up some yards, and Roman Tillmon led us with seven tackles while Logan Brantley broke up a throw.

That is eight straight wins since the opener in Eugene. We are 8-1, 5-0 in the Pac-12 and 4-1 on the road. Oregon State comes to Albertsons Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 14, and the turf has never looked bluer. Bring sunglasses, Beavers.
