articles.title: Utah vs BYU: Dampier, Four Interceptions Keep Utes Perfect 28-20
articles.matchup: Final: BYU Cougars (7-2) 20, Utah Utes (9-0) 28, Sat., Nov. 7, Rice-Eccles Stadium, Salt Lake City. Next: at Arizona, Sat., Nov. 14, Casino Del Sol Stadium, Tucson
articles.text:
Utah Utes 28, BYU Cougars 20, and Rice-Eccles Stadium was a wall of red on Saturday morning in Salt Lake City. Final score 28-20. It was our Red Out and Military Appreciation game, the 101st sellout in a row, and 52,901 of us in red watched four BYU throws land in Ute hands. Nine and oh. Six and oh in the Big 12. Three straight losses to the Cougars in this rivalry, erased.

We came out of the gate flying. Devon Dampier hit Noah Bennee for 47 on the first drive and took it in himself from 22. Next possession, Dampier found Braden Pegan in stride for a 46-yard touchdown, and we were up 14-0 before the game was five minutes old. On a day built to honor the folks who serve, the opening salute came early.

Then the snowpack slid the wrong way. We put the ball on the ground twice before halftime, BYU kicked two field goals, Bear Bachmeier found Legend Glasker for 75, and LJ Martin walked in from 4. Down 20-14 at the break in our own building. That halftime felt like a chairlift stuck in a whiteout.

The second half belonged to the defense: a shutout, with the Cougars held to 111 yards after the break, per the AP. Dampier hit Pegan from 14 late in the third for a 21-20 lead, then ran it in from 3 with 12:03 left for 28-20. He even caught one, a 29-yarder from receiver Creed Whittemore, his first catch as a Ute. Two touchdown throws, two touchdown runs, 266 yards of offense. Our quarterback ran the whole course.

And the gates BYU could not clear? Lance Holtzclaw intercepted Bachmeier. James Chenault Jr. intercepted him. With the Cougars at our 2, Trey Reynolds intercepted him in the end zone with 4:39 to go, and Nate Ritchie grabbed the last one in the end zone on the final drive. Four interceptions, four different Utes. Johnathan Hall led us with nine tackles.

Honest grade: three sacks allowed, two lost fumbles, and Dillon Curtis missed his only field goal try. Arizona is next, Saturday, Nov. 14, in Tucson, kickoff time still to be set. Wax the skis. Go Utes.

BYU got a halftime lead. We got the second half, four interceptions and the rivalry back.

articles.title: BYU vs Utah: Four Interceptions Sink the Cougars, 20-28
articles.matchup: Final: BYU Cougars (7-2) 20, Utah Utes (9-0) 28, Sat., Nov. 7, Rice-Eccles Stadium, Salt Lake City. Next: vs Baylor, Sat., Nov. 14, LaVell Edwards Stadium, Provo
articles.text:
BYU Cougars 20, Utah Utes 28. Final score 28-20 at Rice-Eccles Stadium, and the three-game streak we carried into this rivalry is done. We led 20-14 at halftime in Salt Lake City and did not score again. Seven and two now, four and two in the Big 12, and a long, quiet drive back down to Provo.

Back home on Saturday night, BYU's student cast was singing The Music Man in Concert on the Mainstage Theatre in the Arts Building, with a live orchestra and all seventy-six trombones. Up north, our afternoon had its own parade. Four interceptions marched straight into Ute hands, and no band in Utah County could have drowned that out.

The first half was a ride worth taking. Down 14-0 before five minutes were gone, nobody on our side blinked. Matthias Dunn hit from 31 and 38. Our defense came up with two Utah fumbles. Bear Bachmeier hit Legend Glasker in stride for a 75-yard touchdown, and LJ Martin, back from injury, ran in untouched from 4 for a 20-14 lead. Bodie Schoonover lived in their backfield with two sacks and three tackles for loss, and Cade Uluave added a third sack.

Then the trail washed out. Bachmeier finished with 272 yards through the air and ran for 59 more, but three of his four interceptions came after the break. Braden Pegan caught a 14-yarder late in the third to put Utah up 21-20, and Devon Dampier ran in from 3 for 28-20 with 12:03 left. We marched to the Utah 2 and Trey Reynolds intercepted Bachmeier in the end zone with 4:39 to go. We got back to the Utah 41 on the last drive, and Nate Ritchie took that one in the end zone too.

Glasker caught seven for 118. Walker Lyons caught seven for 97. We won time of possession and still lost the day, because four giveaways and 11 flags for 80 yards will beat you in any rivalry, let alone this one.

Baylor comes to LaVell Edwards Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 14, kickoff time still to be set. Trail-guide dad joke of the week: all we should be handing out at Edwards is a warm welcome. Yes, it squeaked. Go Cougs.

articles.title: Northwestern vs Iowa: Wildcats' First Ryan Field Loss, 24-10
articles.matchup: Final: Iowa (7-2) 24, Northwestern (6-3) 10, Sat., Nov. 7, Ryan Field, Evanston. Next: at Ohio State, Sat., Nov. 14, Ohio Stadium, Columbus
articles.text:
Iowa 24, Northwestern 10. Footnote one: this is the first loss in the history of the new Ryan Field, and I would like it noted that the stadium itself played beautifully. The Great Chicago Food Festival opened at 4:30, the Great Big Ten Grillout fired up, and 31,151 of us showed up hungry for a sixth home win. We left with full stomachs and nothing else.

Data first, feelings later. We converted 1 of 11 third downs. We went 1 for 4 on fourth down, including two stops on fourth-and-1. We ran 37 times for 105 yards. Iowa did not let us inside its 26-yard marker until the fourth quarter. Those numbers are the whole investigation, and I will still write the 2,000 words.

articles.title: Iowa vs Northwestern: Hawkeyes Win in Evanston Again, 24-10
articles.matchup: Final: Iowa (7-2) 24, Northwestern (6-3) 10, Sat., Nov. 7, Ryan Field, Evanston. Next: vs. Purdue, Sat., Nov. 14, Kinnick Stadium, Iowa City
articles.text:
Iowa 24, Northwestern 10, and I'm sitting here in my one black-and-gold sweater grinning like a man who just got the corn in before the rain. Saturday morning in Iowa City, folks hauled their leftover jack-o'-lanterns to Chauncey Swan Park for Jack SPLAT!, watching them dropped off the parking ramp and splattered for the compost pile. By Saturday night our defense was doing the same thing to the Northwestern offense in Evanston.

Hank Brown started it like a man with somewhere to be. He went 4 for 4 on the opening drive and then ran a quarterback draw 21 yards for the touchdown. Our next score was a 97-yard drive, helped along by a 45-yard L.J. Phillips Jr. run, and Brown capped it with a 24-yard throw to Tony Diaz early in the second quarter. That was 14-0 and plenty of breathing room.

Now let me talk about the part of football I love most. Northwestern finally kicked a 45-yard field goal late in the third, and Braeden Jackson took the very next kickoff 96 yards to the house. That is his second kickoff return touchdown this season, and I nearly sent the lamp flying. Caden Buhr followed with a 52-yard field goal, and it was 24-3.

The defense is the reason I still sleep at night. Northwestern converted 1 of 11 third downs and 1 of 4 fourth downs, ran for 2.8 yards a carry, and did not get inside our 26 until the fourth quarter. Cam Buffington made 12 tackles, Jayden Montgomery had nine with a sack, and Bryce Hawthorne got a sack of his own.

Phillips had his best day in black and gold, 128 yards on 21 carries. Brown finished 16 of 21 for 126 yards with a touchdown, a score on the ground and one interception. We lost a fumble too, so the coaches will have plenty to say on Monday. Fair enough.

That is five straight wins against Northwestern and the first loss anybody has handed the Wildcats in their new stadium. We are 7-2 and 4-2 in the Big Ten, and Purdue comes to Kinnick Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 14. I'll be wearing the sweater. My wife has stopped asking.

articles.title: Houston vs Cincinnati: Sanford's Dash Wins Homecoming 31-24
articles.matchup: Final: Houston Cougars (7-2) 31, Cincinnati Bearcats (5-4) 24, Sat., Nov. 7, TDECU Stadium, Houston. Next: at Colorado, Fri., Nov. 13, 10:15 PM ET, Folsom Field, Boulder
articles.text:
Houston 31, Cincinnati 24, and Homecoming at TDECU Stadium has a happy landing. The Cougars came off the bye to host the Bearcats in front of 32,372, and we got the program's first win against Cincinnati since 2016, plus its first home win against them since 2015. Mission control, you may exhale now.

Liftoff was instant. Conner Weigman found Amare Thomas for an 8-yard score, then for 31 more, and we were up 14-0 before the first quarter was half gone. Thomas finished with six catches for 78 yards and both touchdowns. Weigman went 17 of 24 for 227 yards with no interceptions and added a 2-yard keeper in the second quarter, 21-10 at the break.

Then the Bearcats got their thrusters working. JC French IV threw two scores and ran in another, and with 6:21 left it was 24-24. Houston, we had a problem. That's when Re'Shaun Sanford II hit the hole, slipped between two defenders and outran the entire secondary for a 51-yard touchdown with 5:10 to go. Sanford finished with 126 yards on 15 carries, and Makhi Hughes added 90 on 12. We ran for 241 yards at 6.9 a pop. That is escape velocity.

The final stage separation came on replay. Cincinnati reached our 42, French threw a swing toss that officials first ruled incomplete, then a review called it a backward toss, and Christian Brathwaite was credited with the recovery with 2:11 left. From there the offense ran out the clock, and Homecoming was ours.

Honest flight review: the defense bent plenty. Cincinnati ran 71 plays, piled up 30 first downs and converted 9 of 14 third downs. Jaden Yates led us with nine tackles, Ashton Porter had six, and Jalen Mayo, Kentrell Webb and Jordan Allen each broke up a throw. Allen was also ejected for targeting on the fourth-quarter hit that sent Cincinnati's JV Gibson off on a cart, and we are praying for JV's recovery.

We're 7-2 and 4-2 in the Big 12, and the title chase is still on. Next is a Friday night trip to Colorado, Nov. 13, at 10:15 PM ET at Folsom Field in Boulder. Pack the oxygen. Go Coogs.

articles.title: Cincinnati vs Houston: Bearcats Rally, Fall Late 24-31
articles.matchup: Final: Houston Cougars (7-2) 31, Cincinnati Bearcats (5-4) 24, Sat., Nov. 7, TDECU Stadium, Houston. Next: at Iowa State, Sat., Nov. 14, Jack Trice Stadium, Ames
articles.text:
Houston 31, Cincinnati 24, and that's a plain-spaghetti night, no cheese, no onions. Back in Cincinnati, the MakeUC hackathon opened at the 1819 Innovation Hub on Reading Road at 9 a.m., a 31-hour build sprint that runs into Sunday afternoon. Those engineers will ship a working build by then. Our Bearcats built a beautiful comeback in Houston and ran out of clock before the final test.

The first quarter was a bug report. Conner Weigman hit Amare Thomas for 8 yards and then for 31, and we were down 14-0 before we found the on switch. Then JC French IV went to work. He found Cole Tabb for a 17-yard score, Stephen Rusnak knocked in a 28-yarder, and after Weigman ran one in from 2 we answered in the third with French to Gavin Grover for 34. That made it 21-17.

Down 24-17 in the fourth, French finished a drive himself from a yard out with 6:21 left. Tied 24-24. That's a five-way drive, onions and beans. And 71 seconds later, Re'Shaun Sanford II split two defenders and ran 51 yards to the house. We got back to the Houston 42, and then a swing throw from French was ruled a backward toss on replay, Houston fell on it with 2:11 to go, and the Cougars ran out the clock.

The bigger moment came earlier in that quarter. JV Gibson took a hit in the end zone on a slant with 6:59 left, lay still for a few moments and was carted off. The Houston safety was flagged for targeting and ejected. The AP reported JV was moving all four limbs and went to the hospital for precautionary tests. He caught five balls for 54 yards before that. Every Bearcat is praying for him tonight, and so am I.

The chart, because I chart it all: we ran 71 plays, piled up 30 first downs, held the ball for 33:38 and went 9 of 14 on third down. French went 19 of 30 for 217 yards and two touchdowns with no interceptions. Gi'Bran Payne ran for 71 yards and Tabb for 60. Jasper Beeler led the defense with eight tackles. The problem is that Houston ran for 241 yards at 6.9 a carry, and that math doesn't close.

We're 5-4 and 2-4 in the Big 12, one win from bowl eligibility, with a trip to Iowa State on Saturday, Nov. 14, at Jack Trice Stadium in Ames. I'm upgrading back to a three-way the minute we get it. Down the drive, Bearcats.

articles.title: Ohio State vs Oregon: Buckeyes Blow 14-0 Lead, Fall 41-28
articles.matchup: Final: Oregon (6-3) 41, Ohio State (6-3) 28, Sat., Nov. 7, Ohio Stadium, Columbus. Next: vs. Northwestern, Sat., Nov. 14, Ohio Stadium, Columbus
articles.text:
Oregon 41, Ohio State 28, and that's a Columbus problem I can't run away from. The call went out to Scarlet the Shoe, our Buckeyes wore the all-scarlet Scarlet Rush uniforms for the first time since 2024, and 103,551 of us turned Ohio Stadium red. For a quarter it was the prettiest picture in the country.

Bo Jackson ran 16 yards for a touchdown, then 8 more for another, and we led 14-0 with 1:20 left in the first. I ran a victory route down the press box hallway. That was premature. Oregon converted a fake punt on fourth-and-9, scored with 1:25 left in the half, intercepted Luke Fahey at its own 41 and scored again as the half ended. A 14-3 lead turned into a 17-14 deficit in the last 1:25 of the half.

The third quarter hurt the most. Dierre Hill Jr. broke a 48-yard touchdown run on Oregon's first drive, Dakorien Moore made a one-handed catch in the corner for 11 more, and Brandon Smith took a screen 15 yards early in the fourth. Thirty-eight straight points for the Ducks, and a lot of scarlet headed for the exits.

Route Tree segment, because some of our guys deserve the film. Jeremiah Smith caught seven balls for 133 yards and a 13-yard touchdown. Devin McCuin had nine catches for 84. Fahey, in his second start, completed 36 of 50 for 360 yards, two touchdown throws and the interception, and he ran in a two-point try himself. Nate Roberts caught a 15-yard score with 44 seconds left. Earl Little Jr. made 10 tackles.

The honest part: 53 rushing yards on 21 carries, 0 for 4 on fourth down, and back-to-back losses for the first time since 2011. Nobody in Columbus needs a candy fine to feel that one.

We are 6-3 and 4-2 in the Big Ten. Northwestern comes to the Shoe on Saturday, Nov. 14, for Military Appreciation Day, and we owe this crowd a whole lot better than the last three quarters. Go Bucks.

articles.title: Oregon vs Ohio State: Ducks Erase 14-0 Hole, Stun Bucks 41-28
articles.matchup: Final: Oregon (6-3) 41, Ohio State (6-3) 28, Sat., Nov. 7, Ohio Stadium, Columbus. Next: vs. Michigan, Sat., Nov. 14, Autzen Stadium, Eugene
articles.text:
Oregon 41, Ohio State 28, and the Horseshoe went from a sea of scarlet to a sea of empty seats. Back home, the Eugene Saturday Market packed the Park Blocks at 8th and Oak one of the last Saturdays of its season, all handmade everything. Our Ducks spent the same afternoon in Columbus stitching together the comeback of the year.

Uniform of the week first, because it's the law. The new Mummy Duck combo, chrome helmets with dark green wings, white jerseys, black pants and bandage-wrap sleeves, against an all-scarlet stadium? Ten out of ten. The first quarter, though, looked like a model tripping on the runway. Bo Jackson scored from 16 and from 8, and we were down 14-0.

Then the tailoring started. Gage Hurych hit a 33-yard field goal. On fourth-and-9, linebacker Teitum Tuioti took a fake punt snap and found Matayo Uiagalelei for 30 yards, and six plays later Dierre Hill Jr. scored from 9. Devin Jackson intercepted Luke Fahey at our 41, and tight end Jamari Johnson plunged in from 2 to end the half. That was 17 points in the second quarter and a 17-14 lead.

Hill opened the third by cutting right and breaking free for a 48-yard touchdown. Dylan Raiola found Dakorien Moore with a one-handed 11-yard catch in the back corner, then hit Brandon Smith on a 15-yard screen early in the fourth. Thirty-eight straight points. Ohio State scored twice late, and Hurych added a 40-yarder in between.

The fit check: Raiola was 25 of 40 for 257 yards, two touchdown throws and no turnovers. Hill ran 13 times for 75 yards and two scores, and Moore caught seven balls. Devon Jackson made eight tackles with three behind the scrimmage mark, and we stopped the Buckeyes on all four of their fourth-down tries. A clean sheet on giveaways, too.

Final review: 10 out of 10, uniform AND execution. We are 6-3 and 4-2 in the Big Ten. Michigan visits Autzen Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 14, and I am already steaming the jerseys.

articles.title: Minnesota vs UCLA: Two Long Strikes Sink the Gophers 20-34
articles.matchup: Final: UCLA Bruins (9-0) 34, Minnesota Golden Gophers (5-4) 20, Sat., Nov. 7, Huntington Bank Stadium, Minneapolis. Next: at Penn State, Sat., Nov. 14, 7:00 PM ET, Beaver Stadium, University Park
articles.text:
UCLA 34, Minnesota 20. It was 44 degrees at kickoff for Salute to Service at Huntington Bank Stadium, where fan donations bought tickets for active and veteran service members and their families, and Gopher Athletics matched every one. We rowed together at 10:58 like always, 43,841 strong. For more than three quarters, we had the unbeaten Bruins in a real fight.

It opened rough, and I won't pretend otherwise. Luke Drzewiecki lined up a 56-yarder on fourth-and-2 in the first quarter and missed wide right, ending his FBS-best run of 26 straight made field goals. UCLA went the other way and Wayne Knight scored from a yard. Down 10-0. Any ice fisherman knows the one that slips off the hook teaches you the most, and that kicker has earned all the grace in the world.

articles.title: UCLA vs Minnesota: Mizell Goes 75 Twice, Bruins Win 34-20
articles.matchup: Final: UCLA Bruins (9-0) 34, Minnesota Golden Gophers (5-4) 20, Sat., Nov. 7, Huntington Bank Stadium, Minneapolis. Next: vs. Illinois, Fri., Nov. 13, 9:00 PM ET, Rose Bowl, Pasadena
articles.text:
UCLA 34, Minnesota 20, and the Bruins are 9-0. Back in Westwood on Saturday, the James Bridges Theater in Melnitz Hall, where I spend most of my waking life, staged Stories That Heal, a one-night benefit of short scenes and monologues. Fitting, because Ty Dieffenbach spent the morning in Minneapolis shooting two one-scene features of his own, each exactly 75 yards long.

Act one opened at 9 a.m. Los Angeles time in 44-degree air, and the Gophers blinked first. Mateen Bhaghani hit from 37, then Minnesota's kicker missed a 56-yarder wide right on fourth-and-2, ending his FBS-best run of 26 straight makes. Dieffenbach kept it on a read-option for 18, swung it to Wayne Knight for 28, and Knight finished from a yard out. 10-0.

Act two dragged. Darius Taylor ran one in from 3, the Gophers banged a 38-yarder through as the half expired, and it was 10-10. Act three was a reshoot of act one: another 56-yard try sailed wide right, Knight bolted 31 yards around the right side on the next snap, and three plays later Noah Fox-Flores caught a 27-yard score. Then Drake Lindsey found freshman tight end George Rohl from 4, and it was 17-17 with 12:50 left in the fourth.

Here is the storyboard I will frame. Nine seconds of game clock after that tie, Dieffenbach launched it deep and Aidan Mizell, the Florida transfer, outran everybody for a 75-yard touchdown. Minnesota kicked a field goal to make it 24-20. Ten seconds later, same quarterback, same receiver, same 75 yards. Two one-play drives, 150 yards, game. Bhaghani added a 36-yarder to close the credits.

Dieffenbach finished 8 of 16 for a career-high 303 yards and three touchdowns, though he threw an interception and lost a fumble. Knight ran for 109 yards on 18 carries and his 15th score of the season. On defense, Jalen Woods made 11 tackles, and Scooter Jackson intercepted Lindsey and broke up two more throws. The Gophers went 4 of 15 on third down.

Unbeaten at 9-0 and 6-0 in the Big Ten, with the cold-weather road trip in the can. Illinois comes to the Rose Bowl on Friday, Nov. 13, at 9 PM ET, beneath the lights and the palm trees. Cut, print, and send the whole reel to Pasadena.

articles.title: LSU vs Alabama: Tigers Stall on Fourth Down, Fall 31-13
articles.matchup: Final: Alabama Crimson Tide (7-2) 31, LSU Tigers (6-3) 13, Sat., Nov. 7, Tiger Stadium, Baton Rouge. Next: vs. Texas, Sat., Nov. 14, Tiger Stadium, Baton Rouge
articles.text:
Alabama 31, LSU 13, and the 750th home game in LSU football history ended with 102,321 of us filing out of Tiger Stadium in the daylight. It was the last meeting with the Tide as permanent SEC opponents, the 63rd straight season of it, and Lil' Nathan & The Zydeco Big Timers were playing the Fan Zone in front of the PMAC at 11 a.m. Cher, the zydeco won its matchup. We did not win ours.

So here is my gumbo of grief, every ingredient real. The roux: 0 for 4 on fourth down. Chuck McDonald III batted down Sam Leavitt's throw on fourth-and-4 from the Tide 10. Our kicker missed from 56. Luke Metz intercepted Leavitt at the Alabama 24. We went to the half down 10-3 after Ryan Coleman-Williams slipped in from a yard.

Then the third quarter gave us a taste of the good stuff. Our kicker drilled a 41-yarder, and Dilin Jones capped an 11-play, 90-yard drive with a 5-yard run. Tigers 13, Tide 10, with 2:44 left in the quarter, and Death Valley shaking like a pot at full boil. Alabama needed 2:08 to answer. Rico Scott took the first snap 57 yards to our 18, and Keelon Russell found Josh Ford for 7.

The cayenne nobody asked for: fourth-and-10 at our own 25 with about eight minutes left, we went for it, Leavitt was sacked, and three plays later Russell hit Kaleb Edwards from 4. Cederian Morgan had already caught a 25-yard score. Eugene Wilson III lost a fumble, and right tackle Weston Davis was helped off in the third quarter.

And still, Leavitt was tough as a cast-iron pot: 35 of 47 for 380 yards. Jackson Harris caught 11 balls for 166, Trey'Dez Green grabbed 10 for 85, and we outgained Alabama by 172 yards. TJ Dottery made nine tackles, every one of them by himself, and Ty Benefield and DJ Pickett each got a sack. Yards were never the problem. Points were.

We're 6-3 and 3-3 in the SEC. Texas comes to Tiger Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 14. No brass-band parade tonight and no beignets handed around the room, just a long simmer and a new roux next week. Geaux Tigers.

articles.title: Alabama vs LSU: Russell's Three Scores Close Out Tigers 31-13
articles.matchup: Final: Alabama Crimson Tide (7-2) 31, LSU Tigers (6-3) 13, Sat., Nov. 7, Tiger Stadium, Baton Rouge. Next: at Vanderbilt, Sat., Nov. 14, 12:45 PM ET, FirstBank Stadium, Nashville
articles.text:
Alabama 31, LSU 13, and that is Roll Tide in the satisfied tone, the low one I save for Tiger Stadium. Back home, across the Black Warrior River in Historic Downtown Northport, Canebrake's Porchella turned front porches into stages from noon to 5, so Tuscaloosa County had live music right up to kickoff. In Baton Rouge, 102,321 people got a different concert, and the Tide conducted the finale.

This one was won on fourth down. LSU went 0 for 4 there. Chuck McDonald III swatted Sam Leavitt's throw on fourth-and-4 from our 10, and Luke Metz intercepted Leavitt at our 24 and brought it back 28 yards. Metz finished with 11 tackles, Bray Hubbard and Red Morgan made nine apiece, and Caleb Woodson added eight. When the Tigers went for it on fourth-and-10 from their own 25 with about eight minutes left, the rush got home for the sack.

Conor Talty opened the scoring from 43, and Ryan Coleman-Williams took a misdirection around right end from a yard out for a 10-3 halftime lead. Then LSU punched back with a 41-yard field goal and a 90-yard drive, and for 2:08 of game clock we trailed 13-10. My horse would have bolted. Our quarterback did not.

Keelon Russell pushed through an ankle injury, was examined in the medical tent in the third quarter, and came back to throw three touchdowns. Rico Scott turned the first snap of the answer into a 57-yard catch-and-run to the LSU 18, and Russell hit Josh Ford from 7 with 36 seconds left in the third. In the fourth he found Cederian Morgan from 25, then Kaleb Edwards from 4 three plays after that fourth-down sack. Seventeen of 24, 206 yards, no interceptions, no fumbles. Twenty-one straight points to finish.

The honest part: LSU outgained us by 172 yards and ran 28 more plays. We ran for 79 yards on 29 carries and went 3 of 11 on third down. Alex Asparuhov averaged 49.8 yards on five punts and kept the Tigers backed up. Zero turnovers and four fourth-down stops fix a lot of problems.

That is seven wins in our last eight trips to Tiger Stadium, per the AP, in the final meeting with LSU as a permanent SEC opponent. We're 7-2 and 5-2 in the SEC. Next is a trip to Vanderbilt on Saturday, Nov. 14, at 12:45 PM ET at FirstBank Stadium in Nashville. Roll Tide, tone number eleven.

articles.title: Tennessee vs Kentucky: Dark Mode Vols Rule Homecoming, 34-6
articles.matchup: Final: Tennessee (7-2) 34, Kentucky (7-2) 6, Sat., Nov. 7, Neyland Stadium, Knoxville. Next: at Texas A&M, Sat., Nov. 14, Kyle Field, College Station
articles.text:
(Plink-a-plink.) Tennessee 34, Kentucky 6, on Homecoming night, with the Vols dressed in their new adidas Dark Mode jerseys for the first time and 101,915 of us singing in Neyland Stadium. The theme this year was "All Roads Lead to Tennessee." On Saturday night every road led straight to a checkerboard end zone, and Kentucky could not find the exit ramp.

Daune Morris set the tone with the run I will be humming all week, 66 yards right up the gut with 56 seconds left in the first quarter. Before that, Dejuan Lane intercepted Kenny Minchey in our end zone. That is two drives, two big plays, and a ranked visitor already looking for its map.

As an old long snapper, I appreciate a night built on field goals, and Cooper Ranvier hit from 48 and 39 to keep the scoreboard moving while the offense found its feet. Kentucky reached our red zone twice and left with two field goals. Qua Moss jarred the ball loose from Jovantae Barnes in the second quarter, and Kayin Lee pounced on it.

Then the fourth quarter got loud. Moss sacked Minchey in the last minute of the third, the ball came out, and Mariyon Dye scooped it and ran 11 yards to the Kentucky 36. On the next snap, Faizon Brandon threw 24 yards to Mike Matthews for a 20-6 lead. Arion Carter sacked Minchey on fourth down after that, and DeSean Bishop scored twice from 5 yards out to make it 34-6.

Arion Carter was the whole band tonight: 13 tackles, two sacks and four tackles for loss. Jeremiah Telander made 10 tackles and Edwin Spillman nine. Bishop carried 25 times for 109 yards and two scores, and Morris finished with 85 yards on five carries. George MacIntyre completed 9 of 14 for 125 yards without a turnover, and Braylon Staley caught four for 50. We forced three takeaways and gave the ball away zero times.

That is 7-2, 4-2 in the SEC and 5-1 at home. Next Saturday, Nov. 14, we head to Texas A&M and Kyle Field. I tuned the banjo on purpose tonight, folks. Rocky Top sounded just right.

articles.title: Kentucky vs Tennessee: Wildcats' Streak Ends in 34-6 Loss
articles.matchup: Final: Tennessee (7-2) 34, Kentucky (7-2) 6, Sat., Nov. 7, Neyland Stadium, Knoxville. Next: vs. Florida, Sat., Nov. 14, Kroger Field, Lexington
articles.text:
Tennessee 34, Kentucky 6, and I have spent the drive home from Knoxville staring at the white fences along I-75. Back in Lexington on Saturday, the Vintage Market Days crowd filled the Alltech Arena at the Kentucky Horse Park, hunting for antiques. Down in Neyland Stadium, our Wildcats found old problems instead: turnovers, red-zone stalls and a fourth quarter that got away from us.

The bloodlines showed up early. Our second drive started at our own 44 and reached Tennessee territory, and then a Kenny Minchey throw into the end zone was intercepted by Dejuan Lane for a touchback. Late in the first, Daune Morris broke a 66-yard touchdown run right up the middle, and we were chasing from there.

We stayed in the race for a long while. Adam Zouagui hit from 43 and then from 25 with nine seconds left in the half, and it was 10-6 at the break. Twice we reached the red zone and twice we came away with three. Midway through the second quarter, Jovantae Barnes ripped off 15 yards and had the ball knocked loose at our 48, and Tennessee kicked a field goal off it.

The final furlong was rough. With 36 seconds left in the third, Minchey was sacked and fumbled, Tennessee fell on it at our 36, and one play into the fourth Faizon Brandon threw a 24-yard touchdown. Arion Carter sacked Minchey on fourth down on the next drive, and DeSean Bishop ran in twice from 5 yards to finish it.

The honest grading sheet: Minchey completed 26 of 34 for 224 yards with the interception and was sacked repeatedly, finishing with minus-1 rushing yard. Willie Rodriguez caught six balls for 81 yards and Kenny Darby seven for 69. We held the ball for 35:17, but went 6 of 14 on third down and 0 for 2 on fourth. Ty Bryant had nine tackles and Elijah Barnes seven, and Mi'Quise Humphrey-Grace got a sack on George MacIntyre.

Our six-game winning streak is done, and so is the polite part of my evening. We are 7-2, and Florida comes to Kroger Field on Saturday, Nov. 14. A good horse that loses a race goes back to the barn, eats its oats and runs again the next week. Blue blood does not quit in November.

articles.title: Notre Dame vs Miami: Carr and Talich Topple No. 1 Canes 31-24
articles.matchup: Final: Notre Dame Fighting Irish (8-1) 31, Miami Hurricanes (8-1) 24, Sat., Nov. 7, Notre Dame Stadium, Notre Dame. Next: vs. Boston College, Sat., Nov. 14, 3:30 PM ET, Notre Dame Stadium, Notre Dame
articles.text:
Notre Dame 31, Miami 24, and I would posit that 77,622 people have rarely been this loud in Notre Dame Stadium. The night honored the late Lou Holtz: captains from his teams, among them Tony Rice, Byron Spruell and Ricky Watters, presented the flags, and the band saluted him at halftime and again during the 1812 Overture. His 1988 Irish beat No. 1 Miami 31-30 in this building. Thirty-eight years later, the Irish took down the top-ranked Hurricanes again with 31.

Tonight's thesis: CJ Carr was the best quarterback in the stadium. Exhibit A is 29 of 40 for 319 yards, three touchdowns and zero interceptions. He found Jordan Faison for a toe-tapping 27-yard score in the right corner, hit Micah Gilbert on an 18-yard slant with 29 seconds left in the half, and found Gilbert again from 20 two plays after Faison's 56-yard punt return. Gilbert finished with nine catches for 98 yards. It was 24-3 early in the third.

Then Miami scored twice in a hurry, it was 24-17, and my sweater vest needed air. Enter Luke Talich, who undercut a deep out and intercepted Darian Mensah at our 49. On fourth-and-2 at the Miami 43, Carr found Nolan James Jr. split wide for 36 yards, and James finished it from a yard out. That was the deciding possession, and I will defend that claim before any committee.

Spencer Porath's 53-yard try came up short, Miami drove to our 22, and on fourth down Mensah threw to the end zone. Elija Lofton had it with two feet down. Talich ripped it out. Motion carried. James then ran six straight times to burn the Hurricanes' timeouts, Jasper Scaife punted 50 yards, and Boubacar Traore and Bryce Young shared the sack that sealed it.

Footnotes for the defense: the second-quarter stand at our own 1, where Jaiden Ausberry and Traore dropped Mensah for a 3-yard loss and held Miami to a field goal. Kyngstonn Viliamu-Asa added a sack and two tackles for loss. Ausberry and Adon Shuler made nine tackles apiece, and Christian Gray broke up two throws. No turnovers on our side, two on theirs.

That is the program's 10th win against a No. 1 team, per Notre Dame Athletics. We're 8-1. Boston College visits Notre Dame Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 14, at 3:30 PM ET. The defense rests, and Coach Holtz got his tribute the right way.

articles.title: Miami vs Notre Dame: Canes Rally Falls Short in South Bend 24-31
articles.matchup: Final: Notre Dame Fighting Irish (8-1) 31, Miami Hurricanes (8-1) 24, Sat., Nov. 7, Notre Dame Stadium, Notre Dame. Next: vs. Duke, Sat., Nov. 14, 12:00 PM ET, Hard Rock Stadium, Miami Gardens
articles.text:
Notre Dame 31, Miami 24, and the unbeaten ride ended in South Bend on a 40-degree night. Back home in Coral Gables, the Frost Musical Theatre Ensemble raised the curtain on Page to Stage at Gusman Concert Hall at 7:30, the same minute our Canes kicked off. The campus show got its happy ending. Ours in Indiana did not, and my sunglasses went on indoors before halftime.

The first half felt like somebody else's team. We had first-and-goal at the Irish 1 in the second quarter, ran it three times, lost three yards on the last one and settled for a 19-yard Jake Weinberg field goal. CJ Carr hit Jordan Faison for 27 yards and Micah Gilbert for 18 with 29 seconds left, and we walked into the locker room down 17-3. Gilbert scored again from 20 early in the third. 24-3. Silence in my living room.

Then the U remembered who it was. Darian Mensah found Elija Lofton for a 12-yard score, then Cooper Barkate for 12 more, and it was 24-17 with 5:29 left in the third. Mensah to Barkate, it's never too late! Luke Talich jumped a deep out to stop the surge, the Irish converted a fourth down for 36 yards, and Nolan James Jr. plunged in. We answered anyway: Mensah to Barkate from a yard out, 31-24 with 9:53 to go.

You know the rest, and I wish I didn't. Fourth down, 3:36 left, Mensah threw for the corner, and Lofton came down with both feet in and the ball in his hands. Talich tore it loose, the officials ruled no catch, and Notre Dame ran the clock down to about a minute. A sack ended the last drive, and a hook-and-lateral on the final snap bounced away on the turf.

The honest film: Mensah threw for 276 yards and three touchdowns with one interception. Barkate caught 10 balls for 92 yards and two scores, Lofton grabbed seven for 113, and Mohamed Toure made 12 tackles. We ran for just 101 yards, went 6 of 14 on third down and gave it away twice while Notre Dame never did. We also played the whole night without injured receiver Malachi Toney, and the red zone felt every inch of that.

We're 8-1 and still 6-0 in the ACC, and that is the race that decides where December goes. Duke comes to Hard Rock Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 14, at noon. The sunglasses come off Monday. It's all about the U, baby, and the U still has November.

articles.title: Ole Miss vs Georgia: Rebels' Home Streak Ends in 42-7 Loss
articles.matchup: Final: Georgia (8-1) 42, Ole Miss (6-3) 7, Sat., Nov. 7, Vaught-Hemingway Stadium, Oxford. Next: at Oklahoma, Sat., Nov. 14, Memorial Stadium (Norman, OK)
articles.text:
Georgia 42, Ole Miss 7. Our Rebels asked us to wear red, and 68,814 of us did, packing Vaught-Hemingway Stadium to the rafters after the Coca-Cola FanFest opened at 3:30 and the Walk of Champions came through at 4:15. At 6:28 the Vaught was shaking. By halftime Georgia had walked off with the furniture, 28-0.

Mr. Faulkner wrote that the past is never dead. Tonight I would settle for it being briefly unconscious. Our 16-game home winning streak, the pride of this campus, ended on the same grass where it was built. Georgia drove 72 yards, then 96, then 61, then 50, and our first three possessions produced two punts and a 56-yard field goal try that drifted wide.

The one chapter I will reread came late in the half. Down 28-0, we marched to the Georgia 14 behind a 12-yard Joshua Dye run. Then Trinidad Chambliss was sacked for 16 yards, and on the next snap KJ Bolden intercepted him. In the third, Rasean Dinkins stripped Chambliss and returned the fumble to our 22, and Talyn Taylor caught his second touchdown of the night three plays later.

Honest accounting, because I always land on a hard number. Chambliss went 18 of 34 for 170 yards with that interception and no touchdown throws, so his streak of 21 straight games with one is done. He spent the night running from red jerseys and lost 12 yards on nine carries. Horatio Fields was the bright spot with eight catches for 96 yards. Shekai Mills-Knight carried 13 times for 52 yards and finished a 16-play, 75-yard march from 8 yards out with 10:43 left so we did not go home empty.

The defense spent 34:41 on the field and gave up 295 rushing yards. Joenel Aguero, Antonio Kite and Kam Franklin each made six tackles, and Will Echoles got a sack. We were 6 of 16 on third down and 3 of 3 on fourth.

No victory monologue tonight. Just seersucker folded in a drawer and a long walk past the Lyceum. We are 6-3 and 4-3 in the SEC, and next Saturday, Nov. 14, we visit Oklahoma at Memorial Stadium in Norman. Every good novel has a dark middle. Hotty Toddy anyway.

articles.title: Georgia vs Ole Miss: Stockton, Taylor Silence Oxford, Win 42-7
articles.matchup: Final: Georgia (8-1) 42, Ole Miss (6-3) 7, Sat., Nov. 7, Vaught-Hemingway Stadium, Oxford. Next: vs. Missouri, Sat., Nov. 14, Sanford Stadium, Athens
articles.text:
Georgia 42, Ole Miss 7, and track one on the set list was a 46-yard Nate Frazier run on our very first snap. Back home, downtown Athens spent Saturday afternoon watching homemade chariots race along East Clayton Street and College Avenue in the Red Bull Chariot Race. By nightfall in Oxford, the fastest machine in Mississippi wore red and black, and Gunner Stockton was driving it.

Album Review, side one. Seven plays, 72 yards, Craig Dandridge from 4 yards out. Then the cut I will spin all winter: we started at our own 4, and four plays later Stockton dropped a 58-yard rainbow to Talyn Taylor. Ninety-six yards in 2:11. A 3-yard shovel to Ethan Barbour made it 21-0, and Stockton tucked it and ran 15 yards himself for a 28-0 halftime lead.

Now the blitz tracks, because this defense was the headliner. Ole Miss went three-and-out on its first drive and came up empty on a 56-yard field goal try. When the Rebels finally reached our 14 late in the half, Khalil Barnes sacked Trinidad Chambliss for a 16-yard loss, and KJ Bolden intercepted him on the very next snap and brought it back 26 yards. In the third, Rasean Dinkins sacked Chambliss, popped the ball loose, scooped it and returned it 17 yards to the Ole Miss 22. Three plays later Stockton found Taylor for 6 and 35-0.

The liner notes: Stockton went 9 of 15 for 186 yards, four touchdown throws and a rushing score. Taylor caught four balls for 140 yards and three touchdowns, the last a 65-yarder that answered the only Rebel score. We ran for 295 yards on 48 carries, Frazier had 107 of them, and we held the ball for 34:41. Chris Cole led everybody with nine tackles and a sack and a half. Ole Miss finished with 252 yards and 66 on the ground.

Credit to Oxford. That was a sold-out crowd of 68,814 dressed in red, and that building had not lost in 16 straight. It lost tonight, and Kirby Smart finally has a win there on his record.

Album Review verdict: no skips, no filler, best closer of the year. We are 8-1, 6-1 in the SEC and 3-0 on the road. Missouri comes between the hedges at Sanford Stadium next Saturday, Nov. 14, and I already have the walk-out song cued.

articles.title: UNLV vs Wyoming: Rebels' Comeback Show Falls Short, 41-35
articles.matchup: Final: Wyoming Cowboys (6-3) 41, UNLV Rebels (5-4) 35, Sat., Nov. 7, Allegiant Stadium, Paradise. Next: at New Mexico, Sat., Nov. 14, 7:30 PM ET, University Stadium (NM), Albuquerque
articles.text:
Wyoming beat us 41-35. And that's the show, folks, just not the ending we rehearsed. Allegiant Stadium had real legends on the guest list: the UNLV Athletics Hall of Fame class of 2026, seven new members inducted Thursday at the Thomas & Mack Center, was set to be feted at this game. Erick Fedde, Charley Hoffman, Marissa Nichols and the rest earned their bows. Our football team nearly gave them an encore for the ages.

Opening Act review: rough. Wyoming ran for 351 yards, and Samuel Harris and Markell Holman both cleared 100. By the middle of the second quarter it was 24-7, and Ethan Stuhlsatz was living in our backfield on his way to three sacks.

Then the Rebels found the spotlight. Jackson Arnold hit Kayden McGee for a 33-yard touchdown. Denver Harris sacked Tyler Hughes, the ball came loose, and Harris fell on it at the Wyoming 3. Three plays later Arnold found Taz Reddicks from the 8. 24-21 with 1:55 left in the half. Wyoming answered with a touchdown, then a field goal at the gun after an interception, and it was 34-21.

Andre Porter intercepted Landon Sims in the third, and we kept swinging. Down 41-21, Alex Orji came in and scored from the 2 with 22 seconds left in the quarter. Early in the fourth our front stopped Holman on fourth down, and Jai'Den Thomas ran 11 yards for a touchdown at 8:32. 41-35, and I was on my feet.

The finale didn't land. Orji drove us deep into Wyoming territory, but Tyson Shamsid-Deen intercepted him in the end zone with 1:51 left, and Holman's 49-yard run on the next snap closed the curtain.

Thomas ran for 96 yards and two scores. Arnold threw two touchdowns. Peyton Zachary returned four kickoffs for 124 yards with a long of 58. Cam Santee and Mumu Bin-Wahad each made 11 tackles, and Matt Choules punted four times for a 50.0 average. Plenty of Rebels worth applauding.

We're 5-4 and 3-2 in the Mountain West, 3-2 at home. Next week the show goes on the road: New Mexico, 7:30 PM ET at University Stadium in Albuquerque. Curtain up, Rebels.

articles.title: Wyoming vs UNLV: Cowboys Ride Out Rebel Rally, 41-35
articles.matchup: Final: Wyoming Cowboys (6-3) 41, UNLV Rebels (5-4) 35, Sat., Nov. 7, Allegiant Stadium, Paradise. Next: at UTEP, Sat., Nov. 14, 10:00 PM ET, Sun Bowl, El Paso
articles.text:
Wyoming 41, UNLV 35. Yep. Good day for the Brown and Gold. At noon back in Laramie, the Cowgirls blanked Hawai'i at the Madrid Sports Complex and punched their ticket to the Mountain West tournament. Alyssa Glover scored her 10th goal of the season, Izzy Schroder got her first, and Haley Bartel made it stand with her ninth shutout. Then the football team went to the desert and finished the day. Barely.

Ground game. We ran 56 times for 351 yards. Samuel Harris had 128 and two scores, including a 42-yarder in the third that made it 41-21. Markell Holman had 110. Tyler Hughes ran for 71 and threw a 13-yard touchdown to Kyle Frendt on the opening drive.

First half, we had it rolling. Erik Sandvik hit a 43-yarder, Harris scored from the 1, and Landon Sims threw an 18-yard touchdown to Jake Wilson on a trick play for a 24-7 lead. Then we got loose with the ball. Hughes lost a fumble on a sack at our 3, and UNLV scored twice late in the half. Sims answered with a 13-yard touchdown run, Tyson Shamsid-Deen intercepted Jackson Arnold, and Sandvik hit a 35-yarder at the gun. 34-21.

Then it got tight. Sims threw an interception in the third. After Harris made it 41-21, UNLV scored with 22 seconds left in the third and again at 8:32 of the fourth. 41-35. Ethan Stuhlsatz made 10 tackles with three sacks, and earlier our front had stopped Jai'Den Thomas on fourth down at midfield.

Last threat. UNLV drove deep into our end, and Shamsid-Deen intercepted Alex Orji in the end zone with 1:51 left, his second of the night. Next snap, Holman broke four tackles, reversed field and went 49 yards, and we ran out the clock.

Cade Brook had a sack. Steven Perez made seven tackles. Bart Edmiston punted three times for a 55.0 average. My count says this report runs long. Worth it. Good team.

We're 6-3 and 5-1 in the Mountain West. UTEP is next, at the Sun Bowl in El Paso, with a 10 PM ET kickoff a week from tonight. Big sky. Thank the Lord.

Alyssa Glover scored her 10th goal of the season, Izzy Schroder got her first, and Haley Bartel made it stand with her ninth shutout. Then the football team went to the desert and finished the day. Barely.

Ground game. We ran 56 times for 351 yards. Samuel Harris had 128 and two scores, including a 42-yarder in the third that made it 41-21. Markell Holman had 110. Tyler Hughes ran for 71 and threw a 13-yard touchdown to Kyle Frendt on the opening drive.

First half, we had it rolling. Erik Sandvik hit a 43-yarder, Harris scored from the 1, and Landon Sims threw an 18-yard touchdown to Jake Wilson on a trick play for a 24-7 lead. Then we got loose with the ball. Hughes lost a fumble on a sack at our 3, and UNLV scored twice late in the half. Sims answered with a 13-yard touchdown run, Tyson Shamsid-Deen intercepted Jackson Arnold, and Sandvik hit a 35-yarder at the gun. 34-21.

Then it got tight. Sims threw an interception in the third. After Harris made it 41-21, UNLV scored with 22 seconds left in the third and again at 8:32 of the fourth. 41-35. Ethan Stuhlsatz made 10 tackles with three sacks, and earlier our front had stopped Jai'Den Thomas on fourth down at midfield.

Last threat. UNLV drove deep into our end, and Shamsid-Deen intercepted Alex Orji in the end zone with 1:51 left, his second of the night. Next snap, Holman broke four tackles, reversed field and went 49 yards, and we ran out the clock.
Cade Brook had a sack. Steven Perez made seven tackles. Bart Edmiston punted three times for a 55.0 average. My count says this report runs long. Worth it. Good team.
We're 6-3 and 5-1 in the Mountain West. UTEP is next, at the Sun Bowl in El Paso, with a 10 PM ET kickoff a week from tonight. Big sky. Thank the Lord.

Tyson Shamsid-Deen intercepted two throws, the second in the end zone with 1:51 left.
Cowgirls posted a shutout. Cowboys posted 41. Busy day at the ranch.

articles.title: Oregon State vs Texas State: Beavers Felled at Reser, 42-21
articles.matchup: Final: Texas State Bobcats (5-4) 42, Oregon State Beavers (5-4) 21, Sat., Nov. 7, Reser Stadium, Corvallis. Next: at Boise State, Sat., Nov. 14, 6:00 PM ET, Albertsons Stadium, Boise
articles.text:
Texas State beat us 42-21 at Reser. Measure twice, kick once, and tonight we never got the tape out. Tailgate Town at the CH2M HILL Alumni Center opened at 4:30 with barbecue from Pacific Northwest pitmasters, OSU Cheer and the OSU Marching Band, all to welcome the Bobcats for the first meeting ever between these programs. Beaver Nation wanted a strong first impression. Texas State made it instead.

This was a clear-cut, and in a forestry family I don't use that word lightly. Texas State ran 62 times for 386 yards. Torrance Burgess Jr. had 196 of them, Davian Jackson scored three times from the 3 or closer, and the Bobcats held the ball for 35:52. Our defense saw plenty of grass and very little of the football.

There were good branches. Drake Vickers made 12 tackles. Aiden Sullivan made 10 and forced a Davian Jackson fumble, and Gyriece Goodman recovered it, after he'd already intercepted Brad Jackson in the first quarter. TJ Crandall blocked a 28-yard field goal. Takari Hickle had a sack.

The offense never found its canopy. Braden Atkinson went 20 of 36 for 192 yards, so his run of 300-yard games ended at eight, and Jayden Bradley intercepted him in the first quarter, his first interception since Sept. 26. Jesse Legree still caught eight balls for 99, and AJ Newberry scored from the 9 to make it 14-7. We came up empty on fourth down at the Texas State 15 before halftime and missed a 50-yard field goal in the third.

Then the hinge of the night. Burgess ran 63 yards on the last snap of the third quarter, Brad Jackson ran 23 for a touchdown on the first snap of the fourth, Maalik Murphy came in and got intercepted on the next play, and Zechariah Sample's 28-yard catch made it 42-7. Cornell Hatcher Jr. and Kourdey Glass scored late, the second set up by Goodman's fumble recovery.

Caleb Ojeda made all three kicks after touchdowns, and AJ Winsor pinned three punts inside the 20. We're 5-4 and 3-2 in the Pac-12, 3-2 at home. We head to Boise State next, a 6 PM ET kickoff at Albertsons Stadium. A Douglas fir takes a storm and keeps standing. So do we.

articles.title: Texas State vs Oregon State: Bobcats Run Wild in Corvallis, 42-21
articles.matchup: Final: Texas State Bobcats (5-4) 42, Oregon State Beavers (5-4) 21, Sat., Nov. 7, Reser Stadium, Corvallis. Next: vs. Fresno State, Sat., Nov. 14, 4:00 PM ET, UFCU Stadium, San Marcos
articles.text:
Texas State 42, Oregon State 21. Floating on air, y'all! San Marcos kicked off Saturday downtown with the Veterans Day Parade at 10 a.m., kids dressing up their bikes for the Bicycle Brigade on the Hays County Historic Courthouse lawn, and the Texas Capital Air Show opened at San Marcos Regional Airport. Planes above town all day, and by night the Bobcats were flying in Corvallis in the first game these two programs ever played.

My motto is go with the flow, then run it up the middle, and our offense took that literally. We ran 62 times for 386 yards. Torrance Burgess Jr. carried 28 times for 196 yards and a score. Davian Jackson ran for 107 and three touchdowns, from the 2, the 1 and the 3. Brad Jackson ran for 87 more, including a 23-yard touchdown.

The opener set the tone, 15 plays and 75 yards in 6:39, with Davian Jackson punching it in. Then the defense jumped in. We blocked a punt, gave the ball right back on an interception, and then Jayden Bradley intercepted Braden Atkinson, setting up Burgess's 1-yard score a few plays later for a 14-0 lead.

Davian's second score made it 21-7 at halftime, and his third made it 28-7 late in the third quarter. Then Burgess broke a 63-yard run on the last snap of the third, and Brad Jackson ran the final 23 on the first snap of the fourth. Craig Royal Jr. intercepted Oregon State on the very next play, and Brad found Zechariah Sample for a 28-yard touchdown. 42-7. The river was running high.

Brad Jackson was close to perfect throwing it, 16 of 20 for 214 yards, and Sample caught three balls for 95. Chris Dawn Jr. caught seven. We went 10 of 15 on third down and held the ball for 35:52. TJ Burkhalter and Jo'Laison Landry each had a sack, and Chase Davis made six tackles.

Oregon State scored twice late, and Jesse Legree caught eight balls for 99, so the Beavers get their credit. But the current ran our way all night. We're 5-4 and 3-2 in the Pac-12. Fresno State comes to UFCU Stadium next week for a 4 PM ET kickoff. Grab a tube, San Marcos. We're coming home.

articles.title: UTEP vs Hawai'i: Miners Come Up Three Short, 17-14
articles.matchup: Final: Hawai'i Rainbow Warriors (3-6) 17, UTEP Miners (1-8) 14, Sat., Nov. 7, Sun Bowl, El Paso. Next: vs. Wyoming, Sat., Nov. 14, 10:00 PM ET, Sun Bowl, El Paso
articles.text:
Hawai'i beat us 17-14. Mild salsa, mi gente, and I can't stand mild. Leis were the giveaway at the Sun Bowl, El Paso Children's Hospital sponsored the night, and it was the first time we'd hosted Hawai'i since 2004. Women's basketball took on Incarnate Word at 1 p.m., and a hoops ticket got you into the football game free. A whole Saturday of Miners, and we came up three points short.

The effort grade? That's ore worth keeping. Jayden Wilson made 11 tackles and forced a DeVon Rice fumble that Garrett Hawkins recovered. Xavier Smith made nine tackles and intercepted Micah Alejado in the end zone in the final seconds of the half. Kode Lowe had a sack among his seven tackles, and Justin Content made nine stops.

Our first touchdown came fast, three plays and 65 yards in 36 seconds in the second quarter. Carver Cheeks ran for 22, Lamar Sperling ran for 23, and Sperling finished it from the 5. 10-7, and the orange in the stands woke up.

In the fourth, after Hawai'i went 98 yards, Raymond Moore III answered with a seven-play, 79-yard drive and a 15-yard touchdown throw to Judah Ezinwa. 17-14 with 6:57 left. The crowd of 8,581 found its voice.

Then Hawai'i held the ball for the last 6:57, and we never touched it again. That one burns worse than a ghost pepper. Earlier, a 26-yard Kam Thomas run ended in a fumble, and a fourth-down try at the Hawai'i 32 came up short just before halftime. Those are the plays I'll be chewing on all week.

Sperling ran for 63 yards on 11 carries. Moore ran for 41 and threw for 109 and the score. Cheeks caught two for 46. We ran for 179 yards at 5.8 a carry, which tells you the front came to work. Brady Braun punted five times for a 41.6 average, two inside the 20.

We're 1-8 and 0-5 in the Mountain West. Senior Night is next, against Wyoming at the Sun Bowl, 10 PM ET on Nov. 14. Bring the green chile, El Paso. Let's make it Hatch-hot.

articles.title: Hawai'i vs UTEP: Rainbow Warriors Ride It Out, 17-14
articles.matchup: Final: Hawai'i Rainbow Warriors (3-6) 17, UTEP Miners (1-8) 14, Sat., Nov. 7, Sun Bowl, El Paso. Next: vs. North Dakota State, Sat., Nov. 14, 11:00 PM ET, Clarence T.C. Ching Athletics Complex, Honolulu
articles.text:
Hawai'i 17, UTEP 14. Shoots! Time-zone math first, because somebody has to do it: kickoff at the Sun Bowl was 7:30 in El Paso, 4:30 in the afternoon back home in Honolulu. And Saturday night at Bankoh Arena at Stan Sheriff Center, the Rainbow Wahine swept Nevada in front of 6,306 and clinched at least a share of the Mountain West regular-season title. Miliana Sylvester had 13 kills and six blocks. Big day for the islands.

Our guys did their part on the mainland. Micah Alejado threw for 303 yards, and Titan Lacaden was everywhere: 11 catches, 109 yards and a 20-yard touchdown in the first quarter, both career highs. Audric Harris added four catches for 101.

The drive I'll be surfing in my sleep came early in the fourth. We were pinned at our own 2 and went 98 yards in 12 plays. Sitani Mikaele ripped off 23, Lacaden caught one for 18 and another for 23 to the 6, and Mikaele scored from the 6 at 10:08. 17-7.

It didn't come easy, though. Sean Olvera-Harle missed from 42 before hitting a 20-yarder to finish an 18-play, 91-yard march for a 10-0 lead. A throw in the final seconds of the half got intercepted in the end zone, and DeVon Rice lost a fumble in the third. UTEP answered our big drive with a 79-yard march of its own, and it was 17-14 with 6:57 to go.

Then came the closer. Thirteen plays, 40 yards, all 6:57 of clock. Alejado kept the chains moving with short throws to Lacaden and Kainoa Carvalho, Mikaele and Cam Barfield ground out the rest, UTEP spent its timeouts, and Alejado took three knees. Island time, finally working for us.

The defense earned its plate lunch. Jamih Otis made 10 tackles with 1.5 for loss. Elijah Palmer made nine and forced two fumbles, and Matagi Thompson recovered the first one, which set up Lacaden's score. UTEP went 2 of 10 on third down.

We're 3-6 and 2-4 in the Mountain West. North Dakota State comes to the Clarence T.C. Ching Athletics Complex next, with an 11 PM ET kickoff on Nov. 14. Home break, Warriors. Paddle out early.

articles.title: Utah State vs Fresno State: Aggies Hold the Fort in Logan, 17-10
articles.matchup: Final: Utah State Aggies (4-5) 17, Fresno State Bulldogs (5-4) 10, Sat., Nov. 7, Maverik Stadium, Logan. Next: at San Diego State, Sat., Nov. 14, 9:30 PM ET, Snapdragon Stadium, San Diego
articles.text:
Utah State 17, Fresno State 10. Well, neighbors, that one was worth staying up for. It was Salute to Service night at Maverik Stadium, Military Appreciation, with Operation Hat Trick gear raising support for the Rocky Mountain Veterans Center. And Cache Valley's first responders had free seats, the same folks who fought the Canyon Road Fire south of campus this summer.

Our defense gave them a proper thank-you. Fresno State ran 27 times for 16 yards. That's it. Ronnie Mageo had 1.5 sacks and three tackles for loss. Asher Cunningham had eight tackles, two for loss and three quarterback hurries. Brevin Hamblin made nine stops. And Bronson Olevao Jr., who went down to thank the Logan police and firefighters in person back in September, dropped Josiah Freeman for a 10-yard loss late in the fourth.

The offense waited out a scoreless first quarter the way a cow waits on the morning milking, then went 80 yards in three plays across the break. McCae Hillstead hit Anthony Garcia for 37 and ran for 12, Fresno State kept drawing flags, and Sesi Vailahi scored from the 2. Hillstead scored from the 3 at 9:47 of the second, and it was 14-0 at halftime.

The second half was patience. Fresno State drove 66 yards for a field goal, 14-3. Early in the fourth they reached our 18, and our front stuffed Julius Gillick on fourth down. Kian Afrookhteh hit a 43-yard field goal with 4:21 left to make it 17-3. Fresno scored late, Kaina Watson fell on the onside kick, and Hillstead took a knee.

Hillstead went 9 of 14 for 117 yards without an interception and ran 12 times for 56 and a score. Javen Jacobs ran for 36 and returned three punts for 30. Will Evans punted five times and pinned three of them inside the 20. Zero turnovers for the good guys.

We're 4-5 and 3-2 in the Pac-12, 4-1 at home. San Diego State and Snapdragon Stadium are next, 9:30 PM ET on Nov. 14. I'll have my double scoop of Aggie Ice Cream either way, but this week I'm asking for extra fudge. Udderly earned.

articles.title: Fresno State vs Utah State: Bulldogs Run Dry in Logan, 17-10
articles.matchup: Final: Utah State Aggies (4-5) 17, Fresno State Bulldogs (5-4) 10, Sat., Nov. 7, Maverik Stadium, Logan. Next: at Texas State, Sat., Nov. 14, 4:00 PM ET, UFCU Stadium, San Marcos
articles.text:
Utah State beat us 17-10 in Logan. Not that valley, and not that ending. Saturday morning on our campus, Arte Américas brought Bilingual Storytime to Fresno State, stories in English and Spanish with hands-on art for the kids, sponsored by Valley Children's Health, the same name that's on our stadium. By night our Bulldogs were up in Cache Valley writing a story nobody wants read twice.

Here's the chapter that stings: 16 rushing yards on 27 carries. Sixteen. Bryson Donelson had 15 of them on six tries, and Jayden Mandal got sacked and chased until his own run column read minus 10. You can't farm without water, and you can't win in Logan without a ground game.

The first quarter ended scoreless, and Nick Verdugo kept flipping the field, seven punts on the night for a 40.1 average, three inside the 20. Then a 37-yard catch by Anthony Garcia and two Bulldog penalties handed Utah State a three-play, 80-yard drive, and Sesi Vailahi scored from the 2 one snap into the second quarter. McCae Hillstead ran in from the 3 at 9:47, and it was 14-0.

We had chances. Mandal led a 14-play, 66-yard drive in the third that ended with Manaki Watanabe's 32-yard field goal, 14-3. articles.title: Texas Tech vs West Virginia: Castellanos Saves Blackout, 53-48
articles.matchup: Final: Texas Tech Red Raiders (8-1) 53, West Virginia Mountaineers (5-4) 48, Sat., Nov. 7, Galaxy Stadium, Lubbock. Next: at Oklahoma State, Sat., Nov. 14, 9:30 PM ET, Boone Pickens Stadium, Stillwater
articles.text:
Texas Tech 53, West Virginia 48. Close. It was the annual blackout game at Galaxy Stadium, an 8:30 kickoff, our latest home kick since 2003. Forty-five thousand LED wristbands at the gates. Two drone shows on the program, one before kickoff and one after the third quarter. Truth is, that second show lit up the sky above a ballgame I didn't like one bit.

The first half was ours. Thomas Castellanos threw two touchdowns to Terrance Carter Jr., one to Jett Carpenter from the 1 and a 38-yarder to Kenny Johnson. J'Koby Williams went 75 yards on one carry. Quinten Joyner scored from the 1, and Matt Ludwig ran in the two-point try. Forty-one points by halftime. 41-27. Loud.

Then the wind turned. We punted on our first four drives of the second half. West Virginia ran off 21 straight points, and a 74-yard punt return set one of them up. 48-41 after three. I took my hat off and held it.

Stone Harrington hit a 46-yard field goal at the end of a 15-play drive. Then the defense stuffed Cam Cook on third-and-1, and West Virginia punted. Castellanos went to work. Fourth-and-3, he floated one to Micah Hudson for 26. He ran 16 more to the 7, and two plays later he found Johnson from the 5 with 2:44 left. 51-48. Guns up. Quiet.

Trey White closed it. He sacked Michael Hawkins Jr. for 11 yards on fourth down, our offense came up empty at the 5, and White was credited with the safety on the very next snap. Two sacks and 2.5 tackles for loss for White. Austin Romaine made 15 tackles. Mean.

Castellanos finished 18 of 27 for 362 yards, five touchdowns and no interceptions, and ran for 102 more. Williams ran for 160 and caught a 43-yarder. Johnson caught five for 84 and two scores, Carter four for 81 and two. We piled up 638 yards with zero turnovers. The defense gave up 279 on the ground, and that gets fixed this week. Plain as a fence post.

We're 8-1 and 5-1 in the Big 12, 6-0 at home. Next we ride up to Stillwater for Oklahoma State at Boone Pickens Stadium, 9:30 PM ET a week from tonight. Wind's up.

articles.title: West Virginia vs Texas Tech: Hawkins Rally Falls Short, 53-48
articles.matchup: Final: Texas Tech Red Raiders (8-1) 53, West Virginia Mountaineers (5-4) 48, Sat., Nov. 7, Galaxy Stadium, Lubbock. Next: vs. Kansas, Sat., Nov. 14, 5:30 PM ET, Milan Puskar Stadium, Morgantown
articles.text:
Texas Tech beat us 53-48. I'm counting to ten out loud, slow, like I'm reloading. Back home in Morgantown, WVUp All Night had the Mountainlair open from 10 p.m. to 2 a.m. with free bowling and inflatable axe throwing, and our kickoff in Lubbock came at 9:30 Eastern. Any student who bowled straight through this one got the whole ride, because the Mountaineers played past midnight and lost a heartbreaker by five.

The first half was a track meet. Thomas Castellanos threw four touchdowns before the break, J'Koby Williams broke a 75-yard run, and we went to halftime down 41-27. Our offense kept swinging back, though. Amari Latimer scored from the 3, Michael Hawkins Jr. from the 3, and TaRon Francis took a 73-yard catch the distance to put us up 24-21.

Then came the third quarter, and I'd like it framed. KJ Henson sacked Castellanos for 15 yards on Tech's first snap after our opening score of the half, and Tech never found the end zone in the quarter. Hawkins ran one in from the 2. Francis hauled in a 75-yarder to the Tech 4, and Cam Cook punched it in from the 2. Matt Sieg returned a punt 74 yards to the 6, and Hawkins scored from the 3. Twenty-one straight points. 48-41 after three.

The fourth went cold. Stone Harrington hit a 46-yard field goal to make it 48-44. On our next series, Cook got stopped for no gain on third-and-1 at our own 34, we punted, and Tech went 69 yards in nine plays. Castellanos found Micah Hudson for 26 on fourth-and-3 and Kenny Johnson for the 5-yard go-ahead score with 2:44 left. Trey White sacked Hawkins on fourth down, our defense held Tech at the 5, and then Hawkins went down in our own end zone for a safety.

Hawkins threw for 303 yards on just 11 completions and ran for 88 and three scores. Cook ran for 149 on 23 carries. Francis caught three balls for 169. We rolled up 582 yards with zero turnovers, Jack Cassidy made both field goals and all six kicks after touchdowns, and Kameron Reddic made 11 tackles. My pepperoni-roll tally stayed at zero, because Tech never put the ball on the ground either. Hungry night.

We're 5-4 and 2-4 in the Big 12. Kansas visits Milan Puskar Stadium next, 5:30 PM ET on Nov. 14. Bring your voice, Morgantown, and let's sing the old song at the end of that one.
